52.11.s: kūṭasthānāni sarvāṇi dikṣv etāny upadhārayet | prabhānvitāni śvetāni snigdhāni vimalāni ca ||
52.11.d: कूटस्थानानि सर्वाणि दिक्ष्व् एतान्य् उपधारयेत् । प्रभान्वितानि श्वेतानि स्निग्धानि विमलानि च ॥
52.11.m: One should contemplate all these as motionless pivots in the directions; / endowed with radiance, white, unctuous, and stainless,

52.11.s: arciṣmanti prasannāni tāni kuryuḥ prajāhitam | niḥprabhāṇi vivarṇāni nirarcīmṣy amalāni ca ||
52.11.d: अर्चिष्मन्ति प्रसन्नानि तानि कुर्युः प्रजाहितम् । निःप्रभाणि विवर्णानि निरर्चीम्ष्य् अमलानि च ॥
52.11.m: flaming and serene, they bring welfare to subjects; / [when] lusterless, discolored, flameless, and murky,

52.11.s: hrasvāny asnehayuktāni na bhāvāya bhavanti hi | yat kiṃcit sthāvaraṃ loke tat prasanneṣu vardhate ||
52.11.d: ह्रस्वान्य् अस्नेहयुक्तानि न भावाय भवन्ति हि । यत् किंचित् स्थावरं लोके तत् प्रसन्नेषु वर्धते ॥
52.11.m: short, and devoid of gloss, they indeed do not lead to prosperity. / Whatever is fixed in the world increases when they are serene;

52.11.s: kūṭastheṣv aprasanneṣu sthāvaraṃ parihīyate | ādityaś caiva śukraś ca lohitāṅgas tathaiva ca ||
52.11.d: कूटस्थेष्व् अप्रसन्नेषु स्थावरं परिहीयते । आदित्यश् चैव शुक्रश् च लोहिताङ्गस् तथैव च ॥
52.11.m: when the motionless pivots are unpropitious, what is fixed wastes away. / The Sun, Venus, and Mars;

52.11.s: rāhuḥ somaḥ śanaiścaro bṛhaspatibudhau tathā | aindra āgneyo yāmyaś ca nairṛto vāruṇas tathā ||
52.11.d: राहुः सोमः शनैश्चरो बृहस्पतिबुधौ तथा । ऐन्द्र आग्नेयो याम्यश् च नैरृतो वारुणस् तथा ॥
52.11.m: Rāhu, the Moon, Saturn, Jupiter, and Mercury; / [the planets of] Indra, Agni, Yama, Nirṛti, Varuṇa,

52.12.s: vāyavyaś caiva saumyaś ca brāhmaś caivāṣṭamo grahaḥ | navamaś caiva vijñeyo dhūmaketur mahāgrahaḥ ||
52.12.d: वायव्यश् चैव सौम्यश् च ब्राह्मश् चैवाष्टमो ग्रहः । नवमश् चैव विज्ञेयो धूमकेतुर् महाग्रहः ॥
52.12.m: Vāyu, Soma, and the eighth planet of Brahmā; / and the ninth is to be known as the great planet Dhūmaketu.

52.12.s: yugagrahā na cānye te tatrāṣṭau diggrahāḥ smṛtāḥ | sanakṣatreṣu mārgeṣu dṛśyante tu yugagrahāḥ ||
52.12.d: युगग्रहा न चान्ये ते तत्राष्टौ दिग्ग्रहाः स्मृताः । सनक्षत्रेषु मार्गेषु दृश्यन्ते तु युगग्रहाः ॥
52.12.m: The age-planets are not others; the eight directional planets are recorded among them. / The age-planets are seen in the paths containing lunar mansions,

52.12.s: vibhrāntamaṇḍalāḥ śeṣā dṛśyante khacarā grahaḥ | mṛtyor niśvāsajāś cānye jñeyāḥ ṣoḍaśa ketavaḥ ||
52.12.d: विभ्रान्तमण्डलाः शेषा दृश्यन्ते खचरा ग्रहः । मृत्योर् निश्वासजाश् चान्ये ज्ञेयाः षोडश केतवः ॥
52.12.m: while the remaining sky-roaming planets are seen with revolving discs. / Others born from the sigh of Death are to be known as sixteen comets.

52.12.s: kūṣmāṇḍavad visaṃchannas triṇavā dakṣiṇe pathi | ekādaśaiva vijñeyā dvādaśādityasaṃbhavāḥ ||
52.12.d: कूष्माण्डवद् विसंछन्नस् त्रिणवा दक्षिणे पथि । एकादशैव विज्ञेया द्वादशादित्यसंभवाः ॥
52.12.m: Covered like pumpkins, twenty-seven [wander] in the southern path; / eleven are to be known as sprung from the twelve suns.

52.12.s: sūryavarcanirīkṣās te tejodhātumayā grahāḥ | dakṣayajñe tu rudrasya krodhād anye tu niḥsṛtāḥ ||
52.12.d: सूर्यवर्चनिरीक्षास् ते तेजोधातुमया ग्रहाः । दक्षयज्ञे तु रुद्रस्य क्रोधाद् अन्ये तु निःसृताः ॥
52.12.m: Gazing with solar luster, they are planets composed of the element of fire. / Others emerged from Rudra's wrath at the sacrifice of Dakṣa:

52.13.s: bhīmarūpā daśaikaś ca jvalāṅkuśadharā grahāḥ | sapta paitāmahās tv anye tiryaggā jarjaragrahāḥ ||
52.13.d: भीमरूपा दशैकश् च ज्वलाङ्कुशधरा ग्रहाः । सप्त पैतामहास् त्व् अन्ये तिर्यग्गा जर्जरग्रहाः ॥
52.13.m: eleven planets of terrible form, holding flaming goads. / Seven other decrepit planets belong to the Grandfather, moving crosswise,

52.13.s: śikhāḥ sṛjanto vitatās tantuśuklapaṭopamāḥ | śvetaketava ity anye vyākhyātā daśa pañca ca ||
52.13.d: शिखाः सृजन्तो विततास् तन्तुशुक्लपटोपमाः । श्वेतकेतव इत्य् अन्ये व्याख्याता दश पञ्च च ॥
52.13.m: sending forth extended crests resembling white woven cloth. / Fifteen others are explained as Śvetaketus;

52.13.s: uddālakarṣiputrās te nīcair vibhrāntamaṇḍalāḥ | te syuḥ śvetaśikhāḥ sarve saumyāḥ kāntās tanuprabhāḥ ||
52.13.d: उद्दालकर्षिपुत्रास् ते नीचैर् विभ्रान्तमण्डलाः । ते स्युः श्वेतशिखाः सर्वे सौम्याः कान्तास् तनुप्रभाः ॥
52.13.m: they are sons of the sage Uddālaka, with orbits wandering low; / they all have white crests, are benign, beautiful, and of slender light.

52.13.s: aṣṭādaśendunā sārdhaṃ mathyamāne purāmṛte | ketavaḥ kundapuṣpābhāḥ kṣīrodanabhasi smṛtāḥ ||
52.13.d: अष्टादशेन्दुना सार्धं मथ्यमाने पुरामृते । केतवः कुन्दपुष्पाभाः क्षीरोदनभसि स्मृताः ॥
52.13.m: Eighteen along with the Moon, when ambrosia was churned of old, / are recorded in the sky of the Milk Ocean as comets shining like jasmine blossoms.

52.13.s: viraśmayaś ca viśikhā mahākāyā nirarciṣaḥ | raupyakumbhanibhāḥ saumyā grahāḥ syuḥ śītatejasaḥ ||
52.13.d: विरश्मयश् च विशिखा महाकाया निरर्चिषः । रौप्यकुम्भनिभाः सौम्या ग्रहाः स्युः शीततेजसः ॥
52.13.m: Rayless, crestless, large-bodied, devoid of flames, / resembling silver pitchers, they are benign planets of cool radiance.

52.14.s: brahmakopamayas tv eko viśvātmā sarvato grahaḥ | caturyugānte lokānām udayas tasya vidyate ||
52.14.d: ब्रह्मकोपमयस् त्व् एको विश्वात्मा सर्वतो ग्रहः । चतुर्युगान्ते लोकानाम् उदयस् तस्य विद्यते ॥
52.14.m: One planet, however, consists of Brahmā's anger, the self of the universe in every respect; / its rising takes place for the worlds at the end of the four ages.

52.14.s: nakṣatrapatham utsṛjya nabhoaṃśāḥ pārśvacāriṇaḥ | pūrvato 'bhyuditā vā syur nīcair uttaratas tathā ||
52.14.d: नक्षत्रपथम् उत्सृज्य नभोअंशाः पार्श्वचारिणः । पूर्वतो ऽभ्युदिता वा स्युर् नीचैर् उत्तरतस् तथा ॥
52.14.m: Leaving the path of the lunar mansions, occupying portions of the sky, moving on the flank, / they may rise in the east, or low down in the north,

52.14.s: bhūmyām abhyuditā vā syur hrasvasnehapariplutāḥ | sarva eva tu vijñeyā grahā mandaphalodayāḥ ||
52.14.d: भूम्याम् अभ्युदिता वा स्युर् ह्रस्वस्नेहपरिप्लुताः । सर्व एव तु विज्ञेया ग्रहा मन्दफलोदयाः ॥
52.14.m: or they may rise from the earth, bathed in meager oiliness; / all planets indeed are to be known as having outcomes yielding little good fruit.

52.14.s: sarveṣāṃ paitṛkaṃ karma prajābhāgyodbhavaṃ mahat | sarve te sarvato hanyur aśubhaṃ yad vadanti ca ||
52.14.d: सर्वेषां पैतृकं कर्म प्रजाभाग्योद्भवं महत् । सर्वे ते सर्वतो हन्युर् अशुभं यद् वदन्ति च ॥
52.14.m: The great ancestral rites of all people, originating from the fortune of subjects— / all those [planets] destroy from every side whatever they call inauspicious.

52.14.s: tatkarmajanmamāhātmyaṃ śīlābhijanam eva ca | tadrūpāṃs tadguṇāṃś cāpi tanmayāṃs tatparigrahān ||
52.14.d: तत्कर्मजन्ममाहात्म्यं शीलाभिजनम् एव च । तद्रूपांस् तद्गुणांश् चापि तन्मयांस् तत्परिग्रहान् ॥
52.14.m: The majesty of their ritual and birth, their character and noble descent, / their forms, their qualities, those made of them, and their possessions:

52.15.s: sarva eva rogapradā mṛtyuśastrāgnitaskaraiḥ | paśusasyopaghātaiś ca hanyur anyaiś ca kāraṇaiḥ ||
52.15.d: सर्व एव रोगप्रदा मृत्युशस्त्राग्नितस्करैः । पशुसस्योपघातैश् च हन्युर् अन्यैश् च कारणैः ॥
52.15.m: all [these planets] bestow disease, and they destroy through death, weapons, fire, thieves, / blights of cattle and crops, and through other causes.

52.15.s: dhūpanāt sparśanāt sthānād udayāstamasaṃbhavāt | hanyuḥ pañcavidhaṃ sarve ketavo nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
52.15.d: धूपनात् स्पर्शनात् स्थानाद् उदयास्तमसंभवात् । हन्युः पञ्चविधं सर्वे केतवो नात्र संशयः ॥
52.15.m: By smoking, by touching, by [their] station, and through [their] appearance at rising or setting, / all comets bring destruction in five ways; there is no doubt about this.

52.15.s: mṛdudhruvograkṣipreṣu sādhāraṇacareṣu ca | dāruṇeṣu ca ṛkṣeṣu sādhāraṇacareṣu ca | dāruṇeṣu ca ṛkṣeṣu vidyāt tatsadṛśaṃ phalam ||
52.15.d: मृदुध्रुवोग्रक्षिप्रेषु साधारणचरेषु च । दारुणेषु च ऋक्षेषु साधारणचरेषु च । दारुणेषु च ऋक्षेषु विद्यात् तत्सदृशं फलम् ॥
52.15.m: In soft, fixed, fierce, and swift [lunar mansions], / and in common and mobile ones, and in harsh lunar mansions, one should know the result corresponds to that.

52.15.s: yathādiṣṭaṃ yathāvarṇaṃ yathāvargaparigraham | sarva evoditā hanyuḥ sarva eva mahāgrahāḥ ||
52.15.d: यथादिष्टं यथावर्णं यथावर्गपरिग्रहम् । सर्व एवोदिता हन्युः सर्व एव महाग्रहाः ॥
52.15.m: According to what has been taught, according to their color, and according to the class they encompass, / all the great planets, when risen, bring destruction.

52.15.s: mṛtyoḥ kālasya sūryasya brahmaṇas tryambakasya ca | bhaumasya rāhor agneś ca prajātā ye sudāruṇāḥ ||
52.15.d: मृत्योः कालस्य सूर्यस्य ब्रह्मणस् त्र्यम्बकस्य च । भौमस्य राहोर् अग्नेश् च प्रजाता ये सुदारुणाः ॥
52.15.m: Those extremely dreadful [comets] that are born of Mṛtyu, Kāla, the Sun, / Brahmā, Tryambaka, Mars, Rāhu, and Agni;

52.16.s: prajāpateś ca dharmasya somasya varuṇasya ca | pītādyāś ca diśāṃ putrā vijñeyā mṛdudāruṇāḥ ||
52.16.d: प्रजापतेश् च धर्मस्य सोमस्य वरुणस्य च । पीताद्याश् च दिशां पुत्रा विज्ञेया मृदुदारुणाः ॥
52.16.m: and the sons of Prajāpati, Dharma, Soma, and Varuṇa, / and the yellow and other sons of the cardinal directions, are to be known as mildly harsh.

52.16.s: kaśyapasya ca marīcer uddālakaṛṣes tathā | putrā mandaphalā jñeyās teṣām amṛtasaṃbhavāḥ ||
52.16.d: कश्यपस्य च मरीचेर् उद्दालकऋषेस् तथा । पुत्रा मन्दफला ज्ञेयास् तेषाम् अमृतसंभवाः ॥
52.16.m: And the sons of Kaśyapa, Marīci, and the sage Uddālaka, / who are born of nectar, are to be known as yielding slight results.

52.16.s: śukrādīnāṃ ca ye putrā grahāṇāṃ parikīrtitāḥ | teṣāṃ vīryāṇi jāniyāt pitṛbhyaḥ sādhikāni tu ||
52.16.d: शुक्रादीनां च ये पुत्रा ग्रहाणां परिकीर्तिताः । तेषां वीर्याणि जानियात् पितृभ्यः साधिकानि तु ॥
52.16.m: And the sons of the planets beginning with Śukra that have been proclaimed— / one should know their powers to be greater than those of their fathers.

52.16.s: nāradātreyagargāṇāṃ guror uśanasas tathā | grahāṇāṃ saṃgraho hy evam eṣa kārtsnyena kīrtitaḥ ||
52.16.d: नारदात्रेयगर्गाणां गुरोर् उशनसस् तथा । ग्रहाणां संग्रहो ह्य् एवम् एष कार्त्स्न्येन कीर्तितः ॥
52.16.m: Thus this compendium of the planets according to Nārada, the Ātreyas, Garga, / Guru, and Uśanas has been proclaimed in full.

52.16.s: anekaśatasāhasra anekaśatalakṣaṇaḥ | devalabdhavarākāśe prāha sarvān pṛthakpṛthak ||
52.16.d: अनेकशतसाहस्र अनेकशतलक्षणः । देवलब्धवराकाशे प्राह सर्वान् पृथक्पृथक् ॥
52.16.m: Possessing many hundreds of thousands [of aspects], having many hundreds of characteristics, / he declared them all individually in the space granted by the gods' boon.

52.16.s: etadutthe tu sarvasmin bhaye 'tha samupasthite | mahāśāntiṃ prakurvīta rājā rāṣṭrasya rakṣaṇe ||
52.16.d: एतदुत्थे तु सर्वस्मिन् भये ऽथ समुपस्थिते । महाशान्तिं प्रकुर्वीत राजा राष्ट्रस्य रक्षणे ॥
52.16.m: When any danger arising from these has presented itself, / the king should perform a great propitiatory rite for the protection of his realm.

52.16.s: tat prayāti śamaṃ sarvaṃ prajānāṃ tu sukhaṃ bhavet | rājāno muditās tatra pālayanti vasuṃdharām ||
52.16.d: तत् प्रयाति शमं सर्वं प्रजानां तु सुखं भवेत् । राजानो मुदितास् तत्र पालयन्ति वसुंधराम् ॥
52.16.m: All that [danger] goes to pacification, and there will be well-being for the subjects; / the kings, gladdened thereby, protect the earth.

53.1.s: om upetya yaś candramasaṃ raviṃ vā gṛhṇāti sūnor asurasya putraḥ | nibodhataitasya śubhāśubhāni grahasya mṛtyoḥ praticeṣṭitāni ||
53.1.d: ओम् उपेत्य यश् चन्द्रमसं रविं वा गृह्णाति सूनोर् असुरस्य पुत्रः । निबोधतैतस्य शुभाशुभानि ग्रहस्य मृत्योः प्रतिचेष्टितानि ॥
53.1.m: Om. He who approaches and seizes the moon or the sun, the son of the Asura's son— / learn the auspicious and inauspicious actions of this planet of death!

53.1.s: yadā tu rāhuḥ śaśino raver vā grahe grahītukāmo bhavati prasahya | tadā karoty adbhutadarśanāni yair jñāyate rāhur upaiṣyatīti ||
53.1.d: यदा तु राहुः शशिनो रवेर् वा ग्रहे ग्रहीतुकामो भवति प्रसह्य । तदा करोत्य् अद्भुतदर्शनानि यैर् ज्ञायते राहुर् उपैष्यतीति ॥
53.1.m: When Rāhu desires forcibly to seize the moon or the sun [in eclipse], / then he produces portentous sights by which it is known that Rāhu will approach.

53.1.s: udvepate tadā candro yadā rāhuḥ pradṛśyate || pāṇḍur vā jāyate klībaḥ śaśo vāsya vivardhate ||
53.1.d: उद्वेपते तदा चन्द्रो यदा राहुः प्रदृश्यते ॥ पाण्डुर् वा जायते क्लीबः शशो वास्य विवर्धते ॥
53.1.m: Then the moon trembles when Rāhu is seen, / or it becomes pale and feeble, or its hare-mark grows large.

53.1.s: rekhāntarāpurārāṇi kalmaṣāṇi divākare | vadanti ca bhaṛśaṃ śvāno vānti vātāś ca bhīṣaṇāḥ ||
53.1.d: रेखान्तरापुराराणि कल्मषाणि दिवाकरे । वदन्ति च भऋशं श्वानो वान्ति वाताश् च भीषणाः ॥
53.1.m: [There appear] dark spots shaped like lines, spaces, towns, and spokes upon the sun, / and dogs bark vehemently, and fearful winds blow.

53.1.s: saṃdhyayor ubhayoś colkā gavāṃ prakṣīyate payaḥ | kṣīriṇām aiva vṛkṣāṇāṃ tad ahar naśyate payaḥ ||
53.1.d: संध्ययोर् उभयोश् चोल्का गवां प्रक्षीयते पयः । क्षीरिणाम् ऐव वृक्षाणां तद् अहर् नश्यते पयः ॥
53.1.m: Meteors [fall] at both twilights, the milk of cows diminishes, / and on that day the sap of milky trees perishes.

53.2.s: apsu snigdhāni dṛśyante kākābadhnanti maṇḍalam | ūrdhvaṃ vadati gomāyur yadā rāhuḥ pradṛśyate ||
53.2.d: अप्सु स्निग्धानि दृश्यन्ते काकाबध्नन्ति मण्डलम् । ऊर्ध्वं वदति गोमायुर् यदा राहुः प्रदृश्यते ॥
53.2.m: Glossy [reflections] are seen in water, crows form circles, / and the jackal cries pointing upwards, when Rāhu is seen.

53.2.s: candragrahanimittāni śuklapakśāṣṭamīparam | ā paurṇamāsyā dṛśyeran sūryasya ca tathobhayoḥ ||
53.2.d: चन्द्रग्रहनिमित्तानि शुक्लपक्शाष्टमीपरम् । आ पौर्णमास्या दृश्येरन् सूर्यस्य च तथोभयोः ॥
53.2.m: The portents indicating a lunar eclipse may be seen beyond the eighth day of the bright fortnight / up to the full-moon day; and similarly for both in the case of the sun.

53.2.s: udito gṛhyamāṇas tu hanti vedavido janān | bālāṃś ca jaṭilān hanti ye ca kāṣāyavāsasaḥ ||
53.2.d: उदितो गृह्यमाणस् तु हन्ति वेदविदो जनान् । बालांश् च जटिलान् हन्ति ये च काषायवाससः ॥
53.2.m: Seized when risen, [the luminary] destroys people who know the Veda, / and it destroys children, ascetics with matted hair, and those who wear saffron garments.

53.2.s: yauvanasthāṃś ca pūrvāhṇe hanti yajñavido janān | audakāni ca sarvāṇi nāgendrāś cātra duḥkhitāḥ ||
53.2.d: यौवनस्थांश् च पूर्वाह्णे हन्ति यज्ञविदो जनान् । औदकानि च सर्वाणि नागेन्द्राश् चात्र दुःखिताः ॥
53.2.m: [Eclipsed] in the forenoon, it destroys those who are in their youth and people who know the sacrifices, / and all aquatic beings and the great serpent-kings are afflicted here.

53.2.s: atha madhyapathaṃ prāptaḥ śūdrān hanti ca taskarān | parivṛkto nṛpaṃ hanti candraś caraṇacāraṇān ||
53.2.d: अथ मध्यपथं प्राप्तः शूद्रान् हन्ति च तस्करान् । परिवृक्तो नृपं हन्ति चन्द्रश् चरणचारणान् ॥
53.2.m: Now, having reached mid-sky, it destroys Śūdras and thieves; / turned aside, the moon destroys the king and wandering minstrels.

53.3.s: pralambaḥ pramadān hanti kṣatraṃ rāṣṭraṃ ca sarvaśaḥ | traigartāś cātra pīḍyante ye ca daṇḍabhṛto janāḥ ||
53.3.d: प्रलम्बः प्रमदान् हन्ति क्षत्रं राष्ट्रं च सर्वशः । त्रैगर्ताश् चात्र पीड्यन्ते ये च दण्डभृतो जनाः ॥
53.3.m: Hanging down, it destroys women, and the warrior class and the realm entirely; / and here the people of Trigarta and those who bear weapons are afflicted.

53.3.s: uparakto yadodeti yadā vā pratitiṣṭhati | ayogakṣemam ādiśyet triṣu lokeṣu dāruṇam ||
53.3.d: उपरक्तो यदोदेति यदा वा प्रतितिष्ठति । अयोगक्षेमम् आदिश्येत् त्रिषु लोकेषु दारुणम् ॥
53.3.m: When it rises eclipsed, or when it stands [in the sky eclipsed], / one should predict terrible lack of security throughout the three worlds.

53.3.s: śāradaṃ trīṇi varṣāṇi sasyaṃ jātaṃ na pacyate | naidāghenātra jīvanti prajā mūlaphalena vā ||
53.3.d: शारदं त्रीणि वर्षाणि सस्यं जातं न पच्यते । नैदाघेनात्र जीवन्ति प्रजा मूलफलेन वा ॥
53.3.m: The autumn crop that has sprouted will not ripen for three years; / here the subjects survive on summer grain or on roots and fruits.

53.3.s: sarvaṃ saṃgrasate jyotiś ciram antardadhāti vā | hanti sphītāni rāṣṭrāṇi pradhānaṃ ca mahīpatim ||
53.3.d: सर्वं संग्रसते ज्योतिश् चिरम् अन्तर्दधाति वा । हन्ति स्फीतानि राष्ट्राणि प्रधानं च महीपतिम् ॥
53.3.m: If it swallows the whole luminary or conceals it for a long time, / it destroys prosperous realms and the foremost ruler of the earth.

53.3.s: yadi tu rāhur ubhau śaśibhāskarau grasati pakṣam anantaram antataḥ | puruṣaśoṇitakardamavāhinī bhavati bhūr na ca varṣati mādhavaḥ ||
53.3.d: यदि तु राहुर् उभौ शशिभास्करौ ग्रसति पक्षम् अनन्तरम् अन्ततः । पुरुषशोणितकर्दमवाहिनी भवति भूर् न च वर्षति माधवः ॥
53.3.m: If Rāhu swallows both the moon and the sun within one subsequent fortnight, / the earth becomes flowing with mud of human blood, and Indra does not rain.

53.4.s: gṛhītvā bhāskaraṃ pūrvaṃ gṛhṇāti śaśinaṃ yadi | taṃ tu somottaraṃ nāśas tatra rdhyante hi devatāḥ ||
53.4.d: गृहीत्वा भास्करं पूर्वं गृह्णाति शशिनं यदि । तं तु सोमोत्तरं नाशस् तत्र र्ध्यन्ते हि देवताः ॥
53.4.m: If, having seized the sun first, it [then] seizes the moon, / that is an eclipse followed by the moon; there the gods thrive.

53.4.s: vayasāṃ maraṇaṃ chidre prakīrṇe rakṣasāṃ vadhaḥ | nāgānāṃ tu mahānāge chidre devo na varṣati ||
53.4.d: वयसां मरणं छिद्रे प्रकीर्णे रक्षसां वधः । नागानां तु महानागे छिद्रे देवो न वर्षति ॥
53.4.m: Death of birds [occurs] in an eclipse that is broken; in one that is scattered, slaughter of Rakṣases; / in a great eclipse, [destruction] of serpent-beings; in a split eclipse, the rain-god does not rain.

53.4.s: śveto varṇo brāhmaṇānāṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ tu lohitaḥ | vaiśyānāṃ pītako varṇaḥ śūdrāṇāṃ kṛṣṇa ucyate ||
53.4.d: श्वेतो वर्णो ब्राह्मणानां क्षत्रियाणां तु लोहितः । वैश्यानां पीतको वर्णः शूद्राणां कृष्ण उच्यते ॥
53.4.m: White is the color of Brahmins, red of Kṣatriyas, / yellow is the color of Vaiśyas, and black is declared for Śūdras.

53.4.s: eteṣāṃ yena varṇena rāhuś carati bhāskare | yā jātis tasya varṇasya tāṃ sa pīḍayate grahaḥ ||
53.4.d: एतेषां येन वर्णेन राहुश् चरति भास्करे । या जातिस् तस्य वर्णस्य तां स पीडयते ग्रहः ॥
53.4.m: According to which of these colors Rāhu moves upon the sun, / the planet afflicts that caste which corresponds to that color.

53.4.s: śyāmo bhavati vātāya draukṣo bhavati vṛṣṭaye | haridraḥ sarvadhānyānāṃ kopaṃ sṛjati dāruṇam ||
53.4.d: श्यामो भवति वाताय द्रौक्षो भवति वृष्टये । हरिद्रः सर्वधान्यानां कोपं सृजति दारुणम् ॥
53.4.m: Dark blue leads to wind, dry leads to rain; / yellow causes a terrible surge in [the price of] all grains.

53.5.s: tāmro bhavati śastrāya śastrāya rūkṣo bhavati mṛtyave | bahvākāras tu bhūtānāṃ ghoraṃ janayate jvaram ||
53.5.d: ताम्रो भवति शस्त्राय शस्त्राय रूक्षो भवति मृत्यवे । बह्वाकारस् तु भूतानां घोरं जनयते ज्वरम् ॥
53.5.m: Copper-colored leads to weapons, rough leads to weapons and death; / multiform, it produces a fearful fever for living beings.

53.5.s: dhūmavarṇo 'gnivarṇo vā grāmeṣu nagareṣu vā | agnyutpātān gṛhasthānāṃ karotīha mahāgrahaḥ ||
53.5.d: धूमवर्णो ऽग्निवर्णो वा ग्रामेषु नगरेषु वा । अग्न्युत्पातान् गृहस्थानां करोतीह महाग्रहः ॥
53.5.m: Smoke-colored or fire-colored in villages or in cities, / the great planet here causes portentous fires for householders.

53.5.s: nīlalohitaparyanto rāhuś carati bhāskare | amātyo hanti rājānaṃ rājā vāmātyam ātmaha ||
53.5.d: नीललोहितपर्यन्तो राहुश् चरति भास्करे । अमात्यो हन्ति राजानं राजा वामात्यम् आत्मह ॥
53.5.m: When Rāhu moves upon the sun with dark-blue and red rims, / a minister kills the king, or the king, self-destructive, kills the minister.

53.5.s: yasya rājñaś ca nakṣatre svarbhānur uparajyati | rājyabhraṃśaṃ suhṛnnāśaṃ maraṇaṃ cātra nirdiśet ||
53.5.d: यस्य राज्ञश् च नक्षत्रे स्वर्भानुर् उपरज्यति । राज्यभ्रंशं सुहृन्नाशं मरणं चात्र निर्दिशेत् ॥
53.5.m: In whichever king's lunar mansion Svarbhānu causes an eclipse, / in that case one should predict loss of the kingdom, death of friends, and demise.

53.6.s: snigdhavarṇo yadārciṣmān parvasthaḥ snehavān grahaḥ | kṣipraṃ vāpy uditaṃ brūhi sarvabhūtabhayāya vai ||
53.6.d: स्निग्धवर्णो यदार्चिष्मान् पर्वस्थः स्नेहवान् ग्रहः । क्षिप्रं वाप्य् उदितं ब्रूहि सर्वभूतभयाय वै ॥
53.6.m: When the planet situated at the conjunction is glossy-colored, radiant, and oily, / or declare it [so] when swiftly risen, it brings fear to all beings.

53.6.s: pradakṣiṇe tu somasya apasavye tu vigrahaḥ | raśmibhede bhayaṃ ghoram ullekhe mantriṇāṃ vadhaḥ ||
53.6.d: प्रदक्षिणे तु सोमस्य अपसव्ये तु विग्रहः । रश्मिभेदे भयं घोरम् उल्लेखे मन्त्रिणां वधः ॥
53.6.m: When [the passage] is clockwise around the moon, [it brings good], but when counter-clockwise, conflict; / when the rays are pierced, fearful terror; when it is grazed, slaughter of ministers.

53.6.s: darśayitvā tu rūpāṇi yadā rāhur na dṛśyate | śastradurbhikṣasaṃpātair bhayaṃ ghoraṃ vinirdiśet ||
53.6.d: दर्शयित्वा तु रूपाणि यदा राहुर् न दृश्यते । शस्त्रदुर्भिक्षसंपातैर् भयं घोरं विनिर्दिशेत् ॥
53.6.m: When Rāhu, having displayed its forms, is no longer seen, / one should predict fearful terror through clashes of weapons and famine.

53.6.s: gṛhītāstamitayos tu na bhuñjīran dvijātayaḥ | ā punardarśanāt tābhyāṃ japahomau vivartayet ||
53.6.d: गृहीतास्तमितयोस् तु न भुञ्जीरन् द्विजातयः । आ पुनर्दर्शनात् ताभ्यां जपहोमौ विवर्तयेत् ॥
53.6.m: If [the luminaries] set while seized, twice-born men should not eat; / until they are seen again, one should desist from recitation and oblations.

53.6.s: candrasūryagrahe nādyād adyāt snātvā tu muktayoḥ | amuktayor astaṃgayor adyāt snātvā pare 'hani ||
53.6.d: चन्द्रसूर्यग्रहे नाद्याद् अद्यात् स्नात्वा तु मुक्तयोः । अमुक्तयोर् अस्तंगयोर् अद्यात् स्नात्वा परे ऽहनि ॥
53.6.m: One should not eat during an eclipse of the moon or the sun; but having bathed, one may eat when they are released; / if they set unreleased, one may eat after bathing on the following day.

53.6.s: tataḥ ṣaṭsu tataḥ ṣaṭsu tato 'dhyardheṣū vā punaḥ | ardhavarṣeṣu māseṣu ādityasya tato grahaḥ ||
53.6.d: ततः षट्सु ततः षट्सु ततो ऽध्यर्धेषू वा पुनः । अर्धवर्षेषु मासेषु आदित्यस्य ततो ग्रहः ॥
53.6.m: Then after six, then after six, or again after one and a half, / [or] after half-years—after [such] months, an eclipse of the sun occurs.

53.6.s: tataḥ ṣaṭsu tataḥ ṣaṭsu triṣu varṣeṣu vā punaḥ | etāvad eva rāhos tu cāram āhur manīṣiṇaḥ ||
53.6.d: ततः षट्सु ततः षट्सु त्रिषु वर्षेषु वा पुनः । एतावद् एव राहोस् तु चारम् आहुर् मनीषिणः ॥
53.6.m: Then after six, then after six, or again after three years— / precisely this, the wise say, is the course of Rāhu.

54.1.s: oṃ bhārgavas tu purovāca maharṣīn bhagavān ṛṣiḥ | ketusaṃcāraṃ śṛṇuta utthānaṃ caiva yādṛśam ||
54.1.d: ओं भार्गवस् तु पुरोवाच महर्षीन् भगवान् ऋषिः । केतुसंचारं शृणुत उत्थानं चैव यादृशम् ॥
54.1.m: Om. The venerable sage Bhārgava formerly spoke to the great sages: / "Listen to the course of comets and of what sort their appearance is!

54.1.s: nimittani ca vakṣyāmitasyoktāni hi yāni tu | tāni sarvāṇi jāniyād utpātajñānakovidaḥ ||
54.1.d: निमित्तनि च वक्ष्यामितस्योक्तानि हि यानि तु । तानि सर्वाणि जानियाद् उत्पातज्ञानकोविदः ॥
54.1.m: And I shall explain the portents that have been declared concerning it; / one skilled in the knowledge of omens should know all of them.

54.1.s: viprāñ śvetākṛtir hanti kṣatriyān hanti lohitaḥ | vaiśyāṃs tu pītako hanti śūdrān hanti tathāsitaḥ ||
54.1.d: विप्राञ् श्वेताकृतिर् हन्ति क्षत्रियान् हन्ति लोहितः । वैश्यांस् तु पीतको हन्ति शूद्रान् हन्ति तथासितः ॥
54.1.m: A white-formed [comet] destroys Brahmins; a red one destroys Kṣatriyas; / a yellow one destroys Vaiśyas; and a black one likewise destroys Śūdras.

54.1.s: itarān pīḍayet ketur anyavarṇo yadā bhavet | ṣaṇmāsābhyantare rājño maraṇaṃ ca tadādiśet ||
54.1.d: इतरान् पीडयेत् केतुर् अन्यवर्णो यदा भवेत् । षण्मासाभ्यन्तरे राज्ञो मरणं च तदादिशेत् ॥
54.1.m: When a comet is of a different color, it will afflict other [castes]; / and within six months one should predict the king's death.

54.1.s: śvetaḥ śastrākulaṃ kuryāl lohitas tv agnito bhayam | kṣudbhayaṃ pītakaḥ kuryāt kṛṣṇo rogam atholbaṇam ||
54.1.d: श्वेतः शस्त्राकुलं कुर्याल् लोहितस् त्व् अग्नितो भयम् । क्षुद्भयं पीतकः कुर्यात् कृष्णो रोगम् अथोल्बणम् ॥
54.1.m: A white one will cause panic from weapons; a red one, fear of fire; / a yellow one will cause fear of famine; and a black one, virulent disease.

54.2.s: yasmin deśe śiras tasya sa deśaḥ pīḍyate bhṛśam | madhye tu madhyamā pīḍā yato pucchaṃ tato jayaḥ ||
54.2.d: यस्मिन् देशे शिरस् तस्य स देशः पीड्यते भृशम् । मध्ये तु मध्यमा पीडा यतो पुच्छं ततो जयः ॥
54.2.m: In whatever region its head is, that region is afflicted severely; / in the middle [there is] moderate affliction; where its tail is, there is victory.

54.2.s: śaktyākāro 'tināśāya duḥkhāya musalākṛtiḥ | dīrghaḥ sūkṣmaḥ sukhāyaiva hrasvaḥ sthūlo vināśakṛt ||
54.2.d: शक्त्याकारो ऽतिनाशाय दुःखाय मुसलाकृतिः । दीर्घः सूक्ष्मः सुखायैव ह्रस्वः स्थूलो विनाशकृत् ॥
54.2.m: Shaped like a lance, it leads to utter ruin; shaped like a pestle, to sorrow; / long and slender, to happiness alone; short and thick, it brings destruction.

54.2.s: utthānaṃ caiva ketūnāṃ vināśāyaiva hi smṛtam | tasmād ātharvaṇair mantraiḥ śamanam ārayed budhaḥ ||
54.2.d: उत्थानं चैव केतूनां विनाशायैव हि स्मृतम् । तस्माद् आथर्वणैर् मन्त्रैः शमनम् आरयेद् बुधः ॥
54.2.m: The appearance of comets is remembered indeed as bringing destruction; / therefore a wise man should perform appeasement with Atharvan mantras.

54.2.s: māhendrūn anṛtān raydrūn vauśvadevīm athāpi vā | utpāteṣu mahāśāntiṃ kārayed bahudakṣiṇām ||
54.2.d: माहेन्द्रून् अनृतान् रय्द्रून् वौश्वदेवीम् अथापि वा । उत्पातेषु महाशान्तिं कारयेद् बहुदक्षिणाम् ॥
54.2.m: Belonging to great Indra, [Varuṇa], the Rudras, or even the Viśvedevas, / he should have performed a great propitiatory rite for portents, accompanied by generous sacrificial fees.

54.2.s: ārādhitāḥ śamaṃ yānti tadutpātā na saṃśayaḥ | homair japyaiś ca vividhair dānaiś cabahurūpakaiḥ ||
54.2.d: आराधिताः शमं यान्ति तदुत्पाता न संशयः । होमैर् जप्यैश् च विविधैर् दानैश् चबहुरूपकैः ॥
54.2.m: Propitiated, those portents are undoubtedly pacified / by various burnt offerings, recitations, and manifold gifts.

54.2.s: tasya yatra śiro deśe tata utthāya vāvrajet | dhanaṃ vā sarvam utsṛjya mṛtyor mucyetā vā na vā ||
54.2.d: तस्य यत्र शिरो देशे तत उत्थाय वाव्रजेत् । धनं वा सर्वम् उत्सृज्य मृत्योर् मुच्येता वा न वा ॥
54.2.m: Leaving that country where its head lies, he should depart; / or abandoning all wealth, he may or may not be freed from death.

54.2.s: dattvā vā pṛthivīṃ sarvāṃ rājā śāntiṃ niyacchati ||
54.2.d: दत्त्वा वा पृथिवीं सर्वां राजा शान्तिं नियच्छति ॥
54.2.m: Or having given away the entire earth, the king attains peace.

55.1.s: om ṛtuketūn pravakṣyāmi yathāvad anupūrvaśaḥ | yāvanto yasya putrāḥ syuḥ kuryur yac coditā divi ||
55.1.d: ओम् ऋतुकेतून् प्रवक्ष्यामि यथावद् अनुपूर्वशः । यावन्तो यस्य पुत्राः स्युः कुर्युर् यच् चोदिता दिवि ॥
55.1.m: Om. I will explain the seasonal comets properly in regular succession: / how many sons there are of each, and what they will do when arisen in the sky.

55.1.s: sarve te dharaṇījātā māsā ye devanirmitāḥ | ādityaraśmibhir baddhāḥ saure tiṣṭhanti maṇḍale ||
55.1.d: सर्वे ते धरणीजाता मासा ये देवनिर्मिताः । आदित्यरश्मिभिर् बद्धाः सौरे तिष्ठन्ति मण्डले ॥
55.1.m: All these are born of the earth, [corresponding to] months arranged by the gods; / held by the sun's rays, they abide in the solar disc.

55.1.s: daśa vai vāruṇās tatra sūryaputrās tu viṃśatiḥ | caturviṃśatir āgneyā yamaputrā nava smṛtāḥ ||
55.1.d: दश वै वारुणास् तत्र सूर्यपुत्रास् तु विंशतिः । चतुर्विंशतिर् आग्नेया यमपुत्रा नव स्मृताः ॥
55.1.m: Ten indeed are sons of Varuṇa there, and twenty are sons of the Sun; / twenty-four are born of Agni, [and] the sons of Yama are recorded as nine.

55.1.s: aṣṭādaśa ca kauberā vāyuputrās tu viṃśatiḥ | eṣā saṃkhyā tu ketūnāṃ śatam ekottaraṃ smṛtam ||
55.1.d: अष्टादश च कौबेरा वायुपुत्रास् तु विंशतिः । एषा संख्या तु केतूनां शतम् एकोत्तरं स्मृतम् ॥
55.1.m: Eighteen belong to Kubera, and twenty are sons of Vāyu; / this is the enumeration of comets, traditionally handed down as one hundred and one.
In Śrāvaṇa and Prauṣṭhapada, one should designate those belonging to Varuṇa.

55.1.s: ārādhitāḥ śamaṃ yānti tadutpātā na saṃśayaḥ | homair jāpaiś ca vividhair dānaiś ca bahurūpakaiḥ ||
55.1.d: आराधिताः शमं यान्ति तदुत्पाता न संशयः । होमैर् जापैश् च विविधैर् दानैश् च बहुरूपकैः ॥
55.1.m: [Propitiated, those portents are undoubtedly pacified / by various burnt offerings, recitations, and manifold gifts.]

55.1.s: āvāhayet tato meghān pūrṇāṃ kuryād vasuṃdharām | unmattāḥ sarito yānti jalavegasamāhitāḥ ||
55.1.d: आवाहयेत् ततो मेघान् पूर्णां कुर्याद् वसुंधराम् । उन्मत्ताः सरितो यान्ति जलवेगसमाहिताः ॥
55.1.m: Then it summons the clouds [and] makes the earth full; / rivers run wild, swept by the rush of waters.

55.1.s: dhānyaṃ samarghatāṃ yāti ītayo na bhavanti hi udaye vāruṇānāṃ tu etad bhavati lakṣaṇam ||
55.1.d: धान्यं समर्घतां याति ईतयो न भवन्ति हि उदये वारुणानां तु एतद् भवति लक्षणम् ॥
55.1.m: Grain becomes cheap, and calamities do not occur; / at the rising of the comets of Varuṇa, this is the characteristic.

55.2.s: aśvayuji kārttike ca sūryaputrān vinirdiśet | teṣāṃ caiva tu karmāṇi lakṣaṇaiḥ śṛṇu yādṛśaiḥ ||
55.2.d: अश्वयुजि कार्त्तिके च सूर्यपुत्रान् विनिर्दिशेत् । तेषां चैव तु कर्माणि लक्षणैः शृणु यादृशैः ॥
55.2.m: In Aśvayuj and Kārttika, one should designate the sons of the Sun; / hear their deeds according to what their characteristics are.

55.2.s: tato dahati dīptāṃśuḥ sarvānnāni divākaraḥ | mriyante ca tathā gāvaḥ śvāpadāś ca viśeṣataḥ ||
55.2.d: ततो दहति दीप्तांशुः सर्वान्नानि दिवाकरः । म्रियन्ते च तथा गावः श्वापदाश् च विशेषतः ॥
55.2.m: Then the sun of blazing rays scorches all crops; / and cows, and beasts of prey in particular, die.

55.2.s: viṣaṃ ca prabalaṃ tatra sarvadamṣṭriṣu dāruṇam | udaye sūryaputrāṇām etad bhavati lakṣaṇam ||
55.2.d: विषं च प्रबलं तत्र सर्वदम्ष्ट्रिषु दारुणम् । उदये सूर्यपुत्राणाम् एतद् भवति लक्षणम् ॥
55.2.m: Poison becomes potent and terrible in all fanged creatures; / at the rising of the sons of the Sun, this is the characteristic.

55.3.s: mārgaśīrṣe ca pauṣe ca agniputrān vinirdiśet | teṣāṃ caiva tu karmāṇi lakṣaṇaiḥ śṛṇu yādṛśaiḥ ||
55.3.d: मार्गशीर्षे च पौषे च अग्निपुत्रान् विनिर्दिशेत् । तेषां चैव तु कर्माणि लक्षणैः शृणु यादृशैः ॥
55.3.m: In Mārgaśīrṣa and Pauṣa, one should designate the sons of Agni; / hear their deeds according to what their characteristics are.

55.3.s: agnir dahati rāṣṭrāṇi haritāni vanāni ca vidravanti tato deśāḥ samantād bhayapīḍitāḥ ||
55.3.d: अग्निर् दहति राष्ट्राणि हरितानि वनानि च विद्रवन्ति ततो देशाः समन्ताद् भयपीडिताः ॥
55.3.m: Fire burns kingdoms and green forests; / regions then flee in all directions, stricken with fear.

55.3.s: kasmiṃś cij jāyate kṣemaṃ kasmiṃś cij jāyate bhayam | udaye hy agniputrāṇām etad bhavati lakṣaṇam ||
55.3.d: कस्मिंश् चिज् जायते क्षेमं कस्मिंश् चिज् जायते भयम् । उदये ह्य् अग्निपुत्राणाम् एतद् भवति लक्षणम् ॥
55.3.m: In some [realm] well-being arises, in some realm fear arises; / at the rising of the sons of Agni, this is the characteristic.

55.4.s: māghaphālbunayor madhye yamaputrān vinirdiśet | teṣāṃ caiva tu karmāṇi lakṣaṇaiḥ śṛṇu yādṛśaiḥ ||
55.4.d: माघफाल्बुनयोर् मध्ये यमपुत्रान् विनिर्दिशेत् । तेषां चैव तु कर्माणि लक्षणैः शृणु यादृशैः ॥
55.4.m: Between Māgha and Phālguna, one should designate the sons of Yama; / hear their deeds according to what their characteristics are.

55.4.s: śīghraṃ bhavati durbhikṣaṃ hāhābhūtam acetanam | chardijvarātisārāś ca glāniś caivākṣivedanā ||
55.4.d: शीघ्रं भवति दुर्भिक्षं हाहाभूतम् अचेतनम् । छर्दिज्वरातिसाराश् च ग्लानिश् चैवाक्षिवेदना ॥
55.4.m: Swiftly there is a senseless famine filled with lamentations, / and vomiting, fever, diarrhea, exhaustion, and eye-pain.
At the rising of the sons of Yama, this is the characteristic.

55.5.s: caitravaiśākhayor madhye kauberāṃs tu vinirdiśet | teṣāṃ caiva tu karmāṇi lakṣaṇaiḥ śṛṇu yādṛśaiḥ ||
55.5.d: चैत्रवैशाखयोर् मध्ये कौबेरांस् तु विनिर्दिशेत् । तेषां चैव तु कर्माणि लक्षणैः शृणु यादृशैः ॥
55.5.m: Between Caitra and Vaiśākha, one should designate those belonging to Kubera; / hear their deeds according to what their characteristics are.

55.5.s: ucchritair dhvajavedībhir ucchritair dhvajatoraṇaiḥ | havirdhūmākulā tatra dṛśyate vasudhā tadā ||
55.5.d: उच्छ्रितैर् ध्वजवेदीभिर् उच्छ्रितैर् ध्वजतोरणैः । हविर्धूमाकुला तत्र दृश्यते वसुधा तदा ॥
55.5.m: With elevated flag-altars and elevated flag-arches, / the earth is then seen filled with the smoke of oblations.

55.5.s: triviṣṭapaṃ samāpannas tadā śakro mahīpatiḥ | evaṃ prajñās tu manyante kubere graham āgate ||
55.5.d: त्रिविष्टपं समापन्नस् तदा शक्रो महीपतिः । एवं प्रज्ञास् तु मन्यन्ते कुबेरे ग्रहम् आगते ॥
55.5.m: The ruler of the earth then attains heaven like Indra; / thus indeed the wise consider when the heavenly body has arrived in the quarter of Kubera.

55.5.s: udaye tu kuberāṇām etad bhavati lakṣaṇam ||
55.5.d: उदये तु कुबेराणाम् एतद् भवति लक्षणम् ॥
55.5.m: At the rising of the sons of Kubera, this is the characteristic.

55.6.s: jyaiṣṭhe caiva tathāṣāḍhe vāyuputrān vinirdiśet | teṣāṃ caiva tu karmāṇi lakṣaṇaiḥ śṛṇu yādṛśaiḥ ||
55.6.d: ज्यैष्ठे चैव तथाषाढे वायुपुत्रान् विनिर्दिशेत् । तेषां चैव तु कर्माणि लक्षणैः शृणु यादृशैः ॥
55.6.m: In Jyaiṣṭha and likewise in Āṣāḍha, one should designate the sons of Vāyu; / hear their deeds according to what their characteristics are.

55.6.s: vāyanti ca mahāvātā mahāyuddhaṃ mahābhayam | bhajyante ca mahāvṛkṣās toraṇāṭṭālakāni ca ||
55.6.d: वायन्ति च महावाता महायुद्धं महाभयम् । भज्यन्ते च महावृक्षास् तोरणाट्टालकानि च ॥
55.6.m: Mighty winds blow, [and there is] great war and great terror; / mighty trees, archways, and watchtowers are shattered.

55.6.s: gṛhāṇi rāmaṇīyāni kṣayaṃ yānti jalāni ca | udaye vāyuputrāṇām etad bhavati lakṣaṇam ||
55.6.d: गृहाणि रामणीयानि क्षयं यान्ति जलानि च । उदये वायुपुत्राणाम् एतद् भवति लक्षणम् ॥
55.6.m: Delightful homes and waters go to ruin; / at the rising of the sons of Vāyu, this is the characteristic.

55.6.s: ṛtugatam udayanam eṣāṃ mahaujasāṃ vāruṇādiketūnām | jānāti yaḥ phalaṃ ca protkṛṣṭāḥ saṃpadas tasya ||
55.6.d: ऋतुगतम् उदयनम् एषां महौजसां वारुणादिकेतूनाम् । जानाति यः फलं च प्रोत्कृष्टाः संपदस् तस्य ॥
55.6.m: Whoever knows the seasonal rising of these comets of mighty power, beginning with Varuṇa, / and [knows] their result, his prosperities are elevated.

56.1.s: oṃ kṛttikārohiṇīsaumyaṃ madhyaṃ kūrmasya nirdiśet || śeṣān ṛkṣavibhāge tu trikaṃ prati vinirdiśet ||
56.1.d: ओं कृत्तिकारोहिणीसौम्यं मध्यं कूर्मस्य निर्दिशेत् ॥ शेषान् ऋक्षविभागे तु त्रिकं प्रति विनिर्दिशेत् ॥
56.1.m: Om. One should designate Kṛttikā, Rohiṇī, and Saumya as the middle of the tortoise; / but the remaining [regions] one should assign to triads according to the division of the constellations.

56.1.s: sāketamithile mekalālayāv ahichattranāgapuraṃ kāśipāriyātrakurupāñcālāḥ || atha kosalakauśāmbītīraṃ pāṭaliputraṃ kaliṅgapurapṛthivīmaṇḍalamadhye 'bhihate 'bhihanyāt ||
56.1.d: साकेतमिथिले मेकलालयाव् अहिछत्त्रनागपुरं काशिपारियात्रकुरुपाञ्चालाः ॥ अथ कोसलकौशाम्बीतीरं पाटलिपुत्रं कलिङ्गपुरपृथिवीमण्डलमध्ये ऽभिहते ऽभिहन्यात् ॥
56.1.m: Sāketa, Mithilā, the homes of the Mekalas, Ahicchatra, Nāgapura, Kāśi, Pāriyātra, and the Kuru-Pañcālas; / then the region of Kosala, Kauśāmbī, Pāṭaliputra, Kaliṅgapura—when the middle of the circle of the earth is struck, it will strike [these].

56.1.s: aṅgavaṅgakaliṅgamāgadhamahendragavasam ambaṣṭhāḥ || bhāgāḥ pūrvasamudrāḥ śirasy abhihate 'bhihanyāt ||
56.1.d: अङ्गवङ्गकलिङ्गमागधमहेन्द्रगवसम् अम्बष्ठाः ॥ भागाः पूर्वसमुद्राः शिरस्य् अभिहते ऽभिहन्यात् ॥
56.1.m: Aṅga, Vaṅga, Kaliṅga, Magadha, Mahendragava, the Ambaṣṭhas, / [and] the eastern oceans: when its head is struck, it will strike [these].

56.1.s: khaśabhadrā samataṭasamavardhamānakavaidehā gāndhārāḥ || kosalatosalaveṇātaṭasajjapurā mādreyatāmaliptā dakṣiṇapūrve hate 'bhihanyāt ||
56.1.d: खशभद्रा समतटसमवर्धमानकवैदेहा गान्धाराः ॥ कोसलतोसलवेणातटसज्जपुरा माद्रेयतामलिप्ता दक्षिणपूर्वे हते ऽभिहन्यात् ॥
56.1.m: The Khaśas, Bhadras, Samataṭa, Samavardhamāna, the Vaidehas, the Gāndhāras, / Kosala, Tosala, the Veṇā coast, Sajjapura, the Mādreyas, and the Tāmaliptas: when the southeast is struck, it will strike [these].

56.1.s: āvantyakā vidarbhā matsyā cakorabhīmagamrathā yavanavalayakāntīsiṃhalalaṅkuṇanāsikyakarmaṇoyāmimahinarmadabhṛgukacchā dakṣiṇapaścād dhate 'bhihanyāt ||
56.1.d: आवन्त्यका विदर्भा मत्स्या चकोरभीमगम्रथा यवनवलयकान्तीसिंहललङ्कुणनासिक्यकर्मणोयामिमहिनर्मदभृगुकच्छा दक्षिणपश्चाद् धते ऽभिहन्यात् ॥
56.1.m: The Āvantyakas, Vidarbhas, Matsyas, Cakoras, Bhīmarathas, the Yavanas, Valaya, Kāntī, Siṃhala, the Laṅkuṇas, Nāsikya, Karmaṇoyā, the Mahī, the Narmadā, and Bhṛgukaccha: when the southwest is struck, it will strike [these].
The Sahya mountain, Vaijayantī, the Kuṅkuṇas, Nāsikya, Karmaṇoyā, the Mahī, the Narmadā, and Bhṛgukaccha: when the southwest is struck, it will strike [these].

56.1.d: सौराष्ट्रसिन्धुसौवीरमालवा रामराष्ट्रकान्वीतान् ॥ आनर्तगच्छयन्त्रान् पुच्छे ऽभिहते ऽभिहन्यात् ॥
56.1.m: Saurāṣṭra, the Indus, Sauvīra, the Mālavas, accompanied by the Rāmarāṣṭrakas, / the Ānartas, Gacchas, and Yantras: when the tail is struck, it will strike [these].

56.1.s: sārasvatāṃs trigartān matsyān nānvārabālhikān || mathurāpuraṃgadeśān uttarabhāge hate 'bhihanyāt ||
56.1.d: सारस्वतांस् त्रिगर्तान् मत्स्यान् नान्वारबाल्हिकान् ॥ मथुरापुरंगदेशान् उत्तरभागे हते ऽभिहन्यात् ॥
56.1.m: The Sarasvatī dwellers, Trigartas, Matsyas, Nānvāras, and Bālhikas, / the city of Mathurā, and the Gaṅgā lands: when the northern part is struck, it will strike [these].

56.1.s: brahmāvartaṃ śatadruhimavantaṃ parvataṃ ca mainākaṃ kāśmīraṃ caiva tathā uttarapārśve hate 'bhihanyāt ||
56.1.d: ब्रह्मावर्तं शतद्रुहिमवन्तं पर्वतं च मैनाकं काश्मीरं चैव तथा उत्तरपार्श्वे हते ऽभिहन्यात् ॥
56.1.m: Brahmāvarta, Śatadru, Mount Himavat, Maināka, / and likewise Kaśmīr: when the northern flank is struck, it will strike [these].

56.1.s: nepālakāmarūpaṃ ca videhodumbaraṃ tathā || tathāvantyaḥ kaikayaś ca uttarapūrve hate 'bhihanyāt ||
56.1.d: नेपालकामरूपं च विदेहोदुम्बरं तथा ॥ तथावन्त्यः कैकयश् च उत्तरपूर्वे हते ऽभिहन्यात् ॥
56.1.m: Nepal, Kāmarūpa, Videha, Udumbara, / as well as Avanti and Kaikaya: when the northeast is struck, it will strike [these].

57.1.s: viśākhe kṛttikāḥ puṣyaḥ pūrvau proṣṭhapadau tathā | bharaṇyaś ca maghāś caiva phalgunyau prathame tathā ||
57.1.d: विशाखे कृत्तिकाः पुष्यः पूर्वौ प्रोष्ठपदौ तथा । भरण्यश् च मघाश् चैव फल्गुन्यौ प्रथमे तथा ॥
57.1.m: Viśākhā, Kṛttikā, Puṣya, and both Pūrva Proṣṭhapadās, / the Bharaṇīs, Maghā, and both the former Phalgunīs:

57.1.s: yady atra calate bhūmir nirghātolkāsta eva vā | aśarīrāś ca nardante kampante daivatāni ca ||
57.1.d: यद्य् अत्र चलते भूमिर् निर्घातोल्कास्त एव वा । अशरीराश् च नर्दन्ते कम्पन्ते दैवतानि च ॥
57.1.m: if the earth shakes here, or if there is a crash of thunder or meteors, / bodiless voices bellow, and statues of the deities tremble,

57.1.s: ādityo vātra gṛhyeta somo vāpy uparajyate | āgneyaṃ tad vijānīyād durbhikṣaṃ cātra nirdiśet ||
57.1.d: आदित्यो वात्र गृह्येत सोमो वाप्य् उपरज्यते । आग्नेयं तद् विजानीयाद् दुर्भिक्षं चात्र निर्दिशेत् ॥
57.1.m: Or if the sun is eclipsed here, or the moon is obscured, / one should recognize it as of Agni, and one should predict famine here.

57.1.s: alpakṣīrās tathā gāvo agner vyādhiś ca jāyate | purāṇi deśā grāmāś ca pīḍyante hy agninā tadā ||
57.1.d: अल्पक्षीरास् तथा गावो अग्नेर् व्याधिश् च जायते । पुराणि देशा ग्रामाश् च पीड्यन्ते ह्य् अग्निना तदा ॥
57.1.m: Cows yield little milk, and a disease of fire arises; / cities, regions, and villages are afflicted by fire then.

57.1.s: pīḍyante cāgnikarmāṇo agniveśāś ca ye narāḥ | pittajvaras tathā śvāsaha prajāḥ pīḍayate tadā ||
57.1.d: पीड्यन्ते चाग्निकर्माणो अग्निवेशाश् च ये नराः । पित्तज्वरस् तथा श्वासह प्रजाः पीडयते तदा ॥
57.1.m: Those who work with fire and men of the Agniveśa [lineage] are afflicted; / bilious fever and asthma then afflict the people.

57.1.s: akṣirogās tathā ghorāḥ puruṣāṇāṃ viśeṣataḥ | āpagāś cātra śuṣyanti na ca sasyavatī mahī ||
57.1.d: अक्षिरोगास् तथा घोराः पुरुषाणां विशेषतः । आपगाश् चात्र शुष्यन्ति न च सस्यवती मही ॥
57.1.m: Likewise terrible eye diseases, especially for men; / rivers dry up here, and the earth bears no crops.

57.1.s: tapyate ca tadā bhūmir na ca devo 'bhivarṣati | nīlalohitaparyaktā aphalāḥ pādapās tathā ||
57.1.d: तप्यते च तदा भूमिर् न च देवो ऽभिवर्षति । नीललोहितपर्यक्ता अफलाः पादपास् तथा ॥
57.1.m: The earth is scorched then, and the rain-god does not rain; / trees are marked with dark blue and red, and are barren of fruit.

57.1.s: durbhikṣaṃ marako vyādhiḥ paracakrabhayaṃ tathā | etai rūpais tu vijñeyam āgneyaṃ caladarśanam ||
57.1.d: दुर्भिक्षं मरको व्याधिः परचक्रभयं तथा । एतै रूपैस् तु विज्ञेयम् आग्नेयं चलदर्शनम् ॥
57.1.m: Famine, pestilence, disease, and fear of an enemy host— / through these characteristics an earthquake of Agni is to be recognized.

57.2.s: hasto 'śvinyau tathā citrā ṛkṣam aryamadaivatam | brāhmaṃ mṛgaśiraḥ svātir vāyavyaṃ maṇḍalaṃ smṛtam ||
57.2.d: हस्तो ऽश्विन्यौ तथा चित्रा ऋक्षम् अर्यमदैवतम् । ब्राह्मं मृगशिरः स्वातिर् वायव्यं मण्डलं स्मृतम् ॥
57.2.m: Hasta, the two Aśvinīs, and Citrā; the lunar mansion whose deity is Aryaman; / that of Brahmā, Mṛgaśiras, and Svāti are known as the circle of Vāyu.

57.2.s: yady atra calate bhūmir nirghātolkāsta eva vā | aśarīrāś ca nardante kampante daivatāni ca ||
57.2.d: यद्य् अत्र चलते भूमिर् निर्घातोल्कास्त एव वा । अशरीराश् च नर्दन्ते कम्पन्ते दैवतानि च ॥
57.2.m: If the earth shakes here, or a crash of thunder and a meteor-fall [occur], / or bodiless beings roar, and the deities tremble,

57.2.s: ādityo vātra gṛhyeta somo vāpy uparajyate | vāyavyaṃ tad vijānīyād akṣemaṃ cātra nirdiśet ||
57.2.d: आदित्यो वात्र गृह्येत सोमो वाप्य् उपरज्यते । वायव्यं तद् विजानीयाद् अक्षेमं चात्र निर्दिशेत् ॥
57.2.m: or if the sun is eclipsed here, or the moon is obscured, / one should recognize it as of Vāyu, and one should predict danger here.

57.2.s: pāṃsuvarṣaṃ tadā ghoraṃ kṣīre sarpir na vidyate | prāsādatoraṇādīni prapatanti mahītale ||
57.2.d: पांसुवर्षं तदा घोरं क्षीरे सर्पिर् न विद्यते । प्रासादतोरणादीनि प्रपतन्ति महीतले ॥
57.2.m: A terrible rain of dust then [falls], no clarified butter is found in milk, / [and] mansions, archways, and the like crash down onto the earth.

57.2.s: madrakā yavanāś caiva śakāḥ kāmbojabālhikāḥ | gandhārāś ca vinaśyanti etaiḥ sārdhaṃ tathā kila ||
57.2.d: मद्रका यवनाश् चैव शकाः काम्बोजबाल्हिकाः । गन्धाराश् च विनश्यन्ति एतैः सार्धं तथा किल ॥
57.2.m: The Madrakas, Yavanas, Śakas, Kāmbojas, and Bālhikas, / and the Gandhāras perish together with these, it is said.

57.2.s: gajā vājina uṣṭrāś ca vṛkā nakulaceṭakāḥ | pīḍyante vyādhinā sarve ye ca śastropajīvinaḥ ||
57.2.d: गजा वाजिन उष्ट्राश् च वृका नकुलचेटकाः । पीड्यन्ते व्याधिना सर्वे ये च शस्त्रोपजीविनः ॥
57.2.m: Elephants, horses, camels, wolves, and domestic ichneumons, / and all those who live by weapons are afflicted by disease.

57.2.s: pure śreṣṭhā vinaśyanti gaṇeṣu guṇasaṃmitāḥ | gṛhāṇi ramaṇīyāni viśīryante ca sarvaśaḥ ||
57.2.d: पुरे श्रेष्ठा विनश्यन्ति गणेषु गुणसंमिताः । गृहाणि रमणीयानि विशीर्यन्ते च सर्वशः ॥
57.2.m: The eminent in the city perish, [as do] those endowed with virtues in assemblies; / and delightful homes are shattered on all sides.

57.2.s: āyāsaś colbaṇas tatra śastrabhrāmaḥ samantataḥ | etai rūpais tu vijñeyaṃ vāyavyaṃ caladarśanam ||
57.2.d: आयासश् चोल्बणस् तत्र शस्त्रभ्रामः समन्ततः । एतै रूपैस् तु विज्ञेयं वायव्यं चलदर्शनम् ॥
57.2.m: Distress is severe there, and brandishing of weapons [occurs] everywhere; / through these characteristics an earthquake of Vāyu is to be recognized.

57.3.s: ārdrāśleṣās tathā mūlan pūrvāṣāḍhās tathaiva ca | vāruṇaṃ revatī caiva sūryadaivatyam eva ca ||
57.3.d: आर्द्राश्लेषास् तथा मूलन् पूर्वाषाढास् तथैव च । वारुणं रेवती चैव सूर्यदैवत्यम् एव च ॥
57.3.m: Ārdrā, Āśleṣā, Mūla, and Pūrvāṣāḍhā, / that of Varuṇa, Revatī, and that whose deity is Sūrya—

57.3.s: yady atra calate bhūmir nirghātolkāsta eva vā | aśarīrāś ca nardante kampante daivatāni ca ||
57.3.d: यद्य् अत्र चलते भूमिर् निर्घातोल्कास्त एव वा । अशरीराश् च नर्दन्ते कम्पन्ते दैवतानि च ॥
57.3.m: if the earth shakes here, or a crash of thunder and a meteor-fall [occur], / or bodiless beings roar, and the deities tremble,

57.3.s: ādityo vātra gṛhyeta somo vāpy uparajyate | vāruṇaṃ tad vijānīyāt subhikṣaṃ cātra nirdiśet ||
57.3.d: आदित्यो वात्र गृह्येत सोमो वाप्य् उपरज्यते । वारुणं तद् विजानीयात् सुभिक्षं चात्र निर्दिशेत् ॥
57.3.m: or if the sun is eclipsed here, or the moon is obscured, / one should recognize it as of Varuṇa, and one should predict abundance here.

57.3.s: bahukṣīrās tathā gāvo nāgāś ca phalinas tathā | śāntārayaḥ prajāḥ sarvā gomino jaṅgalaṃ payaḥ ||
57.3.d: बहुक्षीरास् तथा गावो नागाश् च फलिनस् तथा । शान्तारयः प्रजाः सर्वा गोमिनो जङ्गलं पयः ॥
57.3.m: Cows yield abundant milk, and trees bear fruit; / all people have their enemies pacified; cattle-owners [prosper, and] water [is plentiful even in] the wilderness.

57.3.s: jalopajīvinaḥ sarve prāpnuvanty ṛddhim uttamām | khecarāś cātra dṛśyante snigdhavarṇāḥ samantataḥ ||
57.3.d: जलोपजीविनः सर्वे प्राप्नुवन्त्य् ऋद्धिम् उत्तमाम् । खेचराश् चात्र दृश्यन्ते स्निग्धवर्णाः समन्ततः ॥
57.3.m: All those who live by water attain the highest prosperity; / and birds of glossy hue are seen on all sides.

57.3.s: nyastaśastrāś ca rājāno brahmakṣatraṃ ca vardhate | etai rūpais tu vijñeyaṃ vāruṇaṃ caladarśanam ||
57.3.d: न्यस्तशस्त्राश् च राजानो ब्रह्मक्षत्रं च वर्धते । एतै रूपैस् तु विज्ञेयं वारुणं चलदर्शनम् ॥
57.3.m: Kings lay down their weapons, and the priesthood and nobility flourish; / through these characteristics an earthquake of Varuṇa is to be recognized.

57.4.s: jyeṣṭhānurādhā śravaṇaḥ śraviṣṭhāś ca punarvasū | prājāpatyam āṣāḍhāś ca māhendraṃ maṇḍalaṃ smṛtam ||
57.4.d: ज्येष्ठानुराधा श्रवणः श्रविष्ठाश् च पुनर्वसू । प्राजापत्यम् आषाढाश् च माहेन्द्रं मण्डलं स्मृतम् ॥
57.4.m: Jyeṣṭhā, Anurādhā, Śravaṇa, Śraviṣṭhā, Punarvasu, / the [lunar mansion] of Prajāpati, and the Aṣāḍhās are known as the circle of Mahendra.

57.4.s: yady atra calate bhūmir nirghātolkāsta eva vā | aśarīrāś ca nardante kampante daivatāni ca ||
57.4.d: यद्य् अत्र चलते भूमिर् निर्घातोल्कास्त एव वा । अशरीराश् च नर्दन्ते कम्पन्ते दैवतानि च ॥
57.4.m: If the earth shakes here, or a crash of thunder and a meteor-fall [occur], / or bodiless beings roar, and the deities tremble,

57.4.s: ādityo vātra gṛhyeta somo vāpy uparajyate | māhendraṃ tad vijānīyāt sukṣemaṃ cātra nirdiśet ||
57.4.d: आदित्यो वात्र गृह्येत सोमो वाप्य् उपरज्यते । माहेन्द्रं तद् विजानीयात् सुक्षेमं चात्र निर्दिशेत् ॥
57.4.m: or if the sun is eclipsed here, or the moon is obscured, / one should recognize it as of Mahendra, and one should predict peace and security here.

57.4.s: gāvaḥ samagravatsāś ca striyaḥ putrasamanvitāḥ | kīṭā vyālā mriyante ca ye cānye svedajantavaḥ ||
57.4.d: गावः समग्रवत्साश् च स्त्रियः पुत्रसमन्विताः । कीटा व्याला म्रियन्ते च ये चान्ये स्वेदजन्तवः ॥
57.4.m: Cows have all their calves, and women are endowed with sons; / insects, predators, and whatever other creatures born of sweat die.

57.4.s: vedādhyayanayajñeṣu brāhmaṇā niratāḥ sadā | viṭkṣatriyāḥ svakarmāṇaḥ śūdrāḥ śuśrūṣakārakāḥ ||
57.4.d: वेदाध्ययनयज्ञेषु ब्राह्मणा निरताः सदा । विट्क्षत्रियाः स्वकर्माणः शूद्राः शुश्रूषकारकाः ॥
57.4.m: Brahmins are constantly devoted to Veda-study and sacrifices; / commoners and warriors perform their own duties; Śūdras render service.

57.4.s: viṃśatiśataṃ tv āgneyaṃ vāyavyaṃ navatiṃ calet | aśītiṃ calate tv aindraṃ vāruṇaṃ saptatiṃ calet ||
57.4.d: विंशतिशतं त्व् आग्नेयं वायव्यं नवतिं चलेत् । अशीतिं चलते त्व् ऐन्द्रं वारुणं सप्ततिं चलेत् ॥
57.4.m: The [circle] of Agni shakes for one hundred and twenty [yojanas]; that of Vāyu shakes for ninety; / that of Indra shakes for eighty; that of Varuṇa shakes for seventy.

57.4.s: āgneyo bhūmikampo yaḥ sa dvimāsād vipacyate | vāruṇas tu phalaṃ sadyo vāyavyas tu trimāsikaḥ || māhendrasya phalaṃ vidyān māsam ardhaṃ tathaiva ca ||
57.4.d: आग्नेयो भूमिकम्पो यः स द्विमासाद् विपच्यते । वारुणस् तु फलं सद्यो वायव्यस् तु त्रिमासिकः ॥ माहेन्द्रस्य फलं विद्यान् मासम् अर्धं तथैव च ॥
57.4.m: The earthquake of Agni comes to fruition after two months; / that of Varuṇa yields fruit immediately; that of Vāyu takes three months; / one should know the fruit of Mahendra's [earthquake to take] a month and a half.

58.1.s: om ata ūrdhvaṃ ca digdāhān kīrtyamānān nibodhata | yathā diśaḥ pradahyante tāsāṃ dāhaphalaṃ ca yat ||
58.1.d: ओम् अत ऊर्ध्वं च दिग्दाहान् कीर्त्यमानान् निबोधत । यथा दिशः प्रदह्यन्ते तासां दाहफलं च यत् ॥
58.1.m: Oṃ. Henceforth understand the conflagrations of the quarters being proclaimed, / how the quarters burn and what the result of their burning is.

58.1.s: indro 'gnir marutaś caiva pradahanti diśo daśa | śubhāśubhāya lokānāṃ kṛtāntenābhicoditāḥ ||
58.1.d: इन्द्रो ऽग्निर् मरुतश् चैव प्रदहन्ति दिशो दश । शुभाशुभाय लोकानां कृतान्तेनाभिचोदिताः ॥
58.1.m: Indra, Agni, and the Maruts burn the ten quarters / for the good and bad of the worlds, impelled by Destiny.

58.1.s: yadāstamita āditye vahner jvālā pradṛśyate | diśāṃ dāhaṃ tu tad vidyād bhārgavasya vaco yathā ||
58.1.d: यदास्तमित आदित्ये वह्नेर् ज्वाला प्रदृश्यते । दिशां दाहं तु तद् विद्याद् भार्गवस्य वचो यथा ॥
58.1.m: When the sun has set, if a flame of fire is seen, / one should know that to be a burning of the quarters, according to the word of Bhārgava.

58.1.s: nānārāgasamutthānāṃ nānāvidhaphalodayāḥ | pāṃśuneva ca saṃchannā digdāhāyogam āśritāḥ ||
58.1.d: नानारागसमुत्थानां नानाविधफलोदयाः । पांशुनेव च संछन्ना दिग्दाहायोगम् आश्रिताः ॥
58.1.m: Arising in diverse hues, bearing various types of results, / [the quarters] covered as if with dust are subject to the unseasonable burning of the quarters.

58.1.s: diśaḥ sarvāḥ pradahyante akṣemāya phalāya ca | avadāhād ṛte dāhaṃ yadi snigdhāḥ pradarśanāḥ ||
58.1.d: दिशः सर्वाः प्रदह्यन्ते अक्षेमाय फलाय च । अवदाहाद् ऋते दाहं यदि स्निग्धाः प्रदर्शनाः ॥
58.1.m: All the quarters burn for an insecure result, / unless the appearance is lustrous without a scorching glow.

58.1.s: tamodhūmarajaskā ye dīptadvijamṛgāvṛtāḥ | pradīptalakṣaṇāḥ satyāḥ sarva evāhitāvahāḥ ||
58.1.d: तमोधूमरजस्का ये दीप्तद्विजमृगावृताः । प्रदीप्तलक्षणाः सत्याः सर्व एवाहितावहाः ॥
58.1.m: Those that possess darkness, smoke, and dust, [or] are accompanied by birds and beasts crying in inauspicious directions, / having the signs of blaze, are indeed all bringers of harm.

58.1.s: tathā kanakakiṃjalkataḍitkalpāḥ śivāś ca ye | rūkṣāḥ kṛṣṇātha māñjiṣṭhā bandhujīvakavac ca ye ||
58.1.d: तथा कनककिंजल्कतडित्कल्पाः शिवाश् च ये । रूक्षाः कृष्णाथ माञ्जिष्ठा बन्धुजीवकवच् च ये ॥
58.1.m: Likewise those resembling the filaments of gold or lightning are auspicious; / those that are rough, black, madder-colored, or like the Bandhujīvaka flower [are inauspicious].

58.1.s: śvetā raktāś ca pītāś ca dāhāḥ kṛṣṇāś ca varṇataḥ | brahmakṣatriyaviṭśūdravināśāya prakīrtitāḥ ||
58.1.d: श्वेता रक्ताश् च पीताश् च दाहाः कृष्णाश् च वर्णतः । ब्रह्मक्षत्रियविट्शूद्रविनाशाय प्रकीर्तिताः ॥
58.1.m: White, red, yellow, and black burnings by color / are proclaimed for the destruction of Brahmins, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, and Śūdras [respectively].

58.1.s: raktāḥ śastrabhayaṃ kuryur pītā vyādhiprakopanāḥ | agnivarṇās tathā kuryur agniśastrabhayaṃ mahat ||
58.1.d: रक्ताः शस्त्रभयं कुर्युर् पीता व्याधिप्रकोपनाः । अग्निवर्णास् तथा कुर्युर् अग्निशस्त्रभयं महत् ॥
58.1.m: Red ones cause fear of weapons; yellow ones provoke diseases; / fire-colored ones cause great danger from fire and weapons.

58.1.s: sapītaparuṣaśyāmā ye ca vāruṇasaṃnibhāḥ | sarva eva kṣudhārogamṛtyuśastrāgnikopanāḥ ||
58.1.d: सपीतपरुषश्यामा ये च वारुणसंनिभाः । सर्व एव क्षुधारोगमृत्युशस्त्राग्निकोपनाः ॥
58.1.m: Those that are yellowish, harsh, and dark, and those resembling Varuṇa's [color], / all provoke hunger, disease, death, weapons, and fire.

58.1.s: ṛtau tu varṣaṃ tīvraṃ syāt sainyavidravam eva ca | bhṛśam uddyotanī saṃdhyā kurute vā grahāgamam ||
58.1.d: ऋतौ तु वर्षं तीव्रं स्यात् सैन्यविद्रवम् एव च । भृशम् उद्द्योतनी संध्या कुरुते वा ग्रहागमम् ॥
58.1.m: In its season there would be fierce rain, and a rout of armies; / or an intensely glowing twilight causes the arrival of planets.

58.1.s: dikṣu dagdhāsu pīḍyante yathādig deśabhaktayaḥ | śakunajñānanirdiṣṭā ye ca tatrādhikārakāḥ ||
58.1.d: दिक्षु दग्धासु पीड्यन्ते यथादिग् देशभक्तयः । शकुनज्ञाननिर्दिष्टा ये च तत्राधिकारकाः ॥
58.1.m: When the quarters burn, the provincial divisions according to each quarter are afflicted, / as indicated by the science of portents, and whoever the rulers there are.

58.1.s: yathoktā tu mahāśāntir yathoktavidhinā kṛtā | sarvaṃ digdāhajaṃ ghoraṃ śamayet sā sadakṣiṇā ||
58.1.d: यथोक्ता तु महाशान्तिर् यथोक्तविधिना कृता । सर्वं दिग्दाहजं घोरं शमयेत् सा सदक्षिणा ॥
58.1.m: The great propitiatory rite, however, performed according to the prescribed rule as stated, / accompanied by a sacrificial fee, pacifies all that is terrible born of the burning of the quarters.

59.1.s: ata ūrdhvaṃ pravakṣyāmi vidyullakṣaṇam uttamam | varṇarūpavikārāṃś ca deśabhāgāñ śubhāśubhān ||
59.1.d: अत ऊर्ध्वं प्रवक्ष्यामि विद्युल्लक्षणम् उत्तमम् । वर्णरूपविकारांश् च देशभागाञ् शुभाशुभान् ॥
59.1.m: Next I will explain the supreme characteristic of lightning, / and the modifications of colour and form, and the regional directions, auspicious and inauspicious.

59.1.s: caturthīṃ pañcamīṃ caiva pratīkṣeta sadā śuciḥ | āṣāḍhaśuddhe niyataṃ vidyuddarśanam adbhutam ||
59.1.d: चतुर्थीं पञ्चमीं चैव प्रतीक्षेत सदा शुचिः । आषाढशुद्धे नियतं विद्युद्दर्शनम् अद्भुतम् ॥
59.1.m: Purified, one should always watch on the fourth and the fifth [tithi] / during the bright fortnight of Āṣāḍha for the portent of the appearance of lightning.

59.1.s: ativṛṣṭim anāvṛṣṭiṃ bhāvābhāvau tathaiva ca | sarvasasyeṣu niṣpattir vidyuto darśane naraḥ ||
59.1.d: अतिवृष्टिम् अनावृष्टिं भावाभावौ तथैव च । सर्वसस्येषु निष्पत्तिर् विद्युतो दर्शने नरः ॥
59.1.m: Excessive rain, drought, as well as plenty and scarcity, / and the yield among all crops, a man [discerns] at the appearance of lightning.

59.1.s: aindryāṃ cet syandate vidyud aindrasthaś cāpi mārutaḥ | subhikṣaṃ kṣemam ārogyaṃ nirītiṃ ca vinirdiśet ||
59.1.d: ऐन्द्र्यां चेत् स्यन्दते विद्युद् ऐन्द्रस्थश् चापि मारुतः । सुभिक्षं क्षेमम् आरोग्यं निरीतिं च विनिर्दिशेत् ॥
59.1.m: If lightning flashes in the east and the wind is also situated in the east, / one should predict abundance, security, health, and freedom from pests.

59.1.s: āgneyyāṃ ced ubhau syātāṃ bhayaṃ śastrāgnivṛṣṭihtaḥ | yāmyāyāṃ viṣamāriś ca vyādhimṛtyubhayaṃ tathā ||
59.1.d: आग्नेय्यां चेद् उभौ स्यातां भयं शस्त्राग्निवृष्टिह्तः । याम्यायां विषमारिश् च व्याधिमृत्युभयं तथा ॥
59.1.m: If both should occur in the south-east, there is fear from weapons, fire, and [heavy] rain; / in the south, a devastating plague as well as fear of disease and death.

59.1.s: kanīyasī tu nairṛtyāṃ tathā bahvītikā samā | madhyamā sasyasaṃpattir vāruṇyāṃ vyādhisaṃkulā ||
59.1.d: कनीयसी तु नैरृत्यां तथा बह्वीतिका समा । मध्यमा सस्यसंपत्तिर् वारुण्यां व्याधिसंकुला ॥
59.1.m: In the south-west, however, it is slight, and similarly a year of abundant pests; / in the west, a middling yield of crops, fraught with diseases.

59.1.s: pataṃgadaṃśamaśakā vāyavyāṃ madhyasapadaḥ | ativāribhayaṃ vidyāt saumyāyāṃ bhūrisaṃpadaḥ ||
59.1.d: पतंगदंशमशका वायव्यां मध्यसपदः । अतिवारिभयं विद्यात् सौम्यायां भूरिसंपदः ॥
59.1.m: In the north-west, locusts, gadflies, and mosquitoes, with middling prosperity; / in the north, one should know there is fear of excessive water, [yet] abundant fortunes.

59.1.s: nirītiḥ sasyasaṃpat tu pradhānāiśyāṃ manoramā | pratilomeṣu vāteṣu ītibāhulyam ādiśet ||
59.1.d: निरीतिः सस्यसंपत् तु प्रधानाइश्यां मनोरमा । प्रतिलोमेषु वातेषु ईतिबाहुल्यम् आदिशेत् ॥
59.1.m: In the north-east, freedom from pests and excellent, delightful crop yields [ensue]; / when winds blow contrariwise, one should predict an abundance of pests.

59.1.s: anulomeṣu vāteṣu nirītiṃ tu samādiśet | śubhāyāṃ syandamānāyām aniṣṭā syandate yadi ||
59.1.d: अनुलोमेषु वातेषु निरीतिं तु समादिशेत् । शुभायां स्यन्दमानायाम् अनिष्टा स्यन्दते यदि ॥
59.1.m: When winds blow favorably, however, one should predict freedom from pests. / When an auspicious [flash] is running, if an inauspicious one flashes,

59.1.s: saṃpadyate mahāsasyān mahāṃś cet syād avagrahaḥ | aśubhā syandate pūrvaṃ yadi paścāc ca śobhanā ||
59.1.d: संपद्यते महासस्यान् महांश् चेत् स्याद् अवग्रहः । अशुभा स्यन्दते पूर्वं यदि पश्चाच् च शोभना ॥
59.1.m: a great crop is produced, even if there should be a great drought. / If an inauspicious [flash] runs first and afterwards an auspicious one,

59.1.s: suvṛṣṭim eva tatrāhur na ca sasyaṃ samṛdhyati | yadā tu sarvāḥ syandante viṣamāṃ vṛṣṭim ādiśet ||
59.1.d: सुवृष्टिम् एव तत्राहुर् न च सस्यं समृध्यति । यदा तु सर्वाः स्यन्दन्ते विषमां वृष्टिम् आदिशेत् ॥
59.1.m: they say there will indeed be good rain, but the crop does not prosper. / But when all flash together, one should predict uneven rain.

59.1.s: bahulāyāṃ vidyuti tu bahuvāribhayaṃ bhavet | savidyutaḥ sastanito darśayanti yadā śubhām ||
59.1.d: बहुलायां विद्युति तु बहुवारिभयं भवेत् । सविद्युतः सस्तनितो दर्शयन्ति यदा शुभाम् ॥
59.1.m: When lightning is abundant, however, there would be fear of excessive water. / When clouds with lightning and with thunder show an auspicious [form]

59.1.s: pūrvottarāṃ diśaṃ meghāḥ suvṛṣṭiṃ tāṃ vijānate | pūrvataḥ pūrvavarṣeṣu dṛśyante yadi toyadāḥ ||
59.1.d: पूर्वोत्तरां दिशं मेघाः सुवृष्टिं तां विजानते । पूर्वतः पूर्ववर्षेषु दृश्यन्ते यदि तोयदाः ॥
59.1.m: in the north-eastern direction, they recognize that as good rain. / If rain-clouds are seen in the east during the early rains,

59.1.s: pradakṣiṇāvartaśubhāḥ suvṛṣṭim iti nirdiśet | āgneyeṣv ativṛṣṭiḥ syāt sasyaṃ cāpi vipadyate ||
59.1.d: प्रदक्षिणावर्तशुभाः सुवृष्टिम् इति निर्दिशेत् । आग्नेयेष्व् अतिवृष्टिः स्यात् सस्यं चापि विपद्यते ॥
59.1.m: turning clockwise and auspicious, one should indicate good rain. / In the south-east there would be excessive rain, and the crop also perishes.

59.1.s: viṣamā vṛṣṭir yāmyeṣu vyādhiṃ mṛtyuṃ ca nirdiśet | bahvītikā nairṛteṣu samūlaphaladāyinī ||
59.1.d: विषमा वृष्टिर् याम्येषु व्याधिं मृत्युं च निर्दिशेत् । बह्वीतिका नैरृतेषु समूलफलदायिनी ॥
59.1.m: Uneven rain in the south, and one should indicate disease and death. / In the south-west, abundant pests, [though] yielding fruits together with roots.

59.1.s: vāruṇeṣu payodeṣu madhyamaṃ sasyam ādiśet | vāyavyāṃ prathamaṃ varṣaṃ yatra varṣati vāsavaḥ ||
59.1.d: वारुणेषु पयोदेषु मध्यमं सस्यम् आदिशेत् । वायव्यां प्रथमं वर्षं यत्र वर्षति वासवः ॥
59.1.m: When rain-clouds are in the west, one should predict a middling crop. / When Indra rains the first rain in the north-west,

59.1.s: tatrātivṛṣṭir bhavati svalpabījāni vāpayet | varṇasnebhopapannās tu pūrvavṛṣṭyāṃ payodharāḥ ||
59.1.d: तत्रातिवृष्टिर् भवति स्वल्पबीजानि वापयेत् । वर्णस्नेभोपपन्नास् तु पूर्ववृष्ट्यां पयोधराः ॥
59.1.m: excessive rain occurs there; one should sow only a few seeds. / But rain-clouds endowed with [proper] colour and glossiness during the first rain,

59.1.s: saumyāṃ yatra pravarṣeyus tatra sarvavṛṣṭyāṃ payodharāḥ ||
59.1.d: सौम्यां यत्र प्रवर्षेयुस् तत्र सर्ववृष्ट्यां पयोधराः ॥
59.1.m: wherever they might pour down rain in the north, there rain-clouds [bring] total rain.

59.1.s: ity etat pūrvavarṣeṣu lakṣaṇaṃ vidyutāṃ sphuṭam | varṣārāvagataṃ sarvaṃ yathāvat parikīrtitam ||
59.1.d: इत्य् एतत् पूर्ववर्षेषु लक्षणं विद्युतां स्फुटम् । वर्षारावगतं सर्वं यथावत् परिकीर्तितम् ॥
59.1.m: Thus this distinct characteristic of lightning during the early rains, / and everything perceived through the sound of rain, has been properly proclaimed.

59.1.s: śubheṣv api mahāśāntir avighātāya vocyate | aśubheṣu samarghāya tasmāt sarveṣu śāntikam iti ||
59.1.d: शुभेष्व् अपि महाशान्तिर् अविघाताय वोच्यते । अशुभेषु समर्घाय तस्मात् सर्वेषु शान्तिकम् इति ॥
59.1.m: A great propitiatory rite is prescribed even for auspicious ones to prevent hindrance, / and for inauspicious ones to secure cheap prices; therefore an apotropaic rite is [performed] for all.

60.1.s: aṣṭau bhavanti nirghātās teṣām indraḥ praśasyate | pūrveṇa vṛṣṭiṃ sasyaṃ ca rājavṛddhiṃ ca nirdiśet ||
60.1.d: अष्टौ भवन्ति निर्घातास् तेषाम् इन्द्रः प्रशस्यते । पूर्वेण वृष्टिं सस्यं च राजवृद्धिं च निर्दिशेत् ॥
60.1.m: There are eight thunderclaps; of them Indra's is praised. / By one in the east, one should predict rain, crops, and the increase of the king.

60.1.s: pūrvottare subhikṣaṃ tu bhūmilābhas tathottare | aparottare caurabhayaṃ vājināṃ cāpy upadravaḥ ||
60.1.d: पूर्वोत्तरे सुभिक्षं तु भूमिलाभस् तथोत्तरे । अपरोत्तरे चौरभयं वाजिनां चाप्य् उपद्रवः ॥
60.1.m: In the north-east, abundance of food, and acquisition of land in the north; / in the north-west, fear of thieves and affliction of horses.

60.1.s: paścimāyāṃ bhayaṃ rājño jalajātiś ca pīḍyate | nairṛte sasyagostrīṇāṃ gaṇānāṃ ca mahad bhayam ||
60.1.d: पश्चिमायां भयं राज्ञो जलजातिश् च पीड्यते । नैरृते सस्यगोस्त्रीणां गणानां च महद् भयम् ॥
60.1.m: In the west, danger to the king, and the class of aquatic creatures is afflicted; / in the south-west, great fear for crops, cows, women, and troops.

60.1.s: dakṣiṇe rājapīḍā syād āyuś cātra vinirdiśet | ānartasya bhayaṃ vidyād yadi syāt pūrvadakṣiṇaḥ ||
60.1.d: दक्षिणे राजपीडा स्याद् आयुश् चात्र विनिर्दिशेत् । आनर्तस्य भयं विद्याद् यदि स्यात् पूर्वदक्षिणः ॥
60.1.m: In the south, there would be affliction to the king, and here one should predict [loss of] life; / one should know fear for Ānarta if it should be in the south-east.

60.1.s: sa yojanaparaḥ śabdo nirghātasya viśāmyati | sarvatra ca bhayaṃ vidyāt tatra yatra viśāmyati ||
60.1.d: स योजनपरः शब्दो निर्घातस्य विशाम्यति । सर्वत्र च भयं विद्यात् तत्र यत्र विशाम्यति ॥
60.1.m: That sound of a thunderclap dies down over a yojana; / and one should know fear everywhere where it dies down.

60.1.s: bhaye raudrīṃ prakurvīta abhayāṃ vābhayapradām | tayā śāmyanti cotpātāḥ sukhaṃ cātyantikaṃ bhavet ||
60.1.d: भये रौद्रीं प्रकुर्वीत अभयां वाभयप्रदाम् । तया शाम्यन्ति चोत्पाताः सुखं चात्यन्तिकं भवेत् ॥
60.1.m: In case of danger, one should perform the raudrī [rite] or the abhayā, which confers safety; / by that, portents are pacified and endless happiness will ensue.

61.1.s: om athātaḥ pariveṣāṇāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ caiva vakṣyate | vṛddhagargo yathā pūrvam uvāca mama suvrata ||
61.1.d: ओम् अथातः परिवेषाणां लक्षणं चैव वक्ष्यते । वृद्धगर्गो यथा पूर्वम् उवाच मम सुव्रत ॥
61.1.m: Oṃ. Now then, the characteristic of halos will be explained, / just as Vṛddhagarga spoke to me of old, O you of good vows.

61.1.s: svāyaṃbhuvaniyogena vikāraṃ kurute 'malaḥ ||
61.1.d: स्वायंभुवनियोगेन विकारं कुरुते ऽमलः ॥
61.1.m: By command of the Self-born, the spotless [sky] undergoes modification.

61.1.s: śvetaḥ śyāmo hariḥ kṛṣṇa iti varṇā vyavasthitāḥ | proktā megheṣu catvāro vyaktāḥ snigdhāḥ supūjitāḥ ||
61.1.d: श्वेतः श्यामो हरिः कृष्ण इति वर्णा व्यवस्थिताः । प्रोक्ता मेघेषु चत्वारो व्यक्ताः स्निग्धाः सुपूजिताः ॥
61.1.m: White, grey, greenish-yellow, and black: these are established as the four colors / proclaimed in clouds; clear and glossy, they are highly regarded.

61.1.s: snigdheṣu pariveṣeṣu vaturṣv eteṣu nārada | saṃdhyāyām atra varṇeṣu vṛṣṭiṃ teṣv abhinirdiśet ||
61.1.d: स्निग्धेषु परिवेषेषु वतुर्ष्व् एतेषु नारद । संध्यायाम् अत्र वर्णेषु वृष्टिं तेष्व् अभिनिर्दिशेत् ॥
61.1.m: Among glossy halos in these four colors at twilight, O Nārada, / in those one should declare rain.

61.1.s: kācanīlāñjanāriṣṭāśanisarpanibheṣu ca | raupyadravasamābheṣu meghas triṣv api varṣati ||
61.1.d: काचनीलाञ्जनारिष्टाशनिसर्पनिभेषु च । रौप्यद्रवसमाभेषु मेघस् त्रिष्व् अपि वर्षति ॥
61.1.m: And when resembling glass, sapphire, collyrium, soapberry, a thunderbolt, and a snake, / or having an appearance like molten silver, the cloud rains even during the three [twilights].

61.1.s: nimagnā tu yadā saṃdhyā bhavaty etat suvṛṣṭaye | ebhyaś ca viparītā ye te 'vṛṣṭibhayadā ghanāḥ ||
61.1.d: निमग्ना तु यदा संध्या भवत्य् एतत् सुवृष्टये । एभ्यश् च विपरीता ये ते ऽवृष्टिभयदा घनाः ॥
61.1.m: When, however, twilight is submerged, this leads to good rain; / and those clouds which are contrary to these bring the fear of drought.

61.1.s: varāhair makarair uṣṭrair vṛkaiḥ kaṅkais tathā kharaiḥ | śaśakākṛtayaḥ kuryuḥ saṃdhyāyāṃ jaladā bhayam ||
61.1.d: वराहैर् मकरैर् उष्ट्रैर् वृकैः कङ्कैस् तथा खरैः । शशकाकृतयः कुर्युः संध्यायां जलदा भयम् ॥
61.1.m: Having the forms of boars, crocodiles, camels, wolves, herons, and donkeys, / or resembling hares, clouds at twilight would produce fear,

61.1.s: hemapāvakavarṇāś ca vipulaṃ ca janakṣayam | śabdaṃ śvakharagomāyugṛdhravāyasasaṃsthitāḥ ||
61.1.d: हेमपावकवर्णाश् च विपुलं च जनक्षयम् । शब्दं श्वखरगोमायुगृध्रवायससंस्थिताः ॥
61.1.m: and those colored like gold and fire [produce] extensive destruction of people. / Standing in the forms of dogs, donkeys, jackals, vultures, and crows, making sound,

61.1.s: pūrvāparāsu saṃdhyāsu saṃgrāmaṃ prāhur unmukhāḥ | aśvasthā vāraṇasthāś ca yeṣu yodhā narā iva ||
61.1.d: पूर्वापरासु संध्यासु संग्रामं प्राहुर् उन्मुखाः । अश्वस्था वारणस्थाश् च येषु योधा नरा इव ॥
61.1.m: facing upwards at the morning and evening twilights, they foretell war. / Clouds in which warriors resembling men, mounted on horses and mounted on elephants,

61.1.s: megheṣu saṃpradṛśyante ye pāśāṅkuśasaṃnibhāḥ | tathā savāraṇāś caiva vinighnantaḥ parasparam ||
61.1.d: मेघेषु संप्रदृश्यन्ते ये पाशाङ्कुशसंनिभाः । तथा सवारणाश् चैव विनिघ्नन्तः परस्परम् ॥
61.1.m: are seen, resembling nooses and goads, / and likewise with elephants, striking each other,

61.1.s: kravyādbhir bhakṣyamāṇāś ca gṛdhragomāyuvāyasaiḥ | udyudhyante yadā yuktā rāñjaḥ saṃśayakārakāḥ ||
61.1.d: क्रव्याद्भिर् भक्ष्यमाणाश् च गृध्रगोमायुवायसैः । उद्युध्यन्ते यदा युक्ता राञ्जः संशयकारकाः ॥
61.1.m: and being devoured by flesh-eaters—vultures, jackals, and crows— / when joined together they battle, causing jeopardy to the king.

61.1.s: mayūrāṭṭālapadmendukāśanīlanibhāni tu | saṃdhyāsv abhrāṇi dṛśyante tīvraṃ varṣam upasthitam ||
61.1.d: मयूराट्टालपद्मेन्दुकाशनीलनिभानि तु । संध्यास्व् अभ्राणि दृश्यन्ते तीव्रं वर्षम् उपस्थितम् ॥
61.1.m: Clouds resembling a peacock, a watchtower, a lotus, the moon, a reed, or sapphire, / when seen at the twilights, heavy rain is at hand.

61.1.s: savidyut sadhanuṣkaś ca saghoṣaḥ śikhisaṃnibhaḥ | saṃdhyāsv abhrāṇi dṛśyante tīvraṃ varṣam upasthitam ||
61.1.d: सविद्युत् सधनुष्कश् च सघोषः शिखिसंनिभः । संध्यास्व् अभ्राणि दृश्यन्ते तीव्रं वर्षम् उपस्थितम् ॥
61.1.m: Accompanied by lightning, with a rainbow, with rumbling, and resembling a peacock's crest, / when clouds are seen at the twilights, heavy rain is at hand.

61.1.s: nīlalohitaparyantaṃ kṛṣṇagrīvaṃ savidyutam | vivarṇaṃ parighaṃ dṛṣṭvā vidyād udakavāhakam ||
61.1.d: नीललोहितपर्यन्तं कृष्णग्रीवं सविद्युतम् । विवर्णं परिघं दृष्ट्वा विद्याद् उदकवाहकम् ॥
61.1.m: Having blue and red rims, a dark neck, accompanied by lightning, / having seen a discolored parigha-cloud, one should know it as a water-bearer.

61.1.s: trivarṇe parighe vāpi trivarṇair vā balāhakaiḥ | udayāstamayam iyād yadi sūryaḥ kadā cana ||
61.1.d: त्रिवर्णे परिघे वापि त्रिवर्णैर् वा बलाहकैः । उदयास्तमयम् इयाद् यदि सूर्यः कदा चन ॥
61.1.m: Whether in a three-colored parigha-cloud or with three-colored clouds, / if the sun should ever go to rising or setting,

61.1.s: pṛthivyāṃ rājavaṃśyānāṃ mahad bhayam upasthitam | lokakṣayakaraṃ vidyād yadi devo na varṣati ||
61.1.d: पृथिव्यां राजवंश्यानां महद् भयम् उपस्थितम् । लोकक्षयकरं विद्याद् यदि देवो न वर्षति ॥
61.1.m: great danger has befallen members of royal lineages on earth; / one should know it to cause the destruction of the world, if the god does not rain.

61.1.s: matsyarūpī sādṛśyena yady uttiṣṭheta bhāskaraḥ | sphuṭaraśmis tadādityaḥ sa nirdahati medinīm ||
61.1.d: मत्स्यरूपी सादृश्येन यद्य् उत्तिष्ठेत भास्करः । स्फुटरश्मिस् तदादित्यः स निर्दहति मेदिनीम् ॥
61.1.m: If the sun should rise in the likeness of the form of a fish, / with radiant rays, then the sun scorches the earth.

61.1.s: etad dṛṣṭvā mahad rūpam āditye samupasthite | vispaṣṭaṃ jyotir vispaṣṭaṃ sadyovarṣasya lakṣaṇam ||
61.1.d: एतद् दृष्ट्वा महद् रूपम् आदित्ये समुपस्थिते । विस्पष्टं ज्योतिर् विस्पष्टं सद्योवर्षस्य लक्षणम् ॥
61.1.m: Having seen this great form when the sun has appeared, / distinct luminescence is the characteristic of immediate rain.

61.1.s: grahasaṃchādanaṃ cāpi garjanaṃ pratigarjanam | paraspareṇa kurvanti meghā vegasamīritāḥ ||
61.1.d: ग्रहसंछादनं चापि गर्जनं प्रतिगर्जनम् । परस्परेण कुर्वन्ति मेघा वेगसमीरिताः ॥
61.1.m: Covering the planets, and roaring and counter-roaring, / clouds driven by violent wind produce against one another.

61.1.s: tasmiṃś caturvidhe yuddhe meghānāṃ vyomacārinām | utpadyante trayo bhāvās tan me nigadataḥ śṛṇu ||
61.1.d: तस्मिंश् चतुर्विधे युद्धे मेघानां व्योमचारिनाम् । उत्पद्यन्ते त्रयो भावास् तन् मे निगदतः शृणु ॥
61.1.m: In that fourfold battle of clouds wandering in the sky, / three conditions arise; hear that from me as I speak.

61.1.s: garjamāneṣu megheṣu vāraṇaḥ pratigarjati | tāṃ diśaṃ yojayet snenāṃ garjanaṃ yatra mīyate ||
61.1.d: गर्जमानेषु मेघेषु वारणः प्रतिगर्जति । तां दिशं योजयेत् स्नेनां गर्जनं यत्र मीयते ॥
61.1.m: While the clouds are roaring, an elephant roars in response; / one should deploy the army in that direction where the roaring is measured.

61.1.s: vidyuto 'bhravikāreṣu śakrāyudhanibhāyudhāḥ | sphoṭitāśanighaṇṭāś ca yāṃ diśaṃ meghavāraṇāḥ ||
61.1.d: विद्युतो ऽभ्रविकारेषु शक्रायुधनिभायुधाः । स्फोटिताशनिघण्टाश् च यां दिशं मेघवारणाः ॥
61.1.m: In the transformations of the clouds, lightnings have weapons resembling Indra's weapon, / and when the cloud-elephants have ringing thunderbolt-bells in whichever direction,

61.1.s: saṃghaṭṭeṣu samudbhutāḥ parasparajighāṃsavaḥ | tāṃ diśaṃ yojayet senāṃ rājā jayati tāṃ diśam ||
61.1.d: संघट्टेषु समुद्भुताः परस्परजिघांसवः । तां दिशं योजयेत् सेनां राजा जयति तां दिशम् ॥
61.1.m: born in collisions, seeking to slay one another, / into that direction let the king send his army; he conquers that direction.

61.1.s: grahaṇāchādane caiva garjane pratigarjane | evam eva vidhir jñeyaḥ sarvaś caiva viniścayaḥ ||
61.1.d: ग्रहणाछादने चैव गर्जने प्रतिगर्जने । एवम् एव विधिर् ज्ञेयः सर्वश् चैव विनिश्चयः ॥
61.1.m: In eclipse, covering, thunder, and counter-thunder, / just so is the rule to be understood, and every determination.

61.1.s: parimāṇaṃ na śakyaṃ tat samīritum aśeṣataḥ | aparābhravikārāṇāṃ ratnānām iva sāgare ||
61.1.d: परिमाणं न शक्यं तत् समीरितुम् अशेषतः । अपराभ्रविकाराणां रत्नानाम् इव सागरे ॥
61.1.m: It is impossible to declare fully that extent / of other cloud-transformations, as of jewels in the ocean.

61.1.s: saṃdhyā yojanabhāk proktā stanitaṃ tu dviyojanam | parighaḥ pañcayojanyaḥ pratyādityas triyojanaḥ ||
61.1.d: संध्या योजनभाक् प्रोक्ता स्तनितं तु द्वियोजनम् । परिघः पञ्चयोजन्यः प्रत्यादित्यस् त्रियोजनः ॥
61.1.m: Twilight is declared to extend one yojana, but rumbling two yojanas; / a crossbar cloud extends five yojanas, a mock sun three yojanas,

61.1.s: nirghātaḥ ṣaṭ tathā vidyut pariveṣo dviṣaḍyataḥ | dāhaṃ yojanakaṃ cāpi ulkā tv amitabhāginī ||
61.1.d: निर्घातः षट् तथा विद्युत् परिवेषो द्विषड्यतः । दाहं योजनकं चापि उल्का त्व् अमितभागिनी ॥
61.1.m: a thunderclap likewise six, a lightning-flash [and] a halo extend twelve; / sky-glow extends one yojana, while a meteor has an unmeasured range.

61.1.s: daśasaṃsthā samāptāni śāyāṅgāni pramāṇataḥ | aṅgāni tv āntarikṣāṇi vijñeyāni samāsataḥ ||
61.1.d: दशसंस्था समाप्तानि शायाङ्गानि प्रमाणतः । अङ्गानि त्व् आन्तरिक्षाणि विज्ञेयानि समासतः ॥
61.1.m: These aerial members, consisting of ten constituents, are concluded according to their measure; / the atmospheric limbs are to be understood in brief.

62.1.s: oṃ catvāro bhumikampās tu gargaḥ provāca buddhimān | agnir vāyus tathāpaś ca caturthas tv indra ucyate ||
62.1.d: ओं चत्वारो भुमिकम्पास् तु गर्गः प्रोवाच बुद्धिमान् । अग्निर् वायुस् तथापश् च चतुर्थस् त्व् इन्द्र उच्यते ॥
62.1.m: Om. Wise Garga spoke of four earthquakes: / Fire, Wind, and Water, and the fourth is called Indra's.

62.1.s: teṣāṃ rūpaṃ vikārāṃś ca vyākhyāsyāmo 'nupūrvaśaḥ | yaj jñātvā buddhimān dhīro nirdiśed vividhaṃ phalam ||
62.1.d: तेषां रूपं विकारांश् च व्याख्यास्यामो ऽनुपूर्वशः । यज् ज्ञात्वा बुद्धिमान् धीरो निर्दिशेद् विविधं फलम् ॥
62.1.m: We shall explain their appearance and modifications in regular order, / knowing which a wise and steadfast man may predict varied results.

62.1.s: prakampitāyāṃ bhūmau cet saptāhābhyantareṇā tu | bhaveyur atra saṃgrāmā rājñāṃ mṛtyubhayapradāḥ ||
62.1.d: प्रकम्पितायां भूमौ चेत् सप्ताहाभ्यन्तरेणा तु । भवेयुर् अत्र संग्रामा राज्ञां मृत्युभयप्रदाः ॥
62.1.m: If, when the earth is shaken, within seven days / [there should be wars here bringing danger of death to kings,

62.1.s: rājñāṃ virodho bhavati maraṇāni bhavanti ca | tāmraḥ sūryaś ca candraś ca pītāś ca mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ ||
62.1.d: राज्ञां विरोधो भवति मरणानि भवन्ति च । ताम्रः सूर्यश् च चन्द्रश् च पीताश् च मृगपक्षिणः ॥
62.1.m: there is conflict among kings, and deaths occur;] / and the sun and moon are copper-colored, and the beasts and birds are yellow,

62.1.s: diśaḥ sarvā bhaveyuś ca sūryodayasamaprabhāḥ | yad etallakṣaṇopetaṃ vidyād agniprakampitam ||
62.1.d: दिशः सर्वा भवेयुश् च सूर्योदयसमप्रभाः । यद् एतल्लक्षणोपेतं विद्याद् अग्निप्रकम्पितम् ॥
62.1.m: and all the directions should be equal in radiance to sunrise— / one endowed with these characteristics one should know as shaken by Fire.

62.1.s: tasmin bhavati nirdeśaḥ śaunakasya vaco yathā | hiraṇyaṃ ca suvarṇaṃ ca yac cānyad vidyate gṛhe ||
62.1.d: तस्मिन् भवति निर्देशः शौनकस्य वचो यथा । हिरण्यं च सुवर्णं च यच् चान्यद् विद्यते गृहे ॥
62.1.m: Regarding that, there is an instruction according to the words of Śaunaka: / gold, fine gold, and whatever else is found in the house—

62.1.s: sarvam etat parityajya kartavyo dhānyasaṃgrahaḥ | rāṣṭrāṇi saṃdahed agnir grāmāṃś ca nagarāṇi ca
62.1.d: सर्वम् एतत् परित्यज्य कर्तव्यो धान्यसंग्रहः । राष्ट्राणि संदहेद् अग्निर् ग्रामांश् च नगराणि च
62.1.m: abandoning all of this, an accumulation of grain must be made. / Fire may burn the kingdoms, the villages, and the cities,

62.1.s: saṃgrāmāś cātra vartante māṃsaśoṇitakardamāḥ | rājānaś ca virudhyante devaś cātra na varṣati ||
62.1.d: संग्रामाश् चात्र वर्तन्ते मांसशोणितकर्दमाः । राजानश् च विरुध्यन्ते देवश् चात्र न वर्षति ॥
62.1.m: and wars occur here, muddy with flesh and blood; / kings come into conflict, and the god does not rain here.
Thus of these earthquakes, the fire-quake is condemned.

62.2.m: “If, when the earth is shaken...” [is repeated for the next].

62.2.s: atipracaṇḍo bahulo vāyur bhavati dāruṇaḥ | śarkarākarṣaṇaś cāpi dikṣu caiva vidikṣu ca ||
62.2.d: अतिप्रचण्डो बहुलो वायुर् भवति दारुणः । शर्कराकर्षणश् चापि दिक्षु चैव विदिक्षु च ॥
62.2.m: A wind becomes exceedingly fierce, dense, and dreadful, / dragging gravel, both in the cardinal and intermediate directions.

62.2.s: tad etallakṣaṇopetaṃ vidyād vāyuprakampitam | śastrair āvaraṇaṃkuryāt prākāraṃ parikhāṃ tathā ||
62.2.d: तद् एतल्लक्षणोपेतं विद्याद् वायुप्रकम्पितम् । शस्त्रैर् आवरणंकुर्यात् प्राकारं परिखां तथा ॥
62.2.m: One endowed with this characteristic one should know as shaken by Wind. / One should make a protection with weapons, a rampart, and a moat;

62.2.s: na tadā pravased grāmaṃ jñātvātmānaṃ tu gopayet | saṃgrāmāś cātra vardhante māṃsaśoṇitakardamāḥ ||
62.2.d: न तदा प्रवसेद् ग्रामं ज्ञात्वात्मानं तु गोपयेत् । संग्रामाश् चात्र वर्धन्ते मांसशोणितकर्दमाः ॥
62.2.m: one should not then depart from the village, but knowing [the danger] protect oneself. / And here wars increase, muddy with flesh and blood,

62.2.s: virudhyante ca rājāno maraṇāni bhavanti hi | rājaputrasahastrāṇāṃ bhūmiḥ pibati śoṇitam ||
62.2.d: विरुध्यन्ते च राजानो मरणानि भवन्ति हि । राजपुत्रसहस्त्राणां भूमिः पिबति शोणितम् ॥
62.2.m: kings come into conflict, and deaths indeed occur; / the earth drinks the blood of thousands of princes.

62.2.s: māsaṃ viṃśatirātraṃ vā devas tatra na varṣati | dvābhyāṃ gatābhyāṃ māsābhyāṃ paraṃ syād bahulaṃ jalam ||
62.2.d: मासं विंशतिरात्रं वा देवस् तत्र न वर्षति । द्वाभ्यां गताभ्यां मासाभ्यां परं स्याद् बहुलं जलम् ॥
62.2.m: For a month or twenty nights the god does not rain there; / after two months have passed, there would subsequently be abundant water.

62.2.s: daṣṭaṃ dūṣayate cātra kṣatabaddhāni cādhikam | eṣām eva tu kampānāṃ garhitaṃ vāyukampitam ||
62.2.d: दष्टं दूषयते चात्र क्षतबद्धानि चाधिकम् । एषाम् एव तु कम्पानां गर्हितं वायुकम्पितम् ॥
62.2.m: And here a bite becomes corrupt, and bound wounds [fester] excessively; / indeed of these earthquakes, the wind-quake is condemned.

62.3.s: varṣantas tu samāyānti mahāmeghāḥ samantataḥ | nakrāś ca śiśumārāś ca kūrmā makarasaṃsthitāḥ ||
62.3.d: वर्षन्तस् तु समायान्ति महामेघाः समन्ततः । नक्राश् च शिशुमाराश् च कूर्मा मकरसंस्थिताः ॥
62.3.m: Great raining clouds approach from all sides; / crocodiles, porpoises, and turtles situated on sea-monsters

62.3.s: abhrākṛtiṣu dṛśyante grasantaś candrabhāskarau | tad etallakṣaṇopetaṃ vidyād ambuprakampitam ||
62.3.d: अभ्राकृतिषु दृश्यन्ते ग्रसन्तश् चन्द्रभास्करौ । तद् एतल्लक्षणोपेतं विद्याद् अम्बुप्रकम्पितम् ॥
62.3.m: are seen in the cloud-shapes, swallowing the sun and the moon. / One endowed with this characteristic one should know as shaken by Water.

62.3.s: parvateṣu vaped bījam ūṣare jāṅgale tathā | tatroptaṃ nandate bījam anyatra bhuvi naśyati ||
62.3.d: पर्वतेषु वपेद् बीजम् ऊषरे जाङ्गले तथा । तत्रोप्तं नन्दते बीजम् अन्यत्र भुवि नश्यति ॥
62.3.m: One should sow seed on mountains, in saline soil, and in arid land; / seed sown there thrives, [while] elsewhere on earth it perishes.

62.3.s: udajāni tu puṣpāṇi mūlāni ca phalāni ca | gacchanti tatra vṛddhiṃ ca sattvāny udakajāni ca ||
62.3.d: उदजानि तु पुष्पाणि मूलानि च फलानि च । गच्छन्ति तत्र वृद्धिं च सत्त्वान्य् उदकजानि च ॥
62.3.m: Water-born flowers, roots, and fruits, / and water-born creatures attain growth there.

62.3.s: kṣemaṃ subhikṣam ārogyaṃ suvṛṣṭiṃ cātra nirdiśet ||
62.3.d: क्षेमं सुभिक्षम् आरोग्यं सुवृष्टिं चात्र निर्दिशेत् ॥
62.3.m: [One should predict security, plenty of food, health, and abundant rain here.]

62.4.s: gambhīraṃ garjamānas tu megha āyāti pārthivaḥ | snigdho hy añjanasaṃkāśaḥ sumahatparvatopamaḥ ||
62.4.d: गम्भीरं गर्जमानस् तु मेघ आयाति पार्थिवः । स्निग्धो ह्य् अञ्जनसंकाशः सुमहत्पर्वतोपमः ॥
62.4.m: Rumbling deeply, an earthly cloud approaches, / glossy, resembling collyrium, equal to a huge mountain;

62.4.s: vitrāsayan diśaḥ sarvā drutaṃ cāpi pravarṣati | indrāyudhaṃ bhavec cātra vidyut stanitam eva ca ||
62.4.d: वित्रासयन् दिशः सर्वा द्रुतं चापि प्रवर्षति । इन्द्रायुधं भवेच् चात्र विद्युत् स्तनितम् एव च ॥
62.4.m: terrifying all directions, it rains swiftly; / and rainbow, lightning, and rumbling occur here.

62.4.s: suvṛṣṭiṃ kṣemam ārogyaṃ subhikṣaṃ paramā mudaḥ | yajñodbhavais tu modante ānandair moditāḥ prajāḥ ||
62.4.d: सुवृष्टिं क्षेमम् आरोग्यं सुभिक्षं परमा मुदः । यज्ञोद्भवैस् तु मोदन्ते आनन्दैर् मोदिताः प्रजाः ॥
62.4.m: Abundant rain, security, health, plenty of food, and supreme rejoicings [arise]; / the subjects, gladdened by joys arising from sacrifices, rejoice.

62.4.s: eteṣāṃ bhūmikampānāṃ praśastaṃ hīndrakampanam | jānīyāl lakṣaṇair etaiḥ sarvam eva śubhāśubham ||
62.4.d: एतेषां भूमिकम्पानां प्रशस्तं हीन्द्रकम्पनम् । जानीयाल् लक्षणैर् एतैः सर्वम् एव शुभाशुभम् ॥
62.4.m: Indeed, of these earthquakes, Indra's earthquake is auspicious; / one should know all good and bad by these characteristics.

62.4.s: eteṣu triṣu kampeṣu atharvā śāstrakovidaḥ | māhendrīm amṛtāṃ vāpi kuryāc chāntiṃ sadakṣiṇām ||
62.4.d: एतेषु त्रिषु कम्पेषु अथर्वा शास्त्रकोविदः । माहेन्द्रीम् अमृतां वापि कुर्याच् छान्तिं सदक्षिणाम् ॥
62.4.m: During these three earthquakes, an Atharvan priest skilled in the scriptures / should perform the Māhendrī or the Amṛtā propitiatory rite with a sacrificial fee.

62.4.s: indrakampe tu vidhivad aindrair mantrair vidhānavit | tatohalasya pradhānārthaṃ juhuyāc ca japet tathā ||
