67.7.d: वायुर् महान् नभपतिर् वज्रपाणिस् तथा ईश्वरस् । शमनस् सर्वाद्भुतानां महाव्याहृतयस् तथा ॥
67.7.m: "Great Vāyu, lord of the sky, vajra-in-hand, and lord, / pacifier of all portents," and also the great sacred utterances.

67.7.s: hutvā sviṣṭakṛtaṃ ca eva carutantraṃ samāpayet | vimuktotpātadoṣas tu jīvet tu śaradas śatam ||
67.7.d: हुत्वा स्विष्टकृतं च एव चरुतन्त्रं समापयेत् । विमुक्तोत्पातदोषस् तु जीवेत् तु शरदस् शतम् ॥
67.7.m: Having offered the sviṣṭakṛt oblation as well, he should conclude the rite of the boiled oblations. / Freed from the fault of portents, he shall live for a hundred autumns.

67.8.s: atha ced anyaśākhasu kartā bhavati vedavit | japtvā sa ṛgyajuḥsāmnaṃ śatamātraṃ samāhitas ||
67.8.d: अथ चेद् अन्यशाखसु कर्ता भवति वेदवित् । जप्त्वा स ऋग्यजुःसाम्नं शतमात्रं समाहितस् ॥
67.8.m: Now, if the performer is a knower of the Veda from another branch, / having recited, concentrated in mind, about a hundred verses from the Ṛg-, Yajur-, or Sāmaveda,

67.8.s: gāyatryaṣṭaśataṃ japtvā yayajamānas samāhitas | vācayet tam upādhyāyaṃ vastreṇa kanakena vā ||
67.8.d: गायत्र्यष्टशतं जप्त्वा ययजमानस् समाहितस् । वाचयेत् तम् उपाध्यायं वस्त्रेण कनकेन वा ॥
67.8.m: and having recited the Gāyatrī a hundred and eight times, the sacrificer, concentrated in mind, / should make that preceptor speak [blessings] with a gift of garment or gold,

67.8.s: dṛṣṭāṃ ca eva adbhutaṃ yasmins tat ca api pratipādayet | etās tu dakṣiṇās sarvās śaktiyukto na hāpayet ||
67.8.d: दृष्टां च एव अद्भुतं यस्मिन्स् तत् च अपि प्रतिपादयेत् । एतास् तु दक्षिणास् सर्वास् शक्तियुक्तो न हापयेत् ॥
67.8.m: and in whatever [object] the portent was seen, he should also hand that over. / An able man should not omit all these sacrificial fees.

67.8.s: yajamānas tatsuto vā yas svayaṃ kartum arhati | brāhmaṇāya viśeṣeṇa dadyāt tāṃ dakṣiṇāṃ śubhām ||
67.8.d: यजमानस् तत्सुतो वा यस् स्वयं कर्तुम् अर्हति । ब्राह्मणाय विशेषेण दद्यात् तां दक्षिणां शुभाम् ॥
67.8.m: The sacrificer or his son who is capable of performing it himself / should give that auspicious sacrificial fee especially to a brahmin.

67.8.s: japtvā atharvaśiras ca eva kuryāt vipreṣu pūjanam | śaktyā atha bhojanaṃ ca eva kuryāt vipreṣu pūjanam ||
67.8.d: जप्त्वा अथर्वशिरस् च एव कुर्यात् विप्रेषु पूजनम् । शक्त्या अथ भोजनं च एव कुर्यात् विप्रेषु पूजनम् ॥
67.8.m: Having recited the Atharvaśiras, he should perform worship among the Brahmins. / According to his ability, he should provide feeding and worship among the Brahmins.

67.8.s: etad evaṃ samākhyātam adbhutānāṃ viśodhanam | caturṇām api varṇānāṃ yas kuryāt śraddhayā anvitas ||
67.8.d: एतद् एवं समाख्यातम् अद्भुतानां विशोधनम् । चतुर्णाम् अपि वर्णानां यस् कुर्यात् श्रद्धया अन्वितस् ॥
67.8.m: Thus has been explained this purification from portents. / Whoever among the four castes should perform it endowed with faith,

67.8.s: maraṇaṃ na bhavet tasya na duḥkhaṃ na daridratā | sidhyanti sarvakāryāṇi dharme ca asya matir bhavet ||
67.8.d: मरणं न भवेत् तस्य न दुःखं न दरिद्रता । सिध्यन्ति सर्वकार्याणि धर्मे च अस्य मतिर् भवेत् ॥
67.8.m: Death shall not befall him, nor suffering, nor poverty; / all his undertakings succeed, and his mind turns to righteousness.

67.8.s: etat puṇyaṃ paritraṃ ca devatāyāgapūjanam | sarvaśāntikaṃ ca eva pratipuruṣaṃ nibodhata || pratipuruṣaṃ nibodhata iti ||
67.8.d: एतत् पुण्यं परित्रं च देवतायागपूजनम् । सर्वशान्तिकं च एव प्रतिपुरुषं निबोधत ॥ प्रतिपुरुषं निबोधत इति ॥
67.8.m: This is meritorious, pure, a worship through sacrifice to the deities, / and an all-propitiating rite; understand it for each person. Understand it for each person.

68.1.s: om athātaḥ saṃpravakṣyāmi yad uktaṃ padmayoninā | upāṅgaṃ śukracārasta śubhāśubhanivedakam ||
68.1.d: ओम् अथातः संप्रवक्ष्यामि यद् उक्तं पद्मयोनिना । उपाङ्गं शुक्रचारस्त शुभाशुभनिवेदकम् ॥
68.1.m: Om. Now, therefore, I shall declare what was spoken by the lotus-born [Brahmā], / an ancillary limb concerning the course of Venus, indicating good and evil,

68.1.s: svapnādhyāyaṃ pravakṣyāmi kroṣṭuker vacanaṃ yathā | śaśaṃsire purā yaṃ hi śaunakāya mahātmane ||
68.1.d: स्वप्नाध्यायं प्रवक्ष्यामि क्रोष्टुकेर् वचनं यथा । शशंसिरे पुरा यं हि शौनकाय महात्मने ॥
68.1.m: I shall explain the chapter on dreams according to the word of Kroṣṭuki, / which indeed they recited of old to the high-souled Śaunaka.

68.1.s: nimittajñānakuśalāḥ sarvaṃ tasya tu pṛcchataḥ | grahā bhārgavabhaumārkāḥ paittikā dīptitejasaḥ ||
68.1.d: निमित्तज्ञानकुशलाः सर्वं तस्य तु पृच्छतः । ग्रहा भार्गवभौमार्काः पैत्तिका दीप्तितेजसः ॥
68.1.m: To him inquiring about everything, those skilled in the knowledge of omens [spoke]: / The planets Venus, Mars, and the Sun are bilious, of blazing brilliance;

68.1.s: kaphaprakṛtayo madhyā bṛhaspatibudhendavaḥ | vātaprakṛtayaḥ krūrā rāhuketuśanaiścarāḥ ||
68.1.d: कफप्रकृतयो मध्या बृहस्पतिबुधेन्दवः । वातप्रकृतयः क्रूरा राहुकेतुशनैश्चराः ॥
68.1.m: Jupiter, Mercury, and the Moon have phlegmatic constitutions, being middling; / Rāhu, Ketu, and Saturn are cruel, with windy constitutions.

68.1.s: teṣāṃ tathā phalaṃ vidyāt saṃnipāte yathākramam | ete nava grahā jñeyā vātapittakaphātmakāḥ ||
68.1.d: तेषां तथा फलं विद्यात् संनिपाते यथाक्रमम् । एते नव ग्रहा ज्ञेया वातपित्तकफात्मकाः ॥
68.1.m: One should know their fruit likewise in combination, according to order. / These nine planets are to be recognized as composed of wind, bile, and phlegm.

68.1.s: eṣāṃ prakṛtitulyānāṃ niṣiktānāṃ tu teṣu vai | saṃyogeṣu ca jātānāṃ tulya prakṛtitā bhavet ||
68.1.d: एषां प्रकृतितुल्यानां निषिक्तानां तु तेषु वै । संयोगेषु च जातानां तुल्य प्रकृतिता भवेत् ॥
68.1.m: Indeed, when these [planets] matching their humours are situated in them, / and for those born under their conjunctions, there arises an equal constitution.

68.1.s: arkenduprabhavā deham upatiṣṭhanti dehinaḥ | tasmān niṣicyamāneṣu vātapittakapheṣu yaḥ ||
68.1.d: अर्केन्दुप्रभवा देहम् उपतिष्ठन्ति देहिनः । तस्मान् निषिच्यमानेषु वातपित्तकफेषु यः ॥
68.1.m: Things originating from the Sun and the Moon attend the body of the embodied soul. / Therefore, among wind, bile, and phlegm being discharged, whichever

68.1.s: eṣām anyatamo deho yātiriktaḥ prakāśate | pracakṣate sā prakṛtiḥ prakṛtijñānakovidāḥ ||
68.1.d: एषाम् अन्यतमो देहो यातिरिक्तः प्रकाशते । प्रचक्षते सा प्रकृतिः प्रकृतिज्ञानकोविदाः ॥
68.1.m: one of these appears predominant in the body, / that, those skilled in knowledge of humours declare to be the constitution.

68.1.s: tatra ye mānisvāṅgāni ṛjavaḥ kalahapriyāḥ | uṣṇāḥ kapilaromāṇāaḥ svedanā anavekṣaṇāḥ ||
68.1.d: तत्र ये मानिस्वाङ्गानि ऋजवः कलहप्रियाः । उष्णाः कपिलरोमाणाअः स्वेदना अनवेक्षणाः ॥
68.1.m: Among them, those who are proud of their limbs, straight, fond of quarrelling, / hot, with tawny hair, sweating, unobservant,

68.1.s: bahvāśidurbhagāś caiva mṛdvaṅgāḥ śiśirapriyāḥ | lālanāḥ śithilāṅgāś ca priyāś ca priyāś ca lavaṇās tathā ||
68.1.d: बह्वाशिदुर्भगाश् चैव मृद्वङ्गाः शिशिरप्रियाः । लालनाः शिथिलाङ्गाश् च प्रियाश् च प्रियाश् च लवणास् तथा ॥
68.1.m: eating much and ill-fated, soft-limbed, fond of cold, / fond of caressing, loose-limbed, affectionate, and fond of salty food,

68.1.s: tanutvaṅnakharomāṇas tv ācāryās tīkṣṇa eva ca | valīpalitabhūyiṣṭhās tathā khalatino narāḥ ||
68.1.d: तनुत्वङ्नखरोमाणस् त्व् आचार्यास् तीक्ष्ण एव च । वलीपलितभूयिष्ठास् तथा खलतिनो नराः ॥
68.1.m: having thin skin, nails, and hair, teachers, sharp, / having many wrinkles and grey hairs, and men who are bald,

68.1.s: glayate śuṣyate caiṣām āśu mālyānulepanam | dāhātmikāḥ śaśāṅke 'pi pittaprakṛtayas tu te ||
68.1.d: ग्लयते शुष्यते चैषाम् आशु माल्यानुलेपनम् । दाहात्मिकाः शशाङ्के ऽपि पित्तप्रकृतयस् तु ते ॥
68.1.m: and whose garland and ointment quickly wither and dry up, / burning even by the moon—they are of bilious constitution.

68.1.s: svapne caiva prapaśyanti diśaḥ kanakapiṅgalāḥ | maṇḍalāni samūhāṃś ca dikṣu pītāruṇaprabhān ||
68.1.d: स्वप्ने चैव प्रपश्यन्ति दिशः कनकपिङ्गलाः । मण्डलानि समूहांश् च दिक्षु पीतारुणप्रभान् ॥
68.1.m: And in a dream they see the quarters golden-tawny, / and discs and masses in the quarters shining yellow and red,

68.1.s: śṛṅgārimadirān deśāñ śuṣkāṃ malajalāṃ mahīm | śuṣkagulmadrumalatā dahyamānaṃ mahad vanam ||
68.1.d: शृङ्गारिमदिरान् देशाञ् शुष्कां मलजलां महीम् । शुष्कगुल्मद्रुमलता दह्यमानं महद् वनम् ॥
68.1.m: erotic, intoxicating regions, dried-up earth with dirty water, / dry shrubs, trees, and creepers, and a great forest burning,

68.1.s: viśuṣkāṇi ca vastrāṇi rudhirāṅgāṃs tathaiva ca | dahanādīṃś ca devāṃś ca raktam induṃ sugandhikān ||
68.1.d: विशुष्काणि च वस्त्राणि रुधिराङ्गांस् तथैव च । दहनादींश् च देवांश् च रक्तम् इन्दुं सुगन्धिकान् ॥
68.1.m: and dried-up clothes, bloody limbs likewise, / fire and similar gods, a red moon, fragrant things,

68.1.s: palāśāni ca puṣpāṇi karṇikāravanāni ca | digdāhavidyucchulkāś ca dīpyamānaṃ ca pāvakam ||
68.1.d: पलाशानि च पुष्पाणि कर्णिकारवनानि च । दिग्दाहविद्युच्छुल्काश् च दीप्यमानं च पावकम् ॥
68.1.m: and Palāśa blossoms, forests of Karṇikāra, / forest-fire blazes in the quarters, lightning, meteors, and blazing fire;

68.1.s: bhūyiṣṭhaṃ bhūṣitāś cāpi pibanti subahūdakam | saritsaravanānteṣu kūpaprasravaṇeṣu ca ||
68.1.d: भूयिष्ठं भूषिताश् चापि पिबन्ति सुबहूदकम् । सरित्सरवनान्तेषु कूपप्रस्रवणेषु च ॥
68.1.m: mostly adorned, they also drink vast amounts of water / at rivers, lakes, edge of forests, wells, and springs;

68.1.s: uṣṇārtāḥ śītakāmās tu nimajjanti pibanti ca | kalahaṃ caiva kurvanti duḥkhāny anubhavanti ca ||
68.1.d: उष्णार्ताः शीतकामास् तु निमज्जन्ति पिबन्ति च । कलहं चैव कुर्वन्ति दुःखान्य् अनुभवन्ति च ॥
68.1.m: afflicted by heat, desiring cold, they dive and drink; / and they pick quarrels and experience sufferings,

68.1.s: strībhiś caiva vimānyante kṣayante klāmayanti ca | ity evaṃ paittikā jñeyāḥ prakṛtisvapnalakṣaṇe ||
68.1.d: स्त्रीभिश् चैव विमान्यन्ते क्षयन्ते क्लामयन्ति च । इत्य् एवं पैत्तिका ज्ञेयाः प्रकृतिस्वप्नलक्षणे ॥
68.1.m: and they are dishonoured by women, grow weak, and are exhausted. / Thus are bilious persons to be recognized in the characteristics of constitution and dreams.

68.1.s: prakṛtisvapnabhāvaiś ca śleṣmikāṇy api me śṛṇu | snigdhakeśanakhaśmaśrutatatvagromabhāṣiṇaḥ ||
68.1.d: प्रकृतिस्वप्नभावैश् च श्लेष्मिकाण्य् अपि मे शृणु । स्निग्धकेशनखश्मश्रुततत्वग्रोमभाषिणः ॥
68.1.m: And hear from me also the phlegmatic signs by constitution and dream states: / [they have] glossy hair, nails, beard, fine skin and body hair, and pleasant speech,

68.1.s: mahodarabhojoraskadīrghakeśanakhadvijāñ | vaiḍūryopalabaddhe tu saṃnibhair niyamaiḥ śubhaiḥ ||
68.1.d: महोदरभोजोरस्कदीर्घकेशनखद्विजाञ् । वैडूर्योपलबद्धे तु संनिभैर् नियमैः शुभैः ॥
68.1.m: a large belly, broad chest, long hair, nails, and teeth; / having limbs set like cat's-eye gems, with auspicious, steady rules,

68.1.s: sthiropacitasarvāṅgā bhavanti sukhabhāginaḥ | śirodarakaṭiskandhapakṣayor vimalekṣaṇāḥ ||
68.1.d: स्थिरोपचितसर्वाङ्गा भवन्ति सुखभागिनः । शिरोदरकटिस्कन्धपक्षयोर् विमलेक्षणाः ॥
68.1.m: with all limbs firm and fleshy, they are partakers of happiness, / with spotless eyes, [sound] in head, belly, waist, shoulders, and sides,

68.1.s: priyāḥ priyamvadāḥ śūrāḥ kṛtajñā dṛḍhabhaktayaḥ | cirād gṛhṇanti suciraṃ gṛhītaṃ dhārayanti ca ||
68.1.d: प्रियाः प्रियम्वदाः शूराः कृतज्ञा दृढभक्तयः । चिराद् गृह्णन्ति सुचिरं गृहीतं धारयन्ति च ॥
68.1.m: dear, pleasant-speaking, heroic, grateful, firm in devotion; / they learn after a long time, and retain for a very long time what is learned;

68.1.s: na krudhyanti cirāt kruddhāḥ saṃbhavanty antakopamāḥ | pūjābhir vipulāṃ bhūmim āvahanti kulasya ca ||
68.1.d: न क्रुध्यन्ति चिरात् क्रुद्धाः संभवन्त्य् अन्तकोपमाः । पूजाभिर् विपुलां भूमिम् आवहन्ति कुलस्य च ॥
68.1.m: they do not get angry, but once angered after a long time, they become like the God of Death; / through worship they bring vast land to their family,

68.1.s: khyāpayanti ca sarvatra guṇaiś ca vipulair yaśaḥ | māṃśoṣṇatātimadhurapayohārātha suprajāḥ ||
68.1.d: ख्यापयन्ति च सर्वत्र गुणैश् च विपुलैर् यशः । मांशोष्णतातिमधुरपयोहाराथ सुप्रजाः ॥
68.1.m: and spread their fame everywhere by extensive virtues; / eating meat, hot and excessively sweet milk, blessed with good offspring,

68.1.s: na cirāc chuṣyate caiṣāṃ toyamālyānulepanam | nimīlitāsyanayanā niḥśabdā niḥprakampinaḥ ||
68.1.d: न चिराच् छुष्यते चैषां तोयमाल्यानुलेपनम् । निमीलितास्यनयना निःशब्दा निःप्रकम्पिनः ॥
68.1.m: and their water, garlands, and unguents do not dry up quickly; / having closed mouths and eyes, silent, free from trembling,

68.1.s: svapanty ekena pārśvena ciraṃ sukhanibodhanāḥ | nātiduḥkhena jīvanti votpadyante sukhena tu ||
68.1.d: स्वपन्त्य् एकेन पार्श्वेन चिरं सुखनिबोधनाः । नातिदुःखेन जीवन्ति वोत्पद्यन्ते सुखेन तु ॥
68.1.m: they sleep on one side, waking happily after a long time; / they live without great distress and are born into comfort,

68.1.s: śyāmāḥ śyāmāvadātāś ca śrīmanto 'dṛḍharogiṇaḥ | alpāśidīrghakāmās tu bhavanty arthasahiṣṇavaḥ ||
68.1.d: श्यामाः श्यामावदाताश् च श्रीमन्तो ऽदृढरोगिणः । अल्पाशिदीर्घकामास् तु भवन्त्य् अर्थसहिष्णवः ॥
68.1.m: dark or fair-complexioned, prosperous, not prone to severe illness; / eating little, having lasting desires, they are capable of acquiring wealth,

68.1.s: kṣutpipāsāsahāś cāpi kaphaprakṛtayo narāḥ | svapneṣu caiva paśyanti ramyaṃ candanakānanam ||
68.1.d: क्षुत्पिपासासहाश् चापि कफप्रकृतयो नराः । स्वप्नेषु चैव पश्यन्ति रम्यं चन्दनकाननम् ॥
68.1.m: and men of phlegmatic constitution endure hunger and thirst. / And in dreams they see a lovely sandalwood forest,

68.1.s: vikuḍmalapalāśāni pauṇḍarīkavanāni ca | śubhāś ca śiśiraprāyā nadyaḥ śubhajalāvahāḥ ||
68.1.d: विकुड्मलपलाशानि पौण्डरीकवनानि च । शुभाश् च शिशिरप्राया नद्यः शुभजलावहाः ॥
68.1.m: flowering Palāśa trees, groves of white lotuses, / and auspicious, generally cool rivers carrying pure water,

68.1.s: tuṣāreṇāvṛtāś cāpi himavāghapaṭalāni ca | muktāmaṇisuvāśṛṅgā mṛṇālaphalakāni ca ||
68.1.d: तुषारेणावृताश् चापि हिमवाघपटलानि च । मुक्तामणिसुवाशृङ्गा मृणालफलकानि च ॥
68.1.m: and [mountains] covered with frost, masses of snowy clouds, / horns decorated with pearls, lotus-stalk leaves,

68.1.s: varāhakhaḍgamahiṣā mṛgāś ca rathakuñjarāḥ | spaṣṭatāraṃ tu haṃsāś ca vyopoḍhanti nabhastalam ||
68.1.d: वराहखड्गमहिषा मृगाश् च रथकुञ्जराः । स्पष्टतारं तु हंसाश् च व्योपोढन्ति नभस्तलम् ॥
68.1.m: boars, rhinoceroses, buffaloes, deer, chariots, and elephants; / and clearly marked swans taking flight across the sky;

68.1.s: kundagokṣīragaurābhir indoḥ kīrṇagabhastiṣu | protphullakumudākārā vyomni sudhāmbusaprabhaiḥ ||
68.1.d: कुन्दगोक्षीरगौराभिर् इन्दोः कीर्णगभस्तिषु । प्रोत्फुल्लकुमुदाकारा व्योम्नि सुधाम्बुसप्रभैः ॥
68.1.m: in the sky, with rays of the moon scattered white like Kunda flowers or cow's milk, / having the form of blooming white lotuses, with the brilliance of nectar-water,

68.1.s: rājahaṃsapratīkāśaṃ śaśāṅkaṃ cāmaladyutim | śubhrāṇi ca vimānāni phalāni madhurāṇi ca ||
68.1.d: राजहंसप्रतीकाशं शशाङ्कं चामलद्युतिम् । शुभ्राणि च विमानानि फलानि मधुराणि च ॥
68.1.m: the moon resembling a royal swan and of spotless lustre, / and white celestial cars, sweet fruits,

68.1.s: kṛtapuṣpopahārāṇi mahānti bhavanāni ca | brāhmaṇān yajñavādāṃś ca dadhikṣīrāmṛtāni ca ||
68.1.d: कृतपुष्पोपहाराणि महान्ति भवनानि च । ब्राह्मणान् यज्ञवादांश् च दधिक्षीरामृतानि च ॥
68.1.m: large palaces with offerings of flowers made, / Brahmins, recitations of sacrifice, curd, milk, and nectar,

68.1.s: striyaś ca paramodāktāḥ suveṣāḥ svabhyalaṃkṛtāḥ | madhuraśvetapītāni prāyaśaś ciram eva tu ||
68.1.d: स्त्रियश् च परमोदाक्ताः सुवेषाः स्वभ्यलंकृताः । मधुरश्वेतपीतानि प्रायशश् चिरम् एव तु ॥
68.1.m: and supremely elevated women, well-attired and well-adorned; / mostly sweet, white, and yellow things, for a long time indeed;

68.1.s: svapneṣu caivaṃ paśyanti kaphaprakṛtayo narāḥ | prakṛtisvapnabhāveṣu vātikāny api lakṣayet ||
68.1.d: स्वप्नेषु चैवं पश्यन्ति कफप्रकृतयो नराः । प्रकृतिस्वप्नभावेषु वातिकान्य् अपि लक्षयेत् ॥
68.1.m: thus do men of phlegmatic constitution see in dreams. / Among constitutional and dream states, one should also observe those of wind:

68.1.s: calāś ca calavikrāntāḥ kṣipramkṣipraṃ pralāpinaḥ | suptāḥ pralāpinas tv anye kaṣāyakaṭukapriyāḥ ||
68.1.d: चलाश् च चलविक्रान्ताः क्षिप्रम्क्षिप्रं प्रलापिनः । सुप्ताः प्रलापिनस् त्व् अन्ये कषायकटुकप्रियाः ॥
68.1.m: unsteady, unsteady in stride, speaking very quickly, / talking in their sleep, fond of astringent and pungent flavours,

68.1.s: tvagromanakhadantoṣṭhapāṇipādatalādiṣu | rūkṣasphuṭitadurdarśā durbalā duḥkhabhāginaḥ ||
68.1.d: त्वग्रोमनखदन्तोष्ठपाणिपादतलादिषु । रूक्षस्फुटितदुर्दर्शा दुर्बला दुःखभागिनः ॥
68.1.m: rough, cracked, and unsightly on skin, body hair, nails, teeth, lips, palms, and soles; / weak, partakers of misery,

68.1.s: kaṭhinopacitāṅgāś ca bhrāntacittāphutekṣaṇāḥ | lāpino mṛdavaḥ krūrā vidyād asthirabuddhayaḥ ||
68.1.d: कठिनोपचिताङ्गाश् च भ्रान्तचित्ताफुतेक्षणाः । लापिनो मृदवः क्रूरा विद्याद् अस्थिरबुद्धयः ॥
68.1.m: having hard and thick limbs, confused minds, restless eyes, / chattering, soft yet cruel, to be known as unstable in intellect,

68.1.s: nṛtyagītakathāśīla jambhino duḥkhabhāginaḥ | hrasvalomāḥ suvapuṣo durbalā dhamanās tathā ||
68.1.d: नृत्यगीतकथाशील जम्भिनो दुःखभागिनः । ह्रस्वलोमाः सुवपुषो दुर्बला धमनास् तथा ॥
68.1.m: addicted to dance, song, and talk, yawning, partakers of suffering, / with short body hair, of good physique, weak, with visible veins,

68.1.s: kṣāmā bhinnāḥ sadoṣāś ca satataṃ vānavasthitāḥ | hastanakhatvagoṣṭhānāṃ pādānāṃ ca vikāriṇaḥ ||
68.1.d: क्षामा भिन्नाः सदोषाश् च सततं वानवस्थिताः । हस्तनखत्वगोष्ठानां पादानां च विकारिणः ॥
68.1.m: emaciated, split, defective, constantly unsteady, / having afflictions of the hands, nails, skin, lips, and feet,

68.1.s: akasmāt kopanāś cāpi rodanā dhamānās tathā | paraprakṛtiśīlāś ca valganāsphoṭanapriyāḥ ||
68.1.d: अकस्मात् कोपनाश् चापि रोदना धमानास् तथा । परप्रकृतिशीलाश् च वल्गनास्फोटनप्रियाः ॥
68.1.m: getting angry without cause, weeping, sighing, / imitating the nature of others, and fond of leaping and clapping their hands.

68.1.s: durbalāḥ śiśirāś cāpi vātaprakṛtayo naraḥ | svapneṣu caiva paśyanti vātābhravimalā diśaḥ ||
68.1.d: दुर्बलाः शिशिराश् चापि वातप्रकृतयो नरः । स्वप्नेषु चैव पश्यन्ति वाताभ्रविमला दिशः ॥
68.1.m: Men of wind-constitution are weak and chilled; / and in their dreams they see the quarters devoid of wind-clouds,

68.1.s: mārutavegatuṅgāni bhuvanāni vānāni ca | śyāmatārāgrahagaṇaṃ vidhvastārkendumaṇḍalam ||
68.1.d: मारुतवेगतुङ्गानि भुवनानि वानानि च । श्यामताराग्रहगणं विध्वस्तार्केन्दुमण्डलम् ॥
68.1.m: and worlds and forests rising high on the wind's momentum, / a host of dark stars and planets, and the disks of sun and moon destroyed,

68.1.s: dhārācaradbhir viśvābhaiḥ saṃkulaṃ gaganaṃ ghanaiḥ | bhramantaḥ pakṣisaṃghāś ca mṛgāś codbhrāntayūthapāḥ ||
68.1.d: धाराचरद्भिर् विश्वाभैः संकुलं गगनं घनैः । भ्रमन्तः पक्षिसंघाश् च मृगाश् चोद्भ्रान्तयूथपाः ॥
68.1.m: the sky crowded with all-pervading clouds that bring downpours, / wandering flocks of birds, and deer whose herd-leaders have gone astray,

68.1.s: anyāś cāpu śambarāś ca girigahvarakānanāḥ | bhramanti ghnanti dhāvanti ūrdhvebhyaḥ prapatanti ca ||
68.1.d: अन्याश् चापु शम्बराश् च गिरिगह्वरकाननाः । भ्रमन्ति घ्नन्ति धावन्ति ऊर्ध्वेभ्यः प्रपतन्ति च ॥
68.1.m: and other [creatures] and śambara-deer roaming in mountain-caves and forests; / they wander, kill, run, and fall from heights.

68.1.s: svapneṣv etāni paśyanti vātaprakṛtayo narāḥ | miśrasvapnasvabhāveṣu saṃnipātātmakāḥ viduḥ ||
68.1.d: स्वप्नेष्व् एतानि पश्यन्ति वातप्रकृतयो नराः । मिश्रस्वप्नस्वभावेषु संनिपातात्मकाः विदुः ॥
68.1.m: Men of wind-constitution see these things in their dreams. / In mixed dream-natures, they understand them to consist of a combination [of humours].

68.1.s: etās tisraḥ prakṛtayaḥ saṃsṛṣṭāś ca sarvaśaḥ ||
68.1.d: एतास् तिस्रः प्रकृतयः संसृष्टाश् च सर्वशः ॥
68.1.m: These are the three constitutions, and they are mixed together in every way.

68.1.s: samyak karaṇavijñānaṃ tathā svapnād bhavet phalam | śubhaṃ vāpi aśubhaṃ vāpi nirdeṣṭavyam aśeṣataḥ ||
68.1.d: सम्यक् करणविज्ञानं तथा स्वप्नाद् भवेत् फलम् । शुभं वापि अशुभं वापि निर्देष्टव्यम् अशेषतः ॥
68.1.m: From the correct understanding of the instrument, as well as from the dream, the result arises; / whether auspicious or inauspicious, it should be pointed out entirely.

68.1.s: yenayenendriyārthena viddhaḥ svapiti mānavaḥ | tasyatasyendriyārthasya suptaḥ karmāṇi paśyati ||
68.1.d: येनयेनेन्द्रियार्थेन विद्धः स्वपिति मानवः । तस्यतस्येन्द्रियार्थस्य सुप्तः कर्माणि पश्यति ॥
68.1.m: Afflicted by whatever sense-object a man falls asleep, / of that very sense-object he sees the operations when asleep.

68.1.s: prakṛtyākṛtasaṃkalpasaṃbhavā devatāsv api | svapnamālāṃ tu yaḥ paśyed yāṃ tu dṛṣṭvā na tu smaret ||
68.1.d: प्रकृत्याकृतसंकल्पसंभवा देवतास्व् अपि । स्वप्नमालां तु यः पश्येद् यां तु दृष्ट्वा न तु स्मरेत् ॥
68.1.m: Arising from intent not formed by one's own constitution, even in the case of deities— / but if one should see a series of dreams which, having seen, one does not remember,

68.1.s: naite phalaṃ prayacchanti gargasya vacanaṃ yathā | prakṛtyānūkajān āhur eke śubhaphalodayān ||
68.1.d: नैते फलं प्रयच्छन्ति गर्गस्य वचनं यथा । प्रकृत्यानूकजान् आहुर् एके शुभफलोदयान् ॥
68.1.m: these do not yield a result, according to the word of Garga. / Some say that dreams arising from bodily nature bring about the rise of auspicious results.

68.1.s: sārasvataṃ yathānūkaṃ saṃghātasaṃśrayaṃ śṛṇu | dṛṣṭvā bhogam asuptavyaṃ tataḥ prāpya śubhaṃ phalam ||
68.1.d: सारस्वतं यथानूकं संघातसंश्रयं शृणु । दृष्ट्वा भोगम् असुप्तव्यं ततः प्राप्य शुभं फलम् ॥
68.1.m: Hear the nature relating to Sarasvatī, which depends upon assembly: / having seen enjoyment that should not be slept through, one then obtains an auspicious result.

68.1.s: svapnaprakṛtibhāvaṃ tu jñātvā tattvaṃ samādiśet ||
68.1.d: स्वप्नप्रकृतिभावं तु ज्ञात्वा तत्त्वं समादिशेत् ॥
68.1.m: Having recognized the condition of the dream-constitution, one should declare the truth.

68.2.s: gṛhṇīta samudgendvindravāyvagnyarkanadīṃ kṣitim | samudraṃ vāhinīṃ dvīpaṃ laṅghayed vā vasuṃdharām ||
68.2.d: गृह्णीत समुद्गेन्द्विन्द्रवाय्वग्न्यर्कनदीं क्षितिम् । समुद्रं वाहिनीं द्वीपं लङ्घयेद् वा वसुंधराम् ॥
68.2.m: If one should seize the ocean, the moon, Indra, wind, fire, sun, a river, or the earth, / or cross over the sea, an army, an island, or the earth;

68.2.s: vāhinīṃ caturaṅgāṃ ca jīvachattrapatākinīm | dorbhyāṃ ca pratigṛhṇīyāt tathāketuvasuṃdharām ||
68.2.d: वाहिनीं चतुरङ्गां च जीवछत्त्रपताकिनीम् । दोर्भ्यां च प्रतिगृह्णीयात् तथाकेतुवसुंधराम् ॥
68.2.m: and an army of four divisions, alive, with umbrellas and banners, / or if one should receive the earth marked by banners with both arms;

68.2.s: ekapuṣkariṇīparṇe sauvarṇe bhāhane 'pi vā | sarpiṣā pāyasaṃ bhuṅkte gāṃ duhan yaś ca budhyati ||
68.2.d: एकपुष्करिणीपर्णे सौवर्णे भाहने ऽपि वा । सर्पिषा पायसं भुङ्क्ते गां दुहन् यश् च बुध्यति ॥
68.2.m: or if one eats rice-milk with clarified butter on a single lotus-leaf or on a golden vessel, / or if, while milking a cow, he wakes up;

68.2.s: pariveṣaḥ svayaṃ candre yo 'navastravasuṃdharām | parvatāgraṃ samāruhya kṣitiṃ yaś cāvalokayet ||
68.2.d: परिवेषः स्वयं चन्द्रे यो ऽनवस्त्रवसुंधराम् । पर्वताग्रं समारुह्य क्षितिं यश् चावलोकयेत् ॥
68.2.m: if he himself is a halo around the moon, or [sees] the unclad earth, / or having climbed to a mountain peak looks down at the earth;

68.2.s: ā kaṇṭhaṃ majjate yo hi mānavaḥ śoṇitārṇave | rathena siṃhayuktena parvataṃ cādhirohati ||
68.2.d: आ कण्ठं मज्जते यो हि मानवः शोणितार्णवे । रथेन सिंहयुक्तेन पर्वतं चाधिरोहति ॥
68.2.m: if a man is immersed up to the neck in an ocean of blood, / or ascends a mountain on a chariot yoked with lions;

68.2.s: mahīṃ vā kampayed yas tu cālayed vā punar girīm | śvetam aśvam athāruhya pāṇḍuraṃ vāpu yo gajam ||
68.2.d: महीं वा कम्पयेद् यस् तु चालयेद् वा पुनर् गिरीम् । श्वेतम् अश्वम् अथारुह्य पाण्डुरं वापु यो गजम् ॥
68.2.m: or if he shakes the earth, or moves mountains, / or having mounted a white horse or a pale-white elephant,

68.2.s: bhuṅkte puṣkariṇīparṇe pāyasaṃ vāpi sarpiṣā | aṅgavṛddhiṃ śirovṛddhiṃ prāpnuyād yas tu mānavaḥ ||
68.2.d: भुङ्क्ते पुष्करिणीपर्णे पायसं वापि सर्पिषा । अङ्गवृद्धिं शिरोवृद्धिं प्राप्नुयाद् यस् तु मानवः ॥
68.2.m: he eats rice-milk with clarified butter on a lotus-leaf; / or whatever man should attain growth of limbs or growth of the head;

68.2.s: brāhmaṇo vāpi rājā vā svapne yad abhiṣecayet | rājā tu pārthivo jñeyaḥ kroṣṭuker vacanaṃ yathā ||
68.2.d: ब्राह्मणो वापि राजा वा स्वप्ने यद् अभिषेचयेत् । राजा तु पार्थिवो ज्ञेयः क्रोष्टुकेर् वचनं यथा ॥
68.2.m: or if a Brahmin or a king should consecrate [him] in a dream— / he should be known as an earthly king, according to the word of Kroṣṭuki.

68.2.s: śiro vā chidyate yasya vimānaṃ śoṇitaṃ tathā | senāpatyaṃ mahac cāyur arthalābhaṃ tathaiva ca ||
68.2.d: शिरो वा छिद्यते यस्य विमानं शोणितं तथा । सेनापत्यं महच् चायुर् अर्थलाभं तथैव च ॥
68.2.m: Or if one's head is cut off, [or one sees] an aerial chariot, or blood: / commander-in-chief, long life, and similarly the acquisition of wealth;

68.2.s: vibhūṣaṇaṃ ca vidyāṃ ca karṇachedam avāpnuyāt | hastachede labhet putraṃ bāhuchede dhanāgamam ||
68.2.d: विभूषणं च विद्यां च कर्णछेदम् अवाप्नुयात् । हस्तछेदे लभेत् पुत्रं बाहुछेदे धनागमम् ॥
68.2.m: and one obtains an ornament, knowledge, and the cutting off of an ear; / upon the cutting off of a hand he obtains a son, upon the cutting off of an arm the arrival of wealth;

68.2.s: uraḥ sahasralābhaḥ syāt pādachede tathaiva ca | uraḥprajananachede atyantaṃ sukhaṃ dedhate ||
68.2.d: उरः सहस्रलाभः स्यात् पादछेदे तथैव च । उरःप्रजननछेदे अत्यन्तं सुखं देधते ॥
68.2.m: upon [cutting of] the chest there is gain of a thousand, and likewise upon the cutting of a foot; / upon the cutting of the chest and generative organ, supreme happiness increases.

68.2.s: chatrādarśaphaloṣṇīṣaśuklamālyāgame tathā | matsyamāṃsadadhikṣīrarudhirāgama eva ca ||
68.2.d: छत्रादर्शफलोष्णीषशुक्लमाल्यागमे तथा । मत्स्यमांसदधिक्षीररुधिरागम एव च ॥
68.2.m: Likewise, upon the arrival of an umbrella, mirror, fruit, turban, or white garland, / and upon the arrival of fish, meat, curd, milk, or blood;

68.2.s: śaktyaṅkuśapatākānāṃ chattrāsidhanuṣāṃ tathā | vimalānāṃ jalānāṃ ca pūrvoktaṃ tu nidarśanam ||
68.2.d: शक्त्यङ्कुशपताकानां छत्त्रासिधनुषां तथा । विमलानां जलानां च पूर्वोक्तं तु निदर्शनम् ॥
68.2.m: and likewise of spears, elephant-goads, banners, umbrellas, swords, and bows, / and of clear waters—this is the indication previously mentioned.

68.2.s: sūkarakharavāhyānāṃ vadhaś caikapaśor api | narayuktasya yānasya nikṣiptasya gavasya ca ||
68.2.d: सूकरखरवाह्यानां वधश् चैकपशोर् अपि । नरयुक्तस्य यानस्य निक्षिप्तस्य गवस्य च ॥
68.2.m: The killing of riding-beasts such as pigs and donkeys, or even of a single livestock animal, / of a conveyance yoked to a human, or of an abandoned cow;

68.2.s: darśanaṃ cāpy adṛṣṭānām agamyāgamanaṃ tathā | kṣīriṇāṃ phalamvṛkṣāṇāṃ darśanārohaṇāni ca ||
68.2.d: दर्शनं चाप्य् अदृष्टानाम् अगम्यागमनं तथा । क्षीरिणां फलम्वृक्षाणां दर्शनारोहणानि च ॥
68.2.m: and the sight of things not previously seen, approaching forbidden women, / and the sight of and climbing onto milk-yielding and fruit-bearing trees;

68.2.s: viṣadarśanadaṃsparśo dhānyenotsaṅgapūraṇam | dasyubhir hanyamānasya rudataḥ pratibodhanam ||
68.2.d: विषदर्शनदंस्पर्शो धान्येनोत्सङ्गपूरणम् । दस्युभिर् हन्यमानस्य रुदतः प्रतिबोधनम् ॥
68.2.m: the sight and touch of poison, filling one's lap with grain, / waking up while crying out when being beaten by robbers;

68.2.s: dvijebhyo dadhimāṃsasya lābhaḥ piśitabhakṣane | abhakṣyabhakṣaṇe cāpu śvetamālyānulepanam ||
68.2.d: द्विजेभ्यो दधिमांसस्य लाभः पिशितभक्षने । अभक्ष्यभक्षणे चापु श्वेतमाल्यानुलेपनम् ॥
68.2.m: the gain of curd and meat from twice-born men, eating raw flesh, / and upon eating what is unfit to eat, [wearing] a white garland and ointment;

68.2.s: ghātanaṃ śvāpadānāṃ ca pāṇau ca rudhirāgamaḥ | arthalābhāya boddhavyaḥ suhṛnmitrasamāgamaḥ ||
68.2.d: घातनं श्वापदानां च पाणौ च रुधिरागमः । अर्थलाभाय बोद्धव्यः सुहृन्मित्रसमागमः ॥
68.2.m: the killing of beasts of prey, and the arrival of blood in the hand— / this is to be understood as leading to the acquisition of wealth, as is reunion with good friends and allies.

68.2.s: labhate nātra saṃdeho bhārgavasya vaco tathā | śuklāḥ sumanasaḥ kanyā dadhi gobrāhmaṇaṃ vṛṣam ||
68.2.d: लभते नात्र संदेहो भार्गवस्य वचो तथा । शुक्लाः सुमनसः कन्या दधि गोब्राह्मणं वृषम् ॥
68.2.m: He obtains [wealth], there is no doubt about this; thus is the word of Bhārgava. / White flowers, a maiden, curd, a cow, a Brahmin, a bull,

68.2.s: daivatāni nṛpādhyakṣāḥ pāṇḍurāṇi gṛhāṇi ca | suhṛdaḥ saphalā vṛkṣā nakṣatrāṇy amalaṃ jalam ||
68.2.d: दैवतानि नृपाध्यक्षाः पाण्डुराणि गृहाणि च । सुहृदः सफला वृक्षा नक्षत्राण्य् अमलं जलम् ॥
68.2.m: deities, royal overseers, pale-white houses, / friends, fruitful trees, lunar mansions, clear water,

68.2.s: iṣṭakalyāṇaśabdāś ca śuklāmbaradharāḥ striyaḥ | nabho vimalanakṣatraṃ pāvakaṃ viṣamārciṣam ||
68.2.d: इष्टकल्याणशब्दाश् च शुक्लाम्बरधराः स्त्रियः । नभो विमलनक्षत्रं पावकं विषमार्चिषम् ॥
68.2.m: auspicious and agreeable sounds, women wearing white garments, / a sky with bright lunar mansions, a fire with irregular flames—

68.2.s: dṛṣṭvā yas tatkṣaṇaṃ budhyet tasya kalyāṇam ādiśet | vṛkṣān gulmāṃś ca vallīś ca svagṛhe puṣpitā naraḥ ||
68.2.d: दृष्ट्वा यस् तत्क्षणं बुध्येत् तस्य कल्याणम् आदिशेत् । वृक्षान् गुल्मांश् च वल्लीश् च स्वगृहे पुष्पिता नरः ॥
68.2.m: having seen [these], if one wakes up that very moment, one should predict good fortune for him. / A man [seeing] trees, shrubs, and creepers blossoming in his own house,

68.2.s: śuklavāsāḥ striyaś cāpi yaḥ paśyec chrīs tu taṃ bhajet | viṣaśoṇitadigdhāṅgaḥ prītīm āpnoti mānavaḥ ||
68.2.d: शुक्लवासाः स्त्रियश् चापि यः पश्येच् छ्रीस् तु तं भजेत् । विषशोणितदिग्धाङ्गः प्रीतीम् आप्नोति मानवः ॥
68.2.m: and whoever sees women wearing white garments: Fortune attends him. / A man whose limbs are smeared with poison and blood attains joy.

68.2.s: dīptāṅgo labhate bhūmiṃ vardhamānāṅga eva ca | parivāryābhirudito bāndhavaiḥ karuṇaṃ naraḥ ||
68.2.d: दीप्ताङ्गो लभते भूमिं वर्धमानाङ्ग एव च । परिवार्याभिरुदितो बान्धवैः करुणं नरः ॥
68.2.m: One whose limbs are blazing gains land, as does one whose limbs are growing. / A man who, surrounded by kinsmen, is mourned piteously,

68.2.s: śokārto labhate tuṣṭiṃ mṛtaś cāyur avāpnuyāt | śuklamālyāmbaradharo dahyamānaḥ pralīyate ||
68.2.d: शोकार्तो लभते तुष्टिं मृतश् चायुर् अवाप्नुयात् । शुक्लमाल्याम्बरधरो दह्यमानः प्रलीयते ॥
68.2.m: though distressed by grief, attains satisfaction; and one who dies [in a dream] obtains long life. / Wearing a white garland and garments, being burned, one vanishes;

68.2.s: yaḥ svapne saṃbhayed ugraṃ pārakyaṃ so 'rtham āpnuyāt | nāgadantakamudrāṃ ca vīṇāṃ mālāñjanaṃ tathā ||
68.2.d: यः स्वप्ने संभयेद् उग्रं पारक्यं सो ऽर्थम् आप्नुयात् । नागदन्तकमुद्रां च वीणां मालाञ्जनं तथा ॥
68.2.m: he who encounters something terrible in a dream obtains another's wealth. / An ivory signet-ring, a lute, a garland, collyrium,

68.2.s: kāñcanaṃ paśyate yas tu tathā strīṃ labhate naraḥ | uḍḍīyamānān vihagān tathā puṣkariṇīgatān ||
68.2.d: काञ्चनं पश्यते यस् तु तथा स्त्रीं लभते नरः । उड्डीयमानान् विहगान् तथा पुष्करिणीगतान् ॥
68.2.m: and gold: a man who sees these likewise obtains a woman. / Birds flying up and likewise gone to a lotus pond—

68.2.s: mattaṃ kareṇum āruhya parastrīṃ labhate naraḥ | kumārīṃ labhate nārīm āyasair nigaḍair naraḥ ||
68.2.d: मत्तं करेणुम् आरुह्य परस्त्रीं लभते नरः । कुमारीं लभते नारीम् आयसैर् निगडैर् नरः ॥
68.2.m: having mounted an elephant cow in rut, a man obtains another's wife; / bound with iron fetters, a man obtains a maiden as his wife.

68.2.s: baddhvā navāṃ tu yo mālām utpālānāṃ vibudhyate | kavāṭale ca saṃyukte tathaivotpalahastake ||
68.2.d: बद्ध्वा नवां तु यो मालाम् उत्पालानां विबुध्यते । कवाटले च संयुक्ते तथैवोत्पलहस्तके ॥
68.2.m: He who wakes up having bound a new garland of blue lotuses, / or when folding-doors are joined together, or with blue lotuses in his hand,

68.2.s: bhṛṅgāro darpaṇo vāpi labdhvā putrāgamaṃ vadet | taḍāgārāmakūpānāṃ purārañjanayor api ||
68.2.d: भृङ्गारो दर्पणो वापि लब्ध्वा पुत्रागमं वदेत् । तडागारामकूपानां पुरारञ्जनयोर् अपि ॥
68.2.m: or having obtained a water-jug or a mirror, one should declare the arrival of a son. / Of reservoirs, pleasure-gardens, wells, cities, and pleasure-parks,

68.2.s: pūrṇakumbhasya cādeśyaṃ varṣam uttaraṇād bhruvam | cipiṭaḥ kālako nagnaḥ śravaṇo mehate yadi ||
68.2.d: पूर्णकुम्भस्य चादेश्यं वर्षम् उत्तरणाद् भ्रुवम् । चिपिटः कालको नग्नः श्रवणो मेहते यदि ॥
68.2.m: and of a full jar, rain is certainly to be predicted upon crossing over. / If a flat-nosed, black, naked, earless man urinates,

68.2.s: vidikthaḥ sravate cārmiḥ svapne varṣaṃ samādiśet | sūkarīṃ mahiṣīṃ vāpi hastinīṃ śakunīṃ tathā ||
68.2.d: विदिक्थः स्रवते चार्मिः स्वप्ने वर्षं समादिशेत् । सूकरीं महिषीं वापि हस्तिनीं शकुनीं तथा ॥
68.2.m: and if a wave flows in an intermediate quarter, one should predict rain in a dream. / When a sow, a female buffalo, a cow-elephant, or a bird

68.2.s: svapne yadā prasūyeta subhikṣaṃ nirdiśet tadā | śayanāsanayānāni gṛhagrāmapurāṇi ca ||
68.2.d: स्वप्ने यदा प्रसूयेत सुभिक्षं निर्दिशेत् तदा । शयनासनयानानि गृहग्रामपुराणि च ॥
68.2.m: gives birth in a dream, one should then predict abundance of food. / Couches, seats, vehicles, houses, villages, and towns—

68.2.s: yeṣāṃ svapne pralīyante teṣāṃ vṛddhim athādiśet | govṛṣaṃ puruṣaṃ vṛkṣaṃ hastinaṃ parvataṃ gṛham ||
68.2.d: येषां स्वप्ने प्रलीयन्ते तेषां वृद्धिम् अथादिशेत् । गोवृषं पुरुषं वृक्षं हस्तिनं पर्वतं गृहम् ॥
68.2.m: those whose [possessions] vanish in a dream, for them one should then predict increase. / A bull, a man, a tree, an elephant, a mountain, a house:

68.2.s: narasyārohaṇād vṛddhiḥ pāṇḍurāṇi viśeṣataḥ | daivatāni dvijā gāvaḥ pitaro liṅgino grahāḥ ||
68.2.d: नरस्यारोहणाद् वृद्धिः पाण्डुराणि विशेषतः । दैवतानि द्विजा गावः पितरो लिङ्गिनो ग्रहाः ॥
68.2.m: from a man mounting these comes increase, especially if they are pale-white. / Deities, twice-born men, cows, ancestors, ascetics, and planets—

68.2.s: yad vadanti naraṃ svapne tat tathaiva vinirdiśet | saritsarasamudrāṇāṃ taraṇe śokatāraṇam ||
68.2.d: यद् वदन्ति नरं स्वप्ने तत् तथैव विनिर्दिशेत् । सरित्सरसमुद्राणां तरणे शोकतारणम् ॥
68.2.m: whatever they say to a man in a dream, one should declare it to be just so. / In the crossing of rivers, lakes, and oceans lies the crossing over sorrow.

68.2.s: narasya śoṇitaṃ pītvā prakṛtāṇl labhate naraḥ | candrendradhvajasūryāṇāṃ patane nṛpater bhayam ||
68.2.d: नरस्य शोणितं पीत्वा प्रकृताण्ल् लभते नरः । चन्द्रेन्द्रध्वजसूर्याणां पतने नृपतेर् भयम् ॥
68.2.m: Having drunk human blood, a man obtains subjects. / At the falling of the moon, Indra’s banner, or the sun, there is danger for the king.

68.2.s: mahārṇavamahendrāṇāṃ kṣobhe kṣobhaṃ vinirdiśet | keśaśmaśrunakhānāṃ ca patane śokasaṃbhavaḥ ||
68.2.d: महार्णवमहेन्द्राणां क्षोभे क्षोभं विनिर्दिशेत् । केशश्मश्रुनखानां च पतने शोकसंभवः ॥
68.2.m: At the agitation of the great ocean or of great mountains, one should predict disturbance. / And at the falling of hair, beard, or nails, the arising of sorrow [is indicated].

68.2.s: kṛmiṇatvaṃ bhaved dhanyaṃ kroṣṭuker vacanaṃ yathā | kravyādair damṣṭribhiś cāpi vināśo bhūtavigrahe ||
68.2.d: कृमिणत्वं भवेद् धन्यं क्रोष्टुकेर् वचनं यथा । क्रव्यादैर् दम्ष्ट्रिभिश् चापि विनाशो भूतविग्रहे ॥
68.2.m: Being infested with worms is auspicious, according to the word of Kroṣṭuki. / And through carnivorous animals and tusked beasts, destruction occurs in physical combat.

68.2.s: śastramuṣṭiprahāreṣu vijānīyāj jvarāgamam | yadyad ujjvalavad dravyaṃ tattat sukhakaraṃ bhavet ||
68.2.d: शस्त्रमुष्टिप्रहारेषु विजानीयाज् ज्वरागमम् । यद्यद् उज्ज्वलवद् द्रव्यं तत्तत् सुखकरं भवेत् ॥
68.2.m: In blows with weapons or fists, one should know the arrival of fever. / Whatever substance is radiant, that brings happiness.

68.2.s: yadyad virudhyate vāpi svapne tat tasya nirdiśet | nopānena prajātānāṃ darśane sthānam ādiśet ||
68.2.d: यद्यद् विरुध्यते वापि स्वप्ने तत् तस्य निर्दिशेत् । नोपानेन प्रजातानां दर्शने स्थानम् आदिशेत् ॥
68.2.m: Or whatever opposes [one] in a dream, one should predict that for him. / At the sight of those born [without shoes], one should indicate [loss of] place.

68.2.s: upānahabalachattradarśane ca grhe tathā | hasadbhir vā parivṛto nṛtyadbhiḥ svajanair api ||
68.2.d: उपानहबलछत्त्रदर्शने च ग्र्हे तथा । हसद्भिर् वा परिवृतो नृत्यद्भिः स्वजनैर् अपि ॥
68.2.m: And at the sight of shoes, offerings, or an umbrella in the house, / or surrounded by laughing and dancing kinsmen,

68.2.s: saṃyuktaṃ sūkarakharair uṣṭraiḥ kṛṣṇacatuṣpadaiḥ | ratham āruhya yo yāyād akṣatas tu yugaṃdharaḥ ||
68.2.d: संयुक्तं सूकरखरैर् उष्ट्रैः कृष्णचतुष्पदैः । रथम् आरुह्य यो यायाद् अक्षतस् तु युगंधरः ॥
68.2.m: yoked with pigs, donkeys, camels, or black quadrupeds, / he who would ride a chariot, but the yoke-bearer is unbroken,

68.2.s: prakīrṇakeśo hriyate dakṣiṇenāpareṇa vā | dakṣiṇenāgatā kanyā kālikākulavāsinī ||
68.2.d: प्रकीर्णकेशो ह्रियते दक्षिणेनापरेण वा । दक्षिणेनागता कन्या कालिकाकुलवासिनी ॥
68.2.m: with disheveled hair, is carried off to the south or another [direction], / or a maiden arrives from the south, wearing black and dark garments,

68.2.s: nīyate puruṣair yaś ca pāśahastair viśeṣataḥ | nirastānāṃ viṣamāṇāṃ pretenākuśalaṃ bhavet ||
68.2.d: नीयते पुरुषैर् यश् च पाशहस्तैर् विशेषतः । निरस्तानां विषमाणां प्रेतेनाकुशलं भवेत् ॥
68.2.m: and he who is led away especially by men with nooses in hand— / through a dead person, misfortune occurs for those who are overthrown and distressed.

68.2.s: piṇyākasya tilānāṃ ca karṣāsu lavaṇasya ca | rūḍhaśmaśrunakhānāṃ ca duścelānāṃ ca vāsasām ||
68.2.d: पिण्याकस्य तिलानां च कर्षासु लवणस्य च । रूढश्मश्रुनखानां च दुश्चेलानां च वाससाम् ॥
68.2.m: At [the sight of] oil-cake, sesame seeds, salt in pits, / overgrown beard and nails, ragged garments,

68.2.s: virāgavāsasāṃ vāpi vikṛtānāṃ tathaiva ca | sarīsṛpāṇāṃ vyālānāṃ śatrūṇāṃ cāpi darśanam ||
68.2.d: विरागवाससां वापि विकृतानां तथैव च । सरीसृपाणां व्यालानां शत्रूणां चापि दर्शनम् ॥
68.2.m: or discolored clothes, and likewise deformed things, / and the sight of crawling insects, wild beasts, and enemies,

68.2.s: kṛṣṇānāṃ vāpi sarveṣāṃ rājadvijavṛṣād ṛte | darśanaṃ gamanaṃ vāpi śokam āyāsavedanam ||
68.2.d: कृष्णानां वापि सर्वेषां राजद्विजवृषाद् ऋते । दर्शनं गमनं वापि शोकम् आयासवेदनम् ॥
68.2.m: or all black things, except for kings, Brahmins, and bulls, / the sight or departure [of these] brings sorrow and the pain of fatigue.

68.2.s: padmair vā jalabhāṇḍair vā krīḍitāyāsadarśanam | padmāni vāharet svapne hastachedam avāpnuyāt ||
68.2.d: पद्मैर् वा जलभाण्डैर् वा क्रीडितायासदर्शनम् । पद्मानि वाहरेत् स्वप्ने हस्तछेदम् अवाप्नुयात् ॥
68.2.m: The sight of playing with lotuses or water pots brings distress; / or if one plucks lotuses in a dream, he will suffer amputation of the hands.

68.2.s: prasanne tu dhruvaṃ śoko rajjuchede mriyeta saḥ | rūḍhasya srotasā śoko mṛtyuḥ sriotasi naśyataḥ ||
68.2.d: प्रसन्ने तु ध्रुवं शोको रज्जुछेदे म्रियेत सः । रूढस्य स्रोतसा शोको मृत्युः स्रिओतसि नश्यतः ॥
68.2.m: If it is clear, however, sorrow is certain; if the rope is cut, he dies. / For one carried off by a stream, sorrow [arises]; death [arises] for one perishing in a stream.

68.2.s: dantā bāhuṃ tathā śīrṣṇo chinnāṃśadravyadarśanam | bhrātaraṃ pitaraṃ vāpi putraṃ vā nāśayanti te ||
68.2.d: दन्ता बाहुं तथा शीर्ष्णो छिन्नांशद्रव्यदर्शनम् । भ्रातरं पितरं वापि पुत्रं वा नाशयन्ति ते ॥
68.2.m: Teeth, an arm, and the sight of fragments of the head severed— / these destroy a brother, a father, or a son.

68.2.s: dvāre vā sārgale vāpi śayyāṃ śakhāṃ tathaiva ca | svapne yasya pranaśyanti bhāryā tasya vinaśyati ||
68.2.d: द्वारे वा सार्गले वापि शय्यां शखां तथैव च । स्वप्ने यस्य प्रनश्यन्ति भार्या तस्य विनश्यति ॥
68.2.m: In a door, or on a bolt, on a bed, or on a branch, / for him whose [things] perish in a dream, his wife perishes.

68.2.s: kṛkalāso vṛko vāpi puruṣo vāpi piṅgalaḥ | śayyāṃ yasyādhirohanti bhāryā tasyāpi duṣyati ||
68.2.d: कृकलासो वृको वापि पुरुषो वापि पिङ्गलः । शय्यां यस्याधिरोहन्ति भार्या तस्यापि दुष्यति ॥
68.2.m: If a chameleon, a wolf, or a tawny-colored man / climbs onto someone’s bed, his wife becomes unfaithful.

68.2.s: svapne yo mārayet sarpaṃ śvetapītakalohitam | kṛṣṇasya vā śiraś chindyāt putras tasya vinaśyati ||
68.2.d: स्वप्ने यो मारयेत् सर्पं श्वेतपीतकलोहितम् । कृष्णस्य वा शिरश् छिन्द्यात् पुत्रस् तस्य विनश्यति ॥
68.2.m: He who slays in a dream a white, yellow, or red snake, / or cuts off the head of a black one, his son perishes.

68.2.s: rājaputraś ca coraś ca rājabhṛṭyaś ca yo bhavet | tasya svapnāḥ phalaṃ dadyur eteṣu yad udāhṛtam ||
68.2.d: राजपुत्रश् च चोरश् च राजभृट्यश् च यो भवेत् । तस्य स्वप्नाः फलं दद्युर् एतेषु यद् उदाहृतम् ॥
68.2.m: A prince, a thief, or he who is a king’s servant— / for him, dreams bear the fruit that has been declared in these [verses].

68.2.s: yeṣāṃ lābhe bhaved vṛddhis teṣāṃ nāśe guṇo bhavet | yeṣāṃ lābhe bhaved dhānis teṣāṃ lābhe guṇo bhavet ||
68.2.d: येषां लाभे भवेद् वृद्धिस् तेषां नाशे गुणो भवेत् । येषां लाभे भवेद् धानिस् तेषां लाभे गुणो भवेत् ॥
68.2.m: Those things whose gain brings increase, their loss brings benefit; / those things whose gain brings harm, their gain brings benefit.

68.2.s: śubhaṃ dṛṣṭvā tu yaḥ svapne punaḥ paśyaty apūjitam | śubhaṃ vāpy aśubhaṃ vāpi yat paścāt tatphalaṃ labhet ||
68.2.d: शुभं दृष्ट्वा तु यः स्वप्ने पुनः पश्यत्य् अपूजितम् । शुभं वाप्य् अशुभं वापि यत् पश्चात् तत्फलं लभेत् ॥
68.2.m: Having seen an auspicious [dream], he who again sees an unhonored [inauspicious one] / —whether auspicious or inauspicious—he obtains the fruit of whichever comes last.

68.2.s: svapnās tu prathame yāme saṃvatsaravipākinaḥ | dvitīye 'ṣṭasu māseṣu tṛtīye tu tadardhabhāk ||
68.2.d: स्वप्नास् तु प्रथमे यामे संवत्सरविपाकिनः । द्वितीये ऽष्टसु मासेषु तृतीये तु तदर्धभाक् ॥
68.2.m: Dreams in the first watch ripen in a year; / in the second, in eight months; in the third, in half that time.

68.2.s: māsiko govisarge tu sadyaḥpākaḥ prabhātike | kālaḥ pañcasv avasthāsu śarvaryāḥ kīrtitaḥ pṛthak ||
68.2.d: मासिको गोविसर्गे तु सद्यःपाकः प्रभातिके । कालः पञ्चस्व् अवस्थासु शर्वर्याः कीर्तितः पृथक् ॥
68.2.m: At the letting loose of the cattle, it ripens in a month; at dawn, it ripens immediately. / The time during the five phases of the night has been proclaimed separately.

68.2.s: viprebhyaḥ śaktito dānaṃ śāntiḥ svaṣṭyayanādayaḥ | vināśayanti duḥsvapnaṃ prātaś cāśvatthasevanam ||
68.2.d: विप्रेभ्यः शक्तितो दानं शान्तिः स्वष्ट्ययनादयः । विनाशयन्ति दुःस्वप्नं प्रातश् चाश्वत्थसेवनम् ॥
68.2.m: Giving to Brahmins according to one’s ability, propitiatory rites, auspicious benedictions, and the like / destroy a bad dream, as does worshiping the sacred fig tree in the morning.

68.2.s: aśvatthasevā tilapātradānaṃ gosparśanaṃ brāhmaṇatarpaṇaṃ ca | śāntikriyā svastyayanakriyā ca duḥsvapnam etāni vināśayanti ||
68.2.d: अश्वत्थसेवा तिलपात्रदानं गोस्पर्शनं ब्राह्मणतर्पणं च । शान्तिक्रिया स्वस्त्ययनक्रिया च दुःस्वप्नम् एतानि विनाशयन्ति ॥
68.2.m: Worship of the sacred fig tree, the gift of a vessel of sesame, touching a cow, satisfying Brahmins, / the performance of propitiatory rites, and the performance of benedictions—these destroy a bad dream.

68.2.s: vasnakanakadānadevapūjāgurugoṣṭhaniṣevitāni kuryuḥ | dvijavṛṣabḥgavāśvapārthivānāṃ darśanam itihāsamaṅgalāḥ syuḥ ||
68.2.d: वस्नकनकदानदेवपूजागुरुगोष्ठनिषेवितानि कुर्युः । द्विजवृषब्ःगवाश्वपार्थिवानां दर्शनम् इतिहासमङ्गलाः स्युः ॥
68.2.m: They should make gifts of cloth and gold, worship the gods, and frequent the teacher’s cow-pen; / seeing twice-borns, bulls, cows, horses, and kings, they should hear auspicious legends.

68.3.s: imān dṛṣṭvāśubhān svapnān prātar utthāya satvaraḥ | nadīsaṃgamatoyena mukhaṃ saṃmārjya tattvataḥ ||
68.3.d: इमान् दृष्ट्वाशुभान् स्वप्नान् प्रातर् उत्थाय सत्वरः । नदीसंगमतोयेन मुखं संमार्ज्य तत्त्वतः ॥
68.3.m: Having seen these inauspicious dreams, rising early in the morning in haste, / and properly washing his face with water from a river confluence,

68.3.s: hiraṇyavarṇābhir udakaṃ śaṃtātīyamayobhuvā | abhimantrya prayatnena mukhaṃ saṃmārjya tattvataḥ ||
68.3.d: हिरण्यवर्णाभिर् उदकं शंतातीयमयोभुवा । अभिमन्त्र्य प्रयत्नेन मुखं संमार्ज्य तत्त्वतः ॥
68.3.m: having consecrated the water with care using the [hymns] *Hiraṇyavarṇāḥ*, *Śaṃtātīya*, and *Mayobhū*, / and properly wiping his face,

68.3.s: yo na jīvaḥ paro 'pehi vidma te svapna vedanam | rocanā sarṣapā mṛdā samit sakusumaṃ dadhi ||
68.3.d: यो न जीवः परो ऽपेहि विद्म ते स्वप्न वेदनम् । रोचना सर्षपा मृदा समित् सकुसुमं दधि ॥
68.3.m: and [reciting] “Depart, you who are not living... we know your dream-pain,” / [with] yellow orpiment, mustard, earth, sacrificial kindling, flowers, curd,

68.3.s: gām ajaṃ kanakaṃ sattvaṃ kumārīṃ brāhmaṇaṃ śubham | abhivandya nṛpo yāyāt suhṛdāṃś ca manoharān ||
68.3.d: गाम् अजं कनकं सत्त्वं कुमारीं ब्राह्मणं शुभम् । अभिवन्द्य नृपो यायात् सुहृदांश् च मनोहरान् ॥
68.3.m: having saluted a cow, a goat, gold, an animal, a maiden, an auspicious Brahmin, / and pleasing friends, the king should proceed.

68.3.s: yadā tu yātrāṃ nṛpatiḥ kartum icched vidhānavit | atha svastyayanaiḥ saumyaiḥ saumyais tam abhimantrayet ||
68.3.d: यदा तु यात्रां नृपतिः कर्तुम् इच्छेद् विधानवित् । अथ स्वस्त्ययनैः सौम्यैः सौम्यैस् तम् अभिमन्त्रयेत् ॥
68.3.m: When a king who knows the ordinance desires to set out on an expedition, / he should then consecrate him with gentle, benevolent benedictions.

68.3.s: tataḥ śuklāmbaradharo vāgyataḥ saṃyatendriyaḥ | tāṃ niśaṃ saṃviśed rājā bhūmau caivābhimantrayet ||
68.3.d: ततः शुक्लाम्बरधरो वाग्यतः संयतेन्द्रियः । तां निशं संविशेद् राजा भूमौ चैवाभिमन्त्रयेत् ॥
68.3.m: Then, clad in white garments, with speech restrained and senses controlled, / the king should lie down on the ground for that night and consecrate [it],

68.3.s: anyathaiva hi na svapnadarśanārthanidarśanam | evam uktvā narapatiḥ prayatātmā tataḥ svapet ||
68.3.d: अन्यथैव हि न स्वप्नदर्शनार्थनिदर्शनम् । एवम् उक्त्वा नरपतिः प्रयतात्मा ततः स्वपेत् ॥
68.3.m: [saying: “Otherwise, there is no revelation of the meaning of dream visions.”] / Having spoken thus, the king, pure in mind, should then sleep.

68.3.s: praśastasvapnatāṃ dṛṣṭvā tato yāyān narādhipaḥ | svapneṣu vāpraśastreṣu tataḥ śāntiṃ samārabhet ||
68.3.d: प्रशस्तस्वप्नतां दृष्ट्वा ततो यायान् नराधिपः । स्वप्नेषु वाप्रशस्त्रेषु ततः शान्तिं समारभेत् ॥
68.3.m: Having seen an auspicious dream, the lord of men should then march forth. / Or if the dreams are inauspicious, he should then undertake a propitiatory rite:

68.3.s: māhendrīm amṛtāṃ raudrīṃ kuryād vāpy aparājitām | kauberīṃ vā prayuñjīta ādityāṃ vā sadakṣiṇām ||
68.3.d: माहेन्द्रीम् अमृतां रौद्रीं कुर्याद् वाप्य् अपराजिताम् । कौबेरीं वा प्रयुञ्जीत आदित्यां वा सदक्षिणाम् ॥
68.3.m: He should perform the Māhendrī, Amṛtā, Raudrī, or the Aparājitā; / or he should employ the Kauberī, or the Ādityā with a sacrificial fee.

68.3.s: rajanikaradivākarau karābhyāṃ spṛśati yadā grasate 'tha vā narendraḥ | lavaṇajalanidhiṃ nadīṃ ca dorbhyāṃ tarati hradāpadakardamaṃ tamo vā ||
68.3.d: रजनिकरदिवाकरौ कराभ्यां स्पृशति यदा ग्रसते ऽथ वा नरेन्द्रः । लवणजलनिधिं नदीं च दोर्भ्यां तरति ह्रदापदकर्दमं तमो वा ॥
68.3.m: When a king touches the moon and the sun with both hands, or swallows them, / or crosses the salt ocean or a river with his arms, or a deep lake, misfortune, mud, or darkness,

68.3.s: naraturagamahīruhān nagān vā bhavanacarān na virohayed gajān vā | jvalanamaraṇakālavṛddhayogān yadi nṛpa ātmagatāṃś ca paśyatīha ||
68.3.d: नरतुरगमहीरुहान् नगान् वा भवनचरान् न विरोहयेद् गजान् वा । ज्वलनमरणकालवृद्धयोगान् यदि नृप आत्मगतांश् च पश्यतीह ॥
68.3.m: or does not climb onto men, horses, trees, mountains, houses, or elephants; / if a king here sees fires, death, conjunctions of time and growth pertaining to himself;

68.3.s: yadi ca nṛpatir ātmano 'bhracārair bhramati mahīṃ sapurāṃ parikṣipet | yadi ca sa ciramagnagātramātro bhramati nṛpo grasate 'tha medinīṃ vā ||
68.3.d: यदि च नृपतिर् आत्मनो ऽभ्रचारैर् भ्रमति महीं सपुरां परिक्षिपेत् । यदि च स चिरमग्नगात्रमात्रो भ्रमति नृपो ग्रसते ऽथ मेदिनीं वा ॥
68.3.m: and if the king, through his own sky-wandering, wanders the earth and encompasses it along with its cities; / if that king, having his limbs submerged for a long time, roams about, or swallows the earth;

68.3.s: yadi ca jayati damṣṭriṇo narān vā yadi ca bhavet sitamālyadānadhārī | yadi ca ruditi caivam ādi dṛṣṭvā paraviṣayaṃ hṛṣitas tatas tu yāyāt ||
68.3.d: यदि च जयति दम्ष्ट्रिणो नरान् वा यदि च भवेत् सितमाल्यदानधारी । यदि च रुदिति चैवम् आदि दृष्ट्वा परविषयं हृषितस् ततस् तु यायात् ॥
68.3.m: and if he conquers tusked beasts or men, or wears a gift of white garlands, / or if he weeps—having seen such dreams, he should then march against the enemy’s territory rejoicing.

68.4.s: sa kaluṣasalilāvapāṃsumagno madhughṛtatailavasāpradigdhagātraḥ | malinavasanajīrṇaraktavāsā yadi sumanobhir alaṃkṛtaḥ svayaṃ vā ||
68.4.d: स कलुषसलिलावपांसुमग्नो मधुघृततैलवसाप्रदिग्धगात्रः । मलिनवसनजीर्णरक्तवासा यदि सुमनोभिर् अलंकृतः स्वयं वा ॥
68.4.m: If he is submerged in turbid water or dust, his limbs smeared with honey, ghee, oil, or fat, / clad in soiled, worn, or red garments, or himself adorned with flowers,

68.4.s: svapiti jayati khādati prahṛṣṭo vilapati nartati gāyanaprahāsaiḥ | bhavati ca mudito labheta kanyāṃ yadi nṛpatir nayaśo bhavej jayārthī ||
68.4.d: स्वपिति जयति खादति प्रहृष्टो विलपति नर्तति गायनप्रहासैः । भवति च मुदितो लभेत कन्यां यदि नृपतिर् नयशो भवेज् जयार्थी ॥
68.4.m: if he sleeps, conquers, eats delighted, wails, dances with singers’ laughter, / and becomes joyful, or if the king wins a maiden, he will lack prudence if he seeks victory.

68.4.s: mayakharasūkaravānarādhirūḍho hṛtamukuṭāṅgadavastracihnanagnaḥ | vinihataturagadvipo narendro yadi patitadhvajavāṃs tato na yāyāt ||
68.4.d: मयखरसूकरवानराधिरूढो हृतमुकुटाङ्गदवस्त्रचिह्ननग्नः । विनिहततुरगद्विपो नरेन्द्रो यदि पतितध्वजवांस् ततो न यायात् ॥
68.4.m: Mounted on a donkey, an ass, a pig, or a monkey, naked with his crown, armlets, clothes, and emblems stripped, / his horses and elephants slain, and his banner fallen—if the king [sees this], he should not march forth.

68.4.s: narapatir aparājitaḥ parair yo yadi ca paraiḥ parihasyate madadbhiḥ | yadi ca bhavati durdṛśograrūpo atha na sa īdṛśakaḥ parān prayāyāt ||
68.4.d: नरपतिर् अपराजितः परैर् यो यदि च परैः परिहस्यते मदद्भिः । यदि च भवति दुर्दृशोग्ररूपो अथ न स ईदृशकः परान् प्रयायात् ॥
68.4.m: If a ruler of men, unvanquished by enemies, is mocked by exultant foes, / and if he becomes hard to look upon and terrible in form, then being such a one he must not advance against enemies.

68.4.s: svapnān dṛṣṭvā śubhān rājā japadbhir abhimantritaḥ | yuktaḥ sa śakunair bhūpa utpātagaṇavarjitaḥ ||
68.4.d: स्वप्नान् दृष्ट्वा शुभान् राजा जपद्भिर् अभिमन्त्रितः । युक्तः स शकुनैर् भूप उत्पातगणवर्जितः ॥
68.4.m: Having seen auspicious dreams, consecrated by those who recite prayers, / accompanied by good omens, free from groups of portents, the king—

68.4.s: sahāyavān susaṃnaddho nimittajñaiḥ samanvitaḥ | sumuhūrte sunakṣatre prayāyād vasudhādhipaḥ ||
68.4.d: सहायवान् सुसंनद्धो निमित्तज्ञैः समन्वितः । सुमुहूर्ते सुनक्षत्रे प्रयायाद् वसुधाधिपः ॥
68.4.m: having allies, well-armoured, accompanied by experts in omens, / at an auspicious hour and under an auspicious lunar mansion, the lord of the earth should march out.

68.5.s: tailābhyaktaś ca kṛsarāṃ bhuṅkte tailapariplutām | mātaraṃ praviśed yaś ca jvalitaṃ ca hutāśanam ||
68.5.d: तैलाभ्यक्तश् च कृसरां भुङ्क्ते तैलपरिप्लुताम् । मातरं प्रविशेद् यश् च ज्वलितं च हुताशनम् ॥
68.5.m: And if one smeared with oil eats rice cooked with sesame and flooded with oil, / or enters [his] mother or a blazing fire;

68.5.s: prāsadāt parvatāgrād vā pated yaś cāpi mānavaḥ | magnaḥ kardamakūpeṣu jale yaś cāpi naśyati ||
68.5.d: प्रासदात् पर्वताग्राद् वा पतेद् यश् चापि मानवः । मग्नः कर्दमकूपेषु जले यश् चापि नश्यति ॥
68.5.m: or if a man falls from a palace or a mountain peak, / or is submerged in pits of mire, or drowns in water;

68.5.s: drumam unmūlayed yas tu paśyed rājñopasevakam | kumārīvadane yaś ca vānarīṃ vādhigacchati ||
68.5.d: द्रुमम् उन्मूलयेद् यस् तु पश्येद् राज्ञोपसेवकम् । कुमारीवदने यश् च वानरीं वाधिगच्छति ॥
68.5.m: or if one uproots a tree, or sees a king's servant, / or comes upon a maiden's face, or a female monkey;

68.5.s: raktakaṇṭhagate vāpi yasya kaṇṭhe visarjati | vivarṇo vāpi pāśair yo badhyate mriyate tu saḥ ||
68.5.d: रक्तकण्ठगते वापि यस्य कण्ठे विसर्जति । विवर्णो वापि पाशैर् यो बध्यते म्रियते तु सः ॥
68.5.m: or if on one whose throat is red, [another] discharges upon his throat, / or one who becomes discoloured is bound with nooses: he dies.

68.5.s: kāṃsyaṃ vā kāṃsyapātrīṃ vā yasya tejo 'dhirohati | acireṇaiva kālena so 'sinā vadhyate naraḥ ||
68.5.d: कांस्यं वा कांस्यपात्रीं वा यस्य तेजो ऽधिरोहति । अचिरेणैव कालेन सो ऽसिना वध्यते नरः ॥
68.5.m: Upon whomsoever the gleam of bronze or of a bronze vessel ascends, / in no long time that man is slain with a sword.

68.5.s: yūpāgram adhiruhyātha nāvāgram adhirohati | acireṇaiva kālena śūlāgraṃ so 'dhirohati ||
68.5.d: यूपाग्रम् अधिरुह्याथ नावाग्रम् अधिरोहति । अचिरेणैव कालेन शूलाग्रं सो ऽधिरोहति ॥
68.5.m: If having mounted the top of a sacrificial post, he then mounts the prow of a boat, / in no long time he mounts the top of a stake.

68.5.s: muṇḍaḥ kāṣāyavāso vā śvetaraktapaṭo 'pi vā | svapne yasyādhirohanti vyādhis tasyādhirohati ||
68.5.d: मुण्डः काषायवासो वा श्वेतरक्तपटो ऽपि वा । स्वप्ने यस्याधिरोहन्ति व्याधिस् तस्याधिरोहति ॥
68.5.m: If a shaven-headed man, or one wearing ochre garments, or one wearing a white and red cloth, / mounts upon anyone in a dream, disease mounts upon him.

68.5.s: śvā vā ajagaro godhā tarakṣu śalyako 'pi vā | kṛkalāso rurur vyāghro dvīpī yasyādhirohati ||
68.5.d: श्वा वा अजगरो गोधा तरक्षु शल्यको ऽपि वा । कृकलासो रुरुर् व्याघ्रो द्वीपी यस्याधिरोहति ॥
68.5.m: Upon whomsoever mounts a dog, a python, a monitor lizard, a hyena, or a porcupine, / a chameleon, a ruru-deer, a tiger, or a leopard;

68.5.s: ahiś ca raudrajaṭilaḥ śvetaraktapaṭo 'pi vā | svapne yam upatiṣṭhanti vyādhis tam upatiṣṭhati ||
68.5.d: अहिश् च रौद्रजटिलः श्वेतरक्तपटो ऽपि वा । स्वप्ने यम् उपतिष्ठन्ति व्याधिस् तम् उपतिष्ठति ॥
68.5.m: or a snake, or a fearsome matted-haired ascetic, or one wearing a white and red cloth— / whomever they approach in a dream, disease approaches him.

68.5.s: mahībhasmapradigdhāṅgo nirāvaraṇa eva ca | samasyānāṃ sajātānām utsavānāṃ ca darśanam ||
68.5.d: महीभस्मप्रदिग्धाङ्गो निरावरण एव च । समस्यानां सजातानाम् उत्सवानां च दर्शनम् ॥
68.5.m: Having one's limbs smeared with earth and ashes, and being uncovered; / seeing assemblies, kinsmen, and festivities;

68.5.s: durgam adhvānagamanam anūpānāṃ ca sevanam | abhyaṅgaś caiva gātrāṇāṃ tilagomayakardamaiḥ ||
68.5.d: दुर्गम् अध्वानगमनम् अनूपानां च सेवनम् । अभ्यङ्गश् चैव गात्राणां तिलगोमयकर्दमैः ॥
68.5.m: travelling on an impassable road, and resorting to marshy lands, / and the anointing of one's limbs with sesame, cow dung, and mud;

68.5.s: suvarṇamaṇimuktāni bhūṣaṇaṃ rajatāni ca | darśanaṃ vāpy athaiteṣāṃ vyādhīnāṃ saṃpraveśanam ||
68.5.d: सुवर्णमणिमुक्तानि भूषणं रजतानि च । दर्शनं वाप्य् अथैतेषां व्याधीनां संप्रवेशनम् ॥
68.5.m: gold, gems, pearls, ornaments, and silver— / seeing these is the entrance of diseases.

68.5.s: gāyanaṃ nartanaṃ hāsyaṃ vivāhakaraṇaṃ tathā | ānandaś ca pramodaś ca vyasanasya ca darśanam ||
68.5.d: गायनं नर्तनं हास्यं विवाहकरणं तथा । आनन्दश् च प्रमोदश् च व्यसनस्य च दर्शनम् ॥
68.5.m: Singing, dancing, laughing, and contracting a marriage, / joy and delight: [these are] the sight of disaster.

68.5.s: purāṇaghṛtadigdhāṅgo naro maraṇam āpnuyāt | evam uktā mahotpātā vividhāḥ pūrvacoditaḥ ||
68.5.d: पुराणघृतदिग्धाङ्गो नरो मरणम् आप्नुयात् । एवम् उक्ता महोत्पाता विविधाः पूर्वचोदितः ॥
68.5.m: A man whose limbs are smeared with old clarified butter meets with death. / Thus have been stated the manifold great portents proclaimed earlier.

68.5.s: ulkābhedās tathā pañca pariveṣā nava smṛtāḥ | digdāho 'ṣṭavidhaḥ prokto vidyud aṣṭavidhā tathā ||
68.5.d: उल्काभेदास् तथा पञ्च परिवेषा नव स्मृताः । दिग्दाहो ऽष्टविधः प्रोक्तो विद्युद् अष्टविधा तथा ॥
68.5.m: There are five varieties of meteors, and nine halos are recorded; / the burning of the quarters is declared to be eightfold, and lightning likewise eightfold;

68.5.s: catvāro bhūmikampāś ca nirghāto 'ṣṭavidhas tathā | viṃśatī dve ca vijñeyā bhedā hy ulkādiṣu smṛtāḥ ||
68.5.d: चत्वारो भूमिकम्पाश् च निर्घातो ऽष्टविधस् तथा । विंशती द्वे च विज्ञेया भेदा ह्य् उल्कादिषु स्मृताः ॥
68.5.m: and four earthquakes, and meteoric thunder is eightfold; / forty-two divisions are remembered regarding meteors and the like.

68.5.s: mahotpātāś ca bahavaḥ śāntiyogeṣu kīrtitāḥ | teṣu sarveṣu vidhivac chāntikāmo narādhipaḥ ||
68.5.d: महोत्पाताश् च बहवः शान्तियोगेषु कीर्तिताः । तेषु सर्वेषु विधिवच् छान्तिकामो नराधिपः ॥
68.5.m: And many great portents have been proclaimed in the rites of propitiation. / In all of them, desiring propitiation according to the rule, the ruler of men—

68.5.s: atharvāṇaṃ ca vṛṇuyāt sarvaśāstravidaṃ nṛpaḥ | sa vṛto bhayabhītena śamanārthaṃ mahātmanā ||
68.5.d: अथर्वाणं च वृणुयात् सर्वशास्त्रविदं नृपः । स वृतो भयभीतेन शमनार्थं महात्मना ॥
68.5.m: the king should choose an Atharvan priest who knows all scriptures. / Having been chosen by the great-souled [king] alarmed by fear, for the sake of pacification,

68.5.s: prajānām abhayaṃ samyag dāpayet pṛthivīpatiḥ | anantaraṃ gavāṃ pūjā brāhmaṇānāṃ viśeṣataḥ ||
68.5.d: प्रजानाम् अभयं सम्यग् दापयेत् पृथिवीपतिः । अनन्तरं गवां पूजा ब्राह्मणानां विशेषतः ॥
68.5.m: the lord of the earth should properly grant freedom from fear to the subjects. / Immediately after, worship of cows, and especially of brāhmaṇas [should be performed].

68.5.s: devatāyatane sadyo dohān bhūmau prakārayet | satataṃ cānulipyas tu puṣpair dhūpair yathoditaiḥ ||
68.5.d: देवतायतने सद्यो दोहान् भूमौ प्रकारयेत् । सततं चानुलिप्यस् तु पुष्पैर् धूपैर् यथोदितैः ॥
68.5.m: In a temple, he should immediately cause milkings to be made upon the ground; / and [the place] should be continuously anointed, with flowers and incenses as prescribed,

68.5.s: pradīpair vividhaiḥ śubhraiḥ sarvadikṣuprakalpitaiḥ | tathā balyupahāraiś ca pāyasāpūpasaṃyutaiḥ ||
68.5.d: प्रदीपैर् विविधैः शुभ्रैः सर्वदिक्षुप्रकल्पितैः । तथा बल्युपहारैश् च पायसापूपसंयुतैः ॥
68.5.m: with manifold bright lamps arranged in all directions, / and likewise with offerings of tribute accompanied by rice boiled in milk and barley-cakes,

68.5.s: hṛdyair bahuvidhair bhakṣaiḥ sarvadikṣuprakalpitaiḥ | tasminn evāntare śānte goṣṭhe vā jalasaṃnidhau ||
68.5.d: हृद्यैर् बहुविधैर् भक्षैः सर्वदिक्षुप्रकल्पितैः । तस्मिन्न् एवान्तरे शान्ते गोष्ठे वा जलसंनिधौ ॥
68.5.m: with manifold agreeable foods arranged in all directions. / Thereupon, in that pacified [shrine], or in a cowpen, or near water,

68.5.s: nirgatya nagarād vāpi śucau deśe samāhitaḥ | vṛṇuyāc chāntitattvajñān utpātavihitāñ śubhān ||
68.5.d: निर्गत्य नगराद् वापि शुचौ देशे समाहितः । वृणुयाच् छान्तितत्त्वज्ञान् उत्पातविहिताञ् शुभान् ॥
68.5.m: or having departed from the city, concentrated in a pure place, / he should choose auspicious [priests] who know the truth of propitiatory rites and are versed in portents.

68.5.s: ṣoḍaśāṣṭau vṛtās te ca puraścaraṇaśodhitāḥ | aṅgāni kuryur anye ca śatasaṃkhyā dvijottamāḥ ||
68.5.d: षोडशाष्टौ वृतास् ते च पुरश्चरणशोधिताः । अङ्गानि कुर्युर् अन्ये च शतसंख्या द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
68.5.m: Chosen are sixteen [priests] or eight, purified by preparatory observances; / and other excellent twice-born, a hundred in number, should perform the ancillary rites.

68.5.s: udayāste sukhāsīnā japaṃ kuryur atandritāḥ | te sadasyā iti proktā vācane yajñakarmaṇi ||
68.5.d: उदयास्ते सुखासीना जपं कुर्युर् अतन्द्रिताः । ते सदस्या इति प्रोक्ता वाचने यज्ञकर्मणि ॥
68.5.m: Sitting comfortably from sunrise to sunset, they should recite unwearied. / They are declared to be the assistants at the recitation during the sacrificial rite.

68.5.s: teṣāṃ variṣṭhaḥ śāntijña upadraṣṭā manoharaḥ | sarvakarmasu vettā ya ānayet so 'py athādarāt ||
68.5.d: तेषां वरिष्ठः शान्तिज्ञ उपद्रष्टा मनोहरः । सर्वकर्मसु वेत्ता य आनयेत् सो ऽप्य् अथादरात् ॥
68.5.m: The best among them, who knows propitiatory rites, a pleasing overseer, / who is conversant with all rituals, he too should bring them respectfully.

68.5.s: bhūmiṃ saṃśodhya vidhivat kṛtvā tatra ca maṇḍapam | vidhivat kalpayed vediṃ yajñapātrāṇi ca svayam ||
68.5.d: भूमिं संशोध्य विधिवत् कृत्वा तत्र च मण्डपम् । विधिवत् कल्पयेद् वेदिं यज्ञपात्राणि च स्वयम् ॥
68.5.m: Having purified the ground according to the rule and made a pavilion there, / he should himself prepare the altar according to the rule, and the sacrificial vessels.

68.5.s: evaṃ yathoktavidhinā agnimanthanapūrvakām | mahāśāntiṃ prayuñjīta sarvopadravanāśinīm ||
68.5.d: एवं यथोक्तविधिना अग्निमन्थनपूर्वकाम् । महाशान्तिं प्रयुञ्जीत सर्वोपद्रवनाशिनीम् ॥
68.5.m: Thus, according to the prescribed rule, preceded by the churning of fire, / he should perform the great propitiatory rite that destroys all calamities.

68.5.s: annair vastraiś ca vividhaiḥ saṃyuktāṃ bahudakṣiṇām | kārayitvā mahāśāntiṃ varaṃ gāṃ ca nivedayet ||
68.5.d: अन्नैर् वस्त्रैश् च विविधैः संयुक्तां बहुदक्षिणाम् । कारयित्वा महाशान्तिं वरं गां च निवेदयेत् ॥
68.5.m: Accompanied by various foods and garments, with abundant sacrificial fee, / having caused the great propitiatory rite to be performed, he should offer an excellent cow,

68.5.s: gṛham ābharaṇaṃ chattram anaḍudvājinaṃ tathā | kuñjaraṃ vā tathā dattvā ghaṇtābharaṇabhūṣitam ||
68.5.d: गृहम् आभरणं छत्त्रम् अनडुद्वाजिनं तथा । कुञ्जरं वा तथा दत्त्वा घण्ताभरणभूषितम् ॥
68.5.m: a house, ornaments, a parasol, an ox, and a horse; / or having given an elephant adorned with bells and ornaments,

68.5.s: mahat sukham avāpnoti kāryasiddhiṃ ca vindati | kāryasiddhiṃ ca vindati ||
68.5.d: महत् सुखम् अवाप्नोति कार्यसिद्धिं च विन्दति । कार्यसिद्धिं च विन्दति ॥
68.5.m: he attains great happiness and finds success in his undertakings, / and finds success in his undertakings.

69.1.s: om upasaṃgamya munayaḥ sarvajñaṃ śāntamānasam | apṛcchan gatamātsyaryaṃ bhṛguṃ brahmavidāṃ varam ||
69.1.d: ओम् उपसंगम्य मुनयः सर्वज्ञं शान्तमानसम् । अपृच्छन् गतमात्स्यर्यं भृगुं ब्रह्मविदां वरम् ॥
69.1.m: Om. Having approached the all-knowing [sage] of calmed mind, / free from malice, the best among knowers of the ultimate reality, the sages asked Bhṛgu:

69.1.s: kāmā hi bahavo loke saṃsthitā bhinnasādhanāḥ | ekam eva paraṃ teṣāṃ samyak tvaṃ brūhy asaṃśayam ||
69.1.d: कामा हि बहवो लोके संस्थिता भिन्नसाधनाः । एकम् एव परं तेषां सम्यक् त्वं ब्रूह्य् असंशयम् ॥
69.1.m: "Many indeed are the desires abiding in the world, with different means of accomplishment; / tell us truly and without doubt of the single supreme among them."

69.1.s: samāsena pravakṣyāmi yena sarvaṃ pradadyate | atipraśno 'yam udgīrṇas tathāpi kathayāmy aham ||
69.1.d: समासेन प्रवक्ष्यामि येन सर्वं प्रदद्यते । अतिप्रश्नो ऽयम् उद्गीर्णस् तथापि कथयाम्य् अहम् ॥
69.1.m: "I shall declare in brief that by which everything is given. / This is an excessive question that has been raised; nevertheless, I shall speak.

69.1.s: sarvārthasādhanārthāya śrutir āṅgirasī hitā | svatejasā prajvalantī hṛdayaṃ tad athārvaṇām ||
69.1.d: सर्वार्थसाधनार्थाय श्रुतिर् आङ्गिरसी हिता । स्वतेजसा प्रज्वलन्ती हृदयं तद् अथार्वणाम् ॥
69.1.m: For the accomplishment of all ends, the beneficial revelation of the Aṅgirases, / blazing with its own splendour—that is the Heart of the Atharvans.

69.1.s: prabhāvaṃ tasya vakṣyāmi upariṣṭād yathāvidhi | duḥsādhyāni nimittāni tāni vedmi hi kāni cit ||
69.1.d: प्रभावं तस्य वक्ष्यामि उपरिष्टाद् यथाविधि । दुःसाध्यानि निमित्तानि तानि वेद्मि हि कानि चित् ॥
69.1.m: I shall declare its power in full sequence, according to the rule; / for I know certain omens that are difficult to remedy:

69.2.s: akāle yasya jāyante dantāḥ keśair vivarjitaḥ | prabhūtalambakeśo vā tathā hīnādhikāṅguliḥ ||
69.2.d: अकाले यस्य जायन्ते दन्ताः केशैर् विवर्जितः । प्रभूतलम्बकेशो वा तथा हीनाधिकाङ्गुलिः ॥
69.2.m: Whose teeth appear untimely, or one devoid of hair, / or having abundant, hanging hair, or having fewer or more fingers;

69.2.s: dvidantaś cāpi jāyeta tasya karma svaśākhikam | svaśākhāyāṃ tu yat proktaṃ kuryād vātharvaṇaṃ vidhim ||
69.2.d: द्विदन्तश् चापि जायेत तस्य कर्म स्वशाखिकम् । स्वशाखायां तु यत् प्रोक्तं कुर्याद् वाथर्वणं विधिम् ॥
69.2.m: or if one is born with two teeth: the ritual for him belongs to his own Vedic branch; / but what is proclaimed in one's own Vedic branch, or one should perform the Atharvan rite;

69.2.s: dvimūrdhā vā trinetro vā tathaikākṣir dvināsikaḥ | hīnahasto 'paro hy arthe na tv atharvaśirāḥ sa ca ||
69.2.d: द्विमूर्धा वा त्रिनेत्रो वा तथैकाक्षिर् द्विनासिकः । हीनहस्तो ऽपरो ह्य् अर्थे न त्व् अथर्वशिराः स च ॥
69.2.m: or two-headed, or three-eyed, or one-eyed, or two-nosed, / or lacking a hand, or deformed in another limb, but not a headless torso;

69.2.s: kṛtopacāraḥ pañca sapta śuddhātmā sādhyasatkṛtaḥ | sa śāntyudakam ācamya śāntavṛkṣasamīpataḥ ||
69.2.d: कृतोपचारः पञ्च सप्त शुद्धात्मा साध्यसत्कृतः । स शान्त्युदकम् आचम्य शान्तवृक्षसमीपतः ॥
69.2.m: having performed the rites five [or] seven [times], pure in self, honoured by the patron, / having sipped propitiatory water in the vicinity of a pacifying tree,

69.2.s: śāntavṛkṣasamidbhis tu tilais trimadhurais tathā | homaṃ kuryād atharvā tu tena nandati satkulam ||
69.2.d: शान्तवृक्षसमिद्भिस् तु तिलैस् त्रिमधुरैस् तथा । होमं कुर्याद् अथर्वा तु तेन नन्दति सत्कुलम् ॥
69.2.m: with the firewood of a pacifying tree, and with sesame, and with the three sweets, / the Atharvan priest should make the oblation; thereby the noble family rejoices.

69.3.s: na labhed yady atharvāṇaṃ kuryād daśaguṇaṃ svayam | mahāvyāhṛtihomaṃ ca sāvitraṃ japam eva ca ||
69.3.d: न लभेद् यद्य् अथर्वाणं कुर्याद् दशगुणं स्वयम् । महाव्याहृतिहोमं च सावित्रं जपम् एव च ॥
69.3.m: If one should not obtain an Atharvan priest, he should himself perform tenfold / the oblation with the great sacred utterances, and the recitation of the verse to Savitṛ.

69.3.s: vikṛtāṅgo 'dhikāṅgo vā jāto hīnāṅgo eva vā | kulasyādbhutam atyarthaṃ tad atharvā śamaṃ nayet ||
69.3.d: विकृताङ्गो ऽधिकाङ्गो वा जातो हीनाङ्गो एव वा । कुलस्याद्भुतम् अत्यर्थं तद् अथर्वा शमं नयेत् ॥
69.3.m: Whether born deformed in limbs, or with superfluous limbs, or with deficient limbs— / that exceedingly grave portent of the family, the Atharvan priest should bring to peace."

69.3.s: kapyuṣṭrebhagavādīnāṃ jāyante 'ṅgamukhaiḥ samāḥ | yasmin rāṣṭre nṛpas tatra ṣaṇmāsādd hi vinaśyati ||
69.3.d: कप्युष्ट्रेभगवादीनां जायन्ते ऽङ्गमुखैः समाः । यस्मिन् राष्ट्रे नृपस् तत्र षण्मासाद्द् हि विनश्यति ॥
69.3.m: In whosever realm [beings] are born resembling monkeys, camels, elephants, cows, and so forth in their limbs or face, / the king there verily perishes within six months.

69.3.s: kapyādayo va jāyante anyasya tulyagātrakāḥ | vṛkṣe 'nyavṛkṣajaṃ puṣpaṃ jāyate phalam eva vā ||
69.3.d: कप्यादयो व जायन्ते अन्यस्य तुल्यगात्रकाः । वृक्षे ऽन्यवृक्षजं पुष्पं जायते फलम् एव वा ॥
69.3.m: Or if monkeys and the like are born having limbs resembling another [species], / or if on a tree the flower or fruit born of another tree appears,

69.3.s: dvijottamam atharvāṇaṃ tatrecchec chāntim ātmanaḥ | kārayeta mahāśāntiṃ rāṣṭrasya ca purasya ca ||
69.3.d: द्विजोत्तमम् अथर्वाणं तत्रेच्छेच् छान्तिम् आत्मनः । कारयेत महाशान्तिं राष्ट्रस्य च पुरस्य च ॥
69.3.m: there he should seek for himself a propitiatory rite from the best of twice-borns, an Atharvan; / he should cause a great propitiatory rite to be performed for the realm and the city.

69.4.s: upasthite rājyanāśe mahāraurava eva vā | durbhikṣe marake vāpi anāvṛṣṭibhaye 'pi vā ||
69.4.d: उपस्थिते राज्यनाशे महारौरव एव वा । दुर्भिक्षे मरके वापि अनावृष्टिभये ऽपि वा ॥
69.4.m: When the destruction of the kingdom is imminent, or a great tumult, / or in famine, epidemic, or fear of drought,

69.4.s: sarvaṃ rāṣṭre vinaśyeta sasyaṃ śalabhamūṣakaiḥ | akasmān nirjalā vā syād aśoṣā vā mahāsarit ||
69.4.d: सर्वं राष्ट्रे विनश्येत सस्यं शलभमूषकैः । अकस्मान् निर्जला वा स्याद् अशोषा वा महासरित् ॥
69.4.m: or if all the crops in the realm should be destroyed by locusts and mice, / or if a great river that never dries up should suddenly become waterless,

69.4.s: tathānyeṣv apu anukteṣu ghoreṣūpasthiteṣu ca | kuryuḥ śāntim atharvāṇo dvijā hy eteṣu bheṣajam ||
69.4.d: तथान्येष्व् अपु अनुक्तेषु घोरेषूपस्थितेषु च । कुर्युः शान्तिम् अथर्वाणो द्विजा ह्य् एतेषु भेषजम् ॥
69.4.m: and likewise when other terrible [omens] unmentioned here arrive, / Atharvans should perform a propitiatory rite; for the twice-born are a medicine in these [calamities].

69.4.s: labhate rājyayogyo 'pi na rājyaṃ rajanandanaḥ | paṭhan na labhate vidyāṃ dvijaḥ śṛṇvann api śrutam ||
69.4.d: लभते राज्ययोग्यो ऽपि न राज्यं रजनन्दनः । पठन् न लभते विद्यां द्विजः शृण्वन्न् अपि श्रुतम् ॥
69.4.m: When a king's son, though fit for kingship, does not obtain the kingdom; / when a twice-born, though studying, does not obtain learning, or hearing [it], does not retain sacred learning;

69.4.s: ādhitsur api nādhānaṃ kuryād āvāsam eva ca | kanyā pariṇinīṣur vā kāmyeṣv iṣṭapatiṃ na ca ||
69.4.d: आधित्सुर् अपि नाधानं कुर्याद् आवासम् एव च । कन्या परिणिनीषुर् वा काम्येष्व् इष्टपतिं न च ॥
69.4.m: when, though desiring to establish [the sacred fires], he cannot perform the establishment or [settle] a dwelling; / or when a maiden wishing to be wed [cannot find] a desired husband among suitors;

69.5.s: vandhyā vā mṛtavatsā yā durbhagā strīprasū ca yā | sakṛtprasūtā yā nārī garbhaṃ gṛhṇāti naiva ca ||
69.5.d: वन्ध्या वा मृतवत्सा या दुर्भगा स्त्रीप्रसू च या । सकृत्प्रसूता या नारी गर्भं गृह्णाति नैव च ॥
69.5.m: or a woman who is barren, whose children die, who is unfortunate, or who bears only females; / or a woman who, having given birth once, does not conceive again;

69.5.s: sūtikāle 'py atikrānte garbhe sphuraṇavaty api | na sūtiṃ labhate yā tu bahuputrīyate ca yā ||
69.5.d: सूतिकाले ऽप्य् अतिक्रान्ते गर्भे स्फुरणवत्य् अपि । न सूतिं लभते या तु बहुपुत्रीयते च या ॥
69.5.m: or who, even when the time of delivery has passed and the fetus is stirring, / does not obtain delivery; or who longs for many sons;

69.5.s: kṛṣīvalaḥ kṛṣīvalaṃ jayaty āyudhajīvy api | jayāpsur vyavahāre vā saubhāgyaṃ sārvabhautikam ||
69.5.d: कृषीवलः कृषीवलं जयत्य् आयुधजीव्य् अपि । जयाप्सुर् व्यवहारे वा सौभाग्यं सार्वभौतिकम् ॥
69.5.m: when a farmer [wishes to surpass] a farmer, or one who lives by weapons [wishes to] conquer; / or one seeking success in business, or good fortune among all beings—

69.5.s: athāpahantuṃ bhayam evamādikaṃ yadābhilaṣyet phalam uktam eva vā | tadāṅgirasyaṃ varamantrasaṃpadā sphurantam uccaiḥ śaraṇaṃ vrajed dvijam ||
69.5.d: अथापहन्तुं भयम् एवमादिकं यदाभिलष्येत् फलम् उक्तम् एव वा । तदाङ्गिरस्यं वरमन्त्रसंपदा स्फुरन्तम् उच्चैः शरणं व्रजेद् द्विजम् ॥
69.5.m: then, to dispel such fear or when one desires that said fruit, / one should take refuge in the twice-born follower of Aṅgiras, shining brightly through his wealth of excellent mantras.

69.5.s: rātrau dvichāyavṛkṣaṃ vā kusvapnaṃ vāpi riṣṭadam | divā grahān nirīkṣeta bhūmikampaivamādikam ||
69.5.d: रात्रौ द्विछायवृक्षं वा कुस्वप्नं वापि रिष्टदम् । दिवा ग्रहान् निरीक्षेत भूमिकम्पैवमादिकम् ॥
69.5.m: Or [if one sees] a tree with two shadows at night, or a bad dream portending misfortune, / or sees the planets by day, an earthquake, or the like;

69.6.s: jvālādbhutāny atha proktāni yāni ulkādibhedā gaditās tathā ye | svapnādbhutāny api vānyādbhutāni gṛheṣu yāny arthavido vadanti ||
69.6.d: ज्वालाद्भुतान्य् अथ प्रोक्तानि यानि उल्कादिभेदा गदितास् तथा ये । स्वप्नाद्भुतान्य् अपि वान्याद्भुतानि गृहेषु यान्य् अर्थविदो वदन्ति ॥
69.6.m: or the fiery portents that have been mentioned, or the kinds of meteors and the like that have been stated, / or the dream portents, or other portents in houses which those knowing the meaning proclaim—

69.6.s: eteṣu śāntiṃ kurvīta amṛtāṃ vā sadakṣiṇām | raudrīṃ vā vaiśvadevīṃ vā abhayāṃ vāparājitām ||
69.6.d: एतेषु शान्तिं कुर्वीत अमृतां वा सदक्षिणाम् । रौद्रीं वा वैश्वदेवीं वा अभयां वापराजिताम् ॥
69.6.m: in these cases one should perform a propitiatory rite: the Amṛtā accompanied by a sacrificial fee, / or the Raudrī, or the Vaiśvadevī, or the Abhayā, or the Aparājitā,

69.6.s: gobhūhiraṇyavastrānnais tilair vā saphalaiḥ śubhaiḥ | upānacchattrasaṃyuktāṃ gurvābharaṇasaṃyutām ||
69.6.d: गोभूहिरण्यवस्त्रान्नैस् तिलैर् वा सफलैः शुभैः । उपानच्छत्त्रसंयुक्तां गुर्वाभरणसंयुताम् ॥
69.6.m: accompanied by cows, land, gold, garments, food, or sesame, with auspicious fruits, / together with shoes and parasol, and with ornaments for the teacher;

69.6.s: pratipatīyathoktaṃ vā yaḥ kurvīta vidhānvit | etad utpātajaṃ sarvaṃ mahāśāntyā pralīyate ||
69.6.d: प्रतिपतीयथोक्तं वा यः कुर्वीत विधान्वित् । एतद् उत्पातजं सर्वं महाशान्त्या प्रलीयते ॥
69.6.m: or whichever [propitiatory rite] one knowing the ritual performs as prescribed for each counter-measure, / everything arising from omens is dissolved by the great propitiatory rite.

69.6.s: yasya rājño janapade atharvā śāntipāragaḥ | nivasaty api tadrāṣṭraṃ vardhate nirupadravam ||
69.6.d: यस्य राज्ञो जनपदे अथर्वा शान्तिपारगः । निवसत्य् अपि तद्राष्ट्रं वर्धते निरुपद्रवम् ॥
69.6.m: In whosever realm an Atharvan master of propitiatory rites dwells, / that king's realm flourishes free of affliction.

69.7.s: yasya rājño janapade sa nāsti vividhair bhayaiḥ | pīḍyate tasya tad rāṣṭraṃ paṅle gaur iva majjati ||
69.7.d: यस्य राज्ञो जनपदे स नास्ति विविधैर् भयैः । पीड्यते तस्य तद् राष्ट्रं पङ्ले गौर् इव मज्जति ॥
69.7.m: In whosever realm he is not [present], that realm is afflicted / with various terrors and sinks down like a cow in the mire.

69.7.s: tasmād rājā viśeṣeṇa atharvāṇaṃ jitendriyam | dānasaṃmānasatkārair nityaṃ samabhipūjayet ||
69.7.d: तस्माद् राजा विशेषेण अथर्वाणं जितेन्द्रियम् । दानसंमानसत्कारैर् नित्यं समभिपूजयेत् ॥
69.7.m: Therefore a king should constantly and specially worship an Atharvan who has conquered his senses, / with gifts, respect, and hospitality;

69.7.s: nityaṃ ca kārayec chāntiṃ grahaṛkṣāṇi pūjayet | bhūmidohān prakurvīta devatāyataneṣu ca ||
69.7.d: नित्यं च कारयेच् छान्तिं ग्रहऋक्षाणि पूजयेत् । भूमिदोहान् प्रकुर्वीत देवतायतनेषु च ॥
69.7.m: and he should have propitiatory rites performed regularly, worship the planets and lunar mansions, / and carry out milk-libations to the earth and in shrines of the deities;

69.7.s: catuṣpatheṣu goṣṭheṣu tīrtheṣv apsu ca kārayet | gotarpaṇaṃ ca vidhivat sarvadoṣavināśanam ||
69.7.d: चतुष्पथेषु गोष्ठेषु तीर्थेष्व् अप्सु च कारयेत् । गोतर्पणं च विधिवत् सर्वदोषविनाशनम् ॥
69.7.m: and he should have water libations for cows performed at crossroads, in cattle-pens, at sacred bathing places, and in waters / according to rule, destroying all faults.

69.7.s: evaṃ tu khyāpayan rājā sarvakālaṃ jitendriyaḥ | anantaṃ sukham āpnoti kṛtsnāṃ bhuṅkte vasuṃdharām ||
69.7.d: एवं तु ख्यापयन् राजा सर्वकालं जितेन्द्रियः । अनन्तं सुखम् आप्नोति कृत्स्नां भुङ्क्ते वसुंधराम् ॥
69.7.m: Proclaiming this at all times, with his senses subdued, / the king attains endless happiness and enjoys the entire earth.

69.8.s: upasthitaṃ mṛtyum api dvijottamaḥ śamaṃ nayet | adhītyātharvāṅgirasas tādṛśam ādhṛtavrataḥ ||
69.8.d: उपस्थितं मृत्युम् अपि द्विजोत्तमः शमं नयेत् । अधीत्याथर्वाङ्गिरसस् तादृशम् आधृतव्रतः ॥
69.8.m: The best of the twice-born can pacify even imminent death, / having studied the Atharvāṅgiras [texts] of such a kind and having observed his vows.

69.8.s: dyutiṃ prabhāṃ sadā sphuran mantrapavitravān naraḥ | nṛpe dhanini cānyatra śāntyāptvā dakṣiṇāṃ budhaḥ ||
69.8.d: द्युतिं प्रभां सदा स्फुरन् मन्त्रपवित्रवान् नरः । नृपे धनिनि चान्यत्र शान्त्याप्त्वा दक्षिणां बुधः ॥
69.8.m: A wise man who is pure through mantras, constantly radiating splendor and brilliance, / having obtained a sacrificial fee through a propitiatory rite from a king, a rich man, or elsewhere,

69.8.s: sīdan kuṭumbakaḥ poṣaṃ gṛhītvānyat samutsṛjet | triḥ saṃhitāṃ haviṣyādyaṃ japet kṛcchraṃ ca śuddhaye ||
69.8.d: सीदन् कुटुम्बकः पोषं गृहीत्वान्यत् समुत्सृजेत् । त्रिः संहितां हविष्याद्यं जपेत् कृच्छ्रं च शुद्धये ॥
69.8.m: should take [only enough for] the maintenance of his family when in distress, and renounce the rest; / he should recite the Saṃhitā thrice, eat sacrificial food, and perform a Kṛcchra penance for purification.

69.8.s: sāvitrīlakṣam ayutaṃ sahasaram atha cottaram | japtvā daśāṃśako homaḥ kāryo doṣānusārataḥ ||
69.8.d: सावित्रीलक्षम् अयुतं सहसरम् अथ चोत्तरम् । जप्त्वा दशांशको होमः कार्यो दोषानुसारतः ॥
69.8.m: Having recited the Sāvitrī a hundred thousand, ten thousand, or one thousand times followed by [extra recitations], / an oblation of a tenth part should be made according to the fault.

69.8.s: śatīranirmalo yas tu nārcito 'pi dvijottaram | amatsarī nitāntaṃ yaḥ so 'tra śāntiṃ samārabhet ||
69.8.d: शतीरनिर्मलो यस् तु नार्चितो ऽपि द्विजोत्तरम् । अमत्सरी नितान्तं यः सो ऽत्र शान्तिं समारभेत् ॥
69.8.m: He who is pure in body, who is entirely free of envy even toward a superior twice-born / who has not honored him, may undertake a propitiatory rite here.

69.8.s: evaṃvidho 'ṅgirā yatra yāni sādhyāni sādhayet | na nyūnaṃ tatra kiṃcit syād iti tad bhṛgubhāṣitam ||
69.8.d: एवंविधो ऽङ्गिरा यत्र यानि साध्यानि साधयेत् । न न्यूनं तत्र किंचित् स्याद् इति तद् भृगुभाषितम् ॥
69.8.m: Where such a follower of Aṅgiras accomplishes whatever is to be accomplished, / nothing there will fall short; so was it spoken by Bhṛgu.

69.8.s: laghuśāntyudakavidhinā gāyatryā vāpu atharvakaḥ | kuryāt sarvam idaṃ jānann atharvahṛdayaṃ budhaḥ ||
69.8.d: लघुशान्त्युदकविधिना गायत्र्या वापु अथर्वकः । कुर्यात् सर्वम् इदं जानन्न् अथर्वहृदयं बुधः ॥
69.8.m: A wise Atharvan, knowing this Atharva-heart, / may perform all this by the brief rite of propitiatory water, or by the Gāyatrī.

69.9.s: ye na jānanty adhītā api śrutim āṅgirasīṃ dvijāḥ | atharvahṛdayaṃ cāpi na te vedavidaḥ smṛtāḥ ||
69.9.d: ये न जानन्त्य् अधीता अपि श्रुतिम् आङ्गिरसीं द्विजाः । अथर्वहृदयं चापि न ते वेदविदः स्मृताः ॥
69.9.m: Those twice-born who, even though they have studied the sacred revelation of Aṅgiras, / do not know the Atharva-heart, are not considered knowers of the Veda.

69.9.s: atharvahṛdayaṃ vettā atharvā paramaḥ smṛtaḥ | nātharvaṇe 'py idaṃ deyaṃ guror vidveṣayāyini ||
69.9.d: अथर्वहृदयं वेत्ता अथर्वा परमः स्मृतः । नाथर्वणे ऽप्य् इदं देयं गुरोर् विद्वेषयायिनि ॥
69.9.m: The knower of the Atharva-heart is declared to be the highest Atharvan; / this must not be given even to an Atharvan who harbors hostility toward his teacher.

69.9.s: anyaśākhyaṃ dvijo mohāt pāṭhayan pravilīyate | atharvahṛdayaṃ buddhvā yaḥ paṭhed bhaktipūrvakam ||
69.9.d: अन्यशाख्यं द्विजो मोहात् पाठयन् प्रविलीयते । अथर्वहृदयं बुद्ध्वा यः पठेद् भक्तिपूर्वकम् ॥
69.9.m: A twice-born who, out of delusion, teaches it to one belonging to another Vedic branch perishes. / He who, having understood the Atharva-heart, recites it with devotion,

69.9.s: atharvā nādbhutaṃ tasya śāntir eva sadā bhavet | śāntir eva sadā bhavet ||
69.9.d: अथर्वा नाद्भुतं तस्य शान्तिर् एव सदा भवेत् । शान्तिर् एव सदा भवेत् ॥
69.9.m: being an Atharvan, no portent befalls him; there shall always be pacification for him; / there shall always be pacification for him.

70.1.s: oṃ saṃpūjya vidhivat prājñaṃ vidvāṃso munayaḥ purā | apṛcchan bhṛgum avyagraṃ sarvasattvahite ratam ||
70.1.d: ओं संपूज्य विधिवत् प्राज्ञं विद्वांसो मुनयः पुरा । अपृच्छन् भृगुम् अव्यग्रं सर्वसत्त्वहिते रतम् ॥
70.1.m: Om. Having duly honored the wise sage Bhṛgu, who was undistracted and devoted to the welfare of all beings, / the learned sages formerly asked him:

70.1.s: lokatrayaniviṣṭānām utpātānām anekadhā | bhinnānāṃ śamanaṃ noktaṃ vada tv asaṃśayaṃ mune ||
70.1.d: लोकत्रयनिविष्टानाम् उत्पातानाम् अनेकधा । भिन्नानां शमनं नोक्तं वद त्व् असंशयं मुने ॥
