70.1.m: "The pacification of the manifold and distinct omens / occurring in the three worlds has not been declared; speak [of it], O sage, without doubt."

70.1.s: pratyuvāca bhṛgur viprān śṛṇutāhitamānasaḥ | utpātaśamanatritvaṃ kathyamānam asaṃśayam ||
70.1.d: प्रत्युवाच भृगुर् विप्रान् शृणुताहितमानसः । उत्पातशमनत्रित्वं कथ्यमानम् असंशयम् ॥
70.1.m: Bhṛgu replied to the Brahmins: "Listen with attentive minds / to the threefold pacification of omens being declared without doubt.

70.1.s: tatra viprān pravakṣyāmi duriṣṭaśamanakṣamān | atharvāṅgiraso vede vidhijñān sarvakarmaṇām ||
70.1.d: तत्र विप्रान् प्रवक्ष्यामि दुरिष्टशमनक्षमान् । अथर्वाङ्गिरसो वेदे विधिज्ञान् सर्वकर्मणाम् ॥
70.1.m: Among them, I shall declare the Brahmins capable of pacifying misfortune: / Atharvāṅgiras [Brahmins] versed in the Veda and knowing the rules for all rites,
endowed with non-violence, truth, generosity, purity, and faith, / conforming to sacred revelation, tradition, and good conduct, endowed with good lineage, character, and mature age.

70.1.s: teṣām ekaḥ pradhānatve yaḥ śānto dvijasattamaḥ | bhṛgvaṅgirovid atyarthaṃ śuciḥ syāt sādhusaṃmataḥ ||
70.1.d: तेषाम् एकः प्रधानत्वे यः शान्तो द्विजसत्तमः । भृग्वङ्गिरोविद् अत्यर्थं शुचिः स्यात् साधुसंमतः ॥
70.1.m: Among them, the one who is supreme, a calm and excellent twice-born, / profoundly knowing the Bhṛgus and Aṅgirases, pure, and approved by the virtuous,

70.1.s: brahmāṇaṃ taṃ nṛpaḥ kuryād dhotāraṃ sarvavedinam | evam ukte bhṛguṃ viprāḥ procur vigatakalmaṣam ||
70.1.d: ब्रह्माणं तं नृपः कुर्याद् धोतारं सर्ववेदिनम् । एवम् उक्ते भृगुं विप्राः प्रोचुर् विगतकल्मषम् ॥
70.1.m: the king should appoint him as the Brahman priest, [or] as the Hotṛ knowing all Vedas." / When this was spoken, the Brahmins said to Bhṛgu, who was free of impurity:

70.1.s: hotāro bhūmibhartṝṇāṃ mahāśānteḥ prakīrtitāḥ | nanu kṣīṇe vidvan svadharmapracyute 'pi vā ||
70.1.d: होतारो भूमिभर्तॄणां महाशान्तेः प्रकीर्तिताः । ननु क्षीणे विद्वन् स्वधर्मप्रच्युते ऽपि वा ॥
70.1.m: "The Hotṛs of kings for the great propitiatory rite have been proclaimed. / But surely, O learned one, when he is exhausted or has fallen from his own duty,

70.1.s: tatra śāntau prayuktāyāṃ kasya śāntiphalaṃ bhavet | nṛpo 'py adhārmikaḥ kuryād brahmaṇas tarpaṇaṃ purā ||
70.1.d: तत्र शान्तौ प्रयुक्तायां कस्य शान्तिफलं भवेत् । नृपो ऽप्य् अधार्मिकः कुर्याद् ब्रह्मणस् तर्पणं पुरा ॥
70.1.m: if the propitiatory rite is employed there, whose will the fruit of the propitiatory rite be? / Even an unrighteous king should first make an offering to the Brahman priest;

70.1.s: tataḥ kṛtā mahāśāntī rājānaṃ pāti sarvataḥ | sa vṛtaḥ pāvanaṃ gacched dvijānāṃ pāvanāya vai ||
70.1.d: ततः कृता महाशान्ती राजानं पाति सर्वतः । स वृतः पावनं गच्छेद् द्विजानां पावनाय वै ॥
70.1.m: then the performed great propitiatory rite protects the king on every side. / Having been chosen, he should undergo purification for the sanctification of the twice-born:
a vow of twelve days there, subsisting on milk, roots, and fruits.

70.2.s: trīṇi tryahāṇi kurvīta payomūlaphalaiḥ śubhaiḥ | anaśnaṃś ca tryahaṃ dhīraḥ sa puraścaraṇo bhavet ||
70.2.d: त्रीणि त्र्यहाणि कुर्वीत पयोमूलफलैः शुभैः । अनश्नंश् च त्र्यहं धीरः स पुरश्चरणो भवेत् ॥
70.2.m: He should pass three three-day periods on auspicious milk, roots, and fruits, / and for three days the steadfast one should fast; he will then have completed his preparatory rite."

70.2.s: tathaikonaṃ śataṃ nṝṇāṃ śuśrūṣūṇām akalmaṣam | anuktavac ca tryahaṃ tat karmaṇaḥ karaṇe kṣamam ||
70.2.d: तथैकोनं शतं नॄणां शुश्रूषूणाम् अकल्मषम् । अनुक्तवच् च त्र्यहं तत् कर्मणः करणे क्षमम् ॥
70.2.m: Likewise, ninety-nine attendant men, free from taint, / and for three days silent, are capable of performing the rite.

70.2.s: kṛcchraṃ cāpi hitaṃ kṛtvā kuryuḥ karma samāhitāḥ | śuddhātmāno japair homair vaidikair vītamatsarāḥ ||
70.2.d: कृच्छ्रं चापि हितं कृत्वा कुर्युः कर्म समाहिताः । शुद्धात्मानो जपैर् होमैर् वैदिकैर् वीतमत्सराः ॥
70.2.m: Having also observed a wholesome kṛcchra penance, composed, / pure in self, free from malice, they should perform the rite with Vedic recitations and oblations.

70.2.s: tataḥ paraṃ purodhaḥsu divyaṃ tatram avāpnuyāt | grahātithyaṃ ca saṃrabhya diśāṃ yāgaṃ ca sarvataḥ ||
70.2.d: ततः परं पुरोधःसु दिव्यं तत्रम् अवाप्नुयात् । ग्रहातिथ्यं च संरभ्य दिशां यागं च सर्वतः ॥
70.2.m: Thereafter, among royal priests one should obtain the celestial [rite]; / and having undertaken hospitality to the planets, and worship of the cardinal directions everywhere,

70.2.s: nakṣatreṣu ca sarveṣu yāgaṃ kṛtvā vidhānataḥ | tato 'mṛtamahāśāntyā sthāpayet padmasaṃbhavam ||
70.2.d: नक्षत्रेषु च सर्वेषु यागं कृत्वा विधानतः । ततो ऽमृतमहाशान्त्या स्थापयेत् पद्मसंभवम् ॥
70.2.m: and having performed worship for all the lunar mansions according to rule, / one should then install the lotus-born [Brahmā] by means of the Amṛtamahāśānti.

70.3.s: sāvitryā lakṣahomaṃ tu bhaume tiṣṭhed viśāradāḥ | kuryur deyaṃ ca dānānāṃ viprebhyo yasya yat priyam ||
70.3.d: सावित्र्या लक्षहोमं तु भौमे तिष्ठेद् विशारदाः । कुर्युर् देयं च दानानां विप्रेभ्यो यस्य यत् प्रियम् ॥
70.3.m: When [a portent is] terrestrial, skilled [priests] should engage in a hundred-thousand oblations with the Sāvitrī verse; / and of gifts, that which is dear to whichever Brahmin should be given to them.

70.3.s: gobhūmikāñcanāśvānāṃ ratnānāṃ dhānyavāsasām | rathānāṃ vāraṇānāṃ ca dānaṃ kāmam ataḥ param ||
70.3.d: गोभूमिकाञ्चनाश्वानां रत्नानां धान्यवाससाम् । रथानां वारणानां च दानं कामम् अतः परम् ॥
70.3.m: Gifts of cattle, land, gold, and horses, of gems, grain, and garments, / of chariots and of elephants may be given at will beyond this.

70.3.s: tuṣyeyur yena vā viprāḥ saṃbhavo yasya yasya hi | tat tat sarvam upādeyam eṣa dānavidhiḥ smṛtaḥ ||
70.3.d: तुष्येयुर् येन वा विप्राः संभवो यस्य यस्य हि । तत् तत् सर्वम् उपादेयम् एष दानविधिः स्मृतः ॥
70.3.m: Or by whatever the Brahmins might be pleased, whatever each possesses, / all that should be accepted; this is remembered as the rule of gifts.

70.3.s: dadyāc ca gurave grāmaṃ dhenuṃ vāsoyugaṃ tathā | alaṃkāraiś ca saṃpūjya prīṇayet prītamānasaḥ ||
70.3.d: दद्याच् च गुरवे ग्रामं धेनुं वासोयुगं तथा । अलंकारैश् च संपूज्य प्रीणयेत् प्रीतमानसः ॥
70.3.m: And he should give to the guru a village, a cow, and a pair of garments; / and having honoured him with ornaments, pleased in mind, he should gratify him.

70.3.s: anena vidhinā bhaumam adbhutaṃ śamayed guruḥ | eṣa eva vidhir jñeyo viyatye 'py adbhutāśraye ||
70.3.d: अनेन विधिना भौमम् अद्भुतं शमयेद् गुरुः । एष एव विधिर् ज्ञेयो वियत्ये ऽप्य् अद्भुताश्रये ॥
70.3.m: By this rule the guru should appease a terrestrial portent. / This very rule should be known also in the case of a portent belonging to the atmosphere.

70.4.s: viśeṣo 'yaṃ tu sāvitryā daśalakṣāṃs tu homayet | homasamāhitamanāḥ kuryāc ca ghṛtakambalam ||
70.4.d: विशेषो ऽयं तु सावित्र्या दशलक्षांस् तु होमयेत् । होमसमाहितमनाः कुर्याच् च घृतकम्बलम् ॥
70.4.m: The distinction, however, is this: one should offer a million oblations with the Sāvitrī verse; / with mind concentrated on the oblations, he should also make the ghee-blanket.

70.4.s: dhenūnāṃ dvādaśaṃ deyaṃ śataniṣkasamanvitam | gurave dīyamānaṃ tac chamayaty ambarādbhutam ||
70.4.d: धेनूनां द्वादशं देयं शतनिष्कसमन्वितम् । गुरवे दीयमानं तच् छमयत्य् अम्बराद्भुतम् ॥
70.4.m: Twelve cows, accompanied by a hundred niṣkas, are to be given; / that being given to the guru appeases an atmospheric portent.

70.4.s: divyādbhuteṣu kartavyaḥ koṭihomasamanvitaiḥ | gosahasraṃ ca dātavyaṃ gurave dakṣiṇāvidhiḥ ||
70.4.d: दिव्याद्भुतेषु कर्तव्यः कोटिहोमसमन्वितैः । गोसहस्रं च दातव्यं गुरवे दक्षिणाविधिः ॥
70.4.m: For celestial portents, [the rite] is to be performed by those endowed with ten million oblations; / and a thousand cows are to be given to the guru: this is the rule of the sacrificial fee.

70.4.s: eṣa prokto vidhiḥ samyag divyāniṣṭavipatkare | subhikṣakṣemasaṃpattyā prajānāṃ puṣṭivardhanaḥ ||
70.4.d: एष प्रोक्तो विधिः सम्यग् दिव्यानिष्टविपत्करे । सुभिक्षक्षेमसंपत्त्या प्रजानां पुष्टिवर्धनः ॥
70.4.m: This rule has been properly declared for the celestial, misfortune-bringing calamity, / increasing the nourishment of the subjects through the attainment of abundance of food and security.

70.4.s: koṭihomeṣu sarveṣu dravyabhedāśrayaṃ phalam | śāntipuṣṭyabhicārārthaṃ tan me nigadataḥ śṛṇu ||
70.4.d: कोटिहोमेषु सर्वेषु द्रव्यभेदाश्रयं फलम् । शान्तिपुष्ट्यभिचारार्थं तन् मे निगदतः शृणु ॥
70.4.m: In all ten-million oblations, the fruit depends on the variety of materials / for the sake of pacification, prosperity, or sorcery; hear that as I declare it.

70.4.s: saumyavṛkṣāśrayāḥ kāryāḥ samidhaḥ śāntim icchatā | arkakāśmaryanimbānāṃ samidbhiḥ śatruśātanam ||
70.4.d: सौम्यवृक्षाश्रयाः कार्याः समिधः शान्तिम् इच्छता । अर्ककाश्मर्यनिम्बानां समिद्भिः शत्रुशातनम् ॥
70.4.m: Firewood sticks belonging to gentle trees must be prepared by one desiring pacification. / With firewood sticks of arka, kāśmarya, and neem, there is destruction of enemies.

70.4.s: durnāmakaṇṭakambūnāṃ samidbhiś ca viśeṣataḥ | bhagnasphuṭitavṛkṣāṇāṃ phalaṃ śatrunibarhaṇam ||
70.4.d: दुर्नामकण्टकम्बूनां समिद्भिश् च विशेषतः । भग्नस्फुटितवृक्षाणां फलं शत्रुनिबर्हणम् ॥
70.4.m: And particularly with firewood sticks of thorny shrubs and durnāman plants, / [and] of broken and split trees, the fruit is the destruction of enemies.

70.4.s: bilvapadmotpalānāṃ tu śucideśaprarohiṇām | sarvadā sarvakāmāṃs tu homaiḥ prāpnoti mānavaḥ ||
70.4.d: बिल्वपद्मोत्पलानां तु शुचिदेशप्ररोहिणाम् । सर्वदा सर्वकामांस् तु होमैः प्राप्नोति मानवः ॥
70.4.m: With bilva, lotus, and blue water lily growing in pure places, / a man attains all desires at all times through oblations.

70.4.s: tilavrīhiyavādīnāṃ dadhno madhughṛtasya ca | payogodhūmaśālīnāṃ hotā śāntiṃ samārabhet ||
70.4.d: तिलव्रीहियवादीनां दध्नो मधुघृतस्य च । पयोगोधूमशालीनां होता शान्तिं समारभेत् ॥
70.4.m: With sesame, unhusked rice, barley, and the like, with curd, honey, and ghee, / with milk, wheat, and rice, the hotṛ priest should undertake the propitiatory rite.

70.4.s: sarveṣāṃ haviṣāṃ caiva ghṛtaṃ śāntikaraṃ smṛtam | sarvadravye ghṛtaṃ tasmād dhome prakṣepam arhati ||
70.4.d: सर्वेषां हविषां चैव घृतं शान्तिकरं स्मृतम् । सर्वद्रव्ये घृतं तस्माद् धोमे प्रक्षेपम् अर्हति ॥
70.4.m: And of all oblations, ghee is remembered as bringing peace; / therefore, ghee is fit to be cast into the fire in every substance during oblation.

70.5.s: yajñopavītinā kāryaṃ śāntikarma vipaścitā | upavītaṃ tu pitryeṣu sarveṣv eva samārabhet ||
70.5.d: यज्ञोपवीतिना कार्यं शान्तिकर्म विपश्चिता । उपवीतं तु पित्र्येषु सर्वेष्व् एव समारभेत् ॥
70.5.m: The wise man wearing the sacred thread over the left shoulder must perform the propitiatory rite; / he should undertake everything with the thread over the left shoulder, but in ancestral rites [it is worn over the right].

70.5.s: madhvājyadadhidugdheṣu bhakṣyamāṇe vilepane | yantravāhanaśastreṣu bhavaneṣv āyudheṣu ca ||
70.5.d: मध्वाज्यदधिदुग्धेषु भक्ष्यमाणे विलेपने । यन्त्रवाहनशस्त्रेषु भवनेष्व् आयुधेषु च ॥
70.5.m: In honey, clarified butter, curd, and milk, in food being eaten, in anointment, / in mechanical devices, conveyances, and weapons, in houses and in arms,

70.5.s: darpaṇe bhaktapātre ca maṇimuktāphaleṣu ca | bhūṣaṇeṣu tathānyeṣu śayyāyām āsaneṣu ca ||
70.5.d: दर्पणे भक्तपात्रे च मणिमुक्ताफलेषु च । भूषणेषु तथान्येषु शय्यायाम् आसनेषु च ॥
70.5.m: in a mirror, in an eating vessel, in gems and pearls, / in ornaments, likewise in others, on a bed, and on seats,

70.5.s: kākolūkakapotānāṃ madhor vā darśanaṃ bhavet | anyeṣāṃ cāpraśastānām āgamo mṛgapakṣiṇām ||
70.5.d: काकोलूककपोतानां मधोर् वा दर्शनं भवेत् । अन्येषां चाप्रशस्तानाम् आगमो मृगपक्षिणाम् ॥
70.5.m: if there should be the sighting of crows, owls, or pigeons, or of honey, / or the arrival of other unpraised beasts and birds,

70.5.s: aśvetānāṃ ca puṣpāṇāṃ sarīsṛpagaṇasya ca | vasālohitamāṃsānām asthimajjāśiroruhām ||
70.5.d: अश्वेतानां च पुष्पाणां सरीसृपगणस्य च । वसालोहितमांसानाम् अस्थिमज्जाशिरोरुहाम् ॥
70.5.m: and of non-white flowers, and of a horde of serpents, / of fat, blood, and flesh, of bones, marrow, and hair,
